audit_report.headline: Here is where The Beauty Barn® is leaving booked appointments on the table

findings.title: No HTTPS means browsers are flagging your site as not secure
findings.detail: The scan confirmed the site runs on HTTP, not HTTPS, which triggers a 'Not Secure' warning in Chrome and Safari before a visitor even reads a single word. For a medical spa where people are booking injectable treatments and skin procedures, that warning kills trust at the first click and sends appointment-ready visitors straight to a competitor.

findings.title: Missing meta description is costing you clicks from people already searching for med spas in Canton
findings.detail: The scan returned no meta description, which means Google is auto-generating a random snippet from your page text for every search result listing. A medical spa ranked well enough to win Best GA Med Spa 2024 and 2025 is handing Google the pen to write its own pitch, and the result is almost always a generic, unconvincing blurb that suppresses click-through rates by an estimated 5 to 10 percent.

findings.title: Mobile PageSpeed data is unavailable, which is itself a red flag
findings.detail: The PageSpeed scan could not return a score, which typically means the page either timed out or failed to load cleanly during automated testing. Given that the majority of local med spa searches happen on mobile, any load friction translates directly into visitors bouncing before the booking widget even renders.

findings.title: Online booking and a lead form exist but HTTPS is absent, creating a trust gap at the exact moment someone enters personal information
findings.detail: The site has both online booking and a lead form, which is good, but without HTTPS, any data entered through those forms travels unencrypted. Beyond the real security risk, savvy clients who notice the browser warning will abandon the form mid-fill, meaning the booking infrastructure you already paid to build is leaking conversions daily.

findings.title: Three social channels are linked but YouTube is an underleveraged asset for a med spa with a 5-star reputation
findings.detail: Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube are all present, but a YouTube channel for a medical spa sitting on 820 five-star reviews is a significant untapped engine. Before-and-after procedure walkthroughs and provider Q&A videos rank in both YouTube and Google search, and the absence of any visible YouTube content strategy means The Beauty Barn is not converting its strong reputation into the video proof that turns researchers into booked clients.

audit_report.summary: The Beauty Barn has a strong local reputation and the right booking infrastructure in place, but a non-secure site and missing meta description are eroding trust and click-through before that infrastructure ever gets used. Fixing the HTTPS issue and meta description alone removes the two biggest friction points between a Canton-area search and a confirmed appointment.
audit_report.estimate: Resolving HTTPS, adding a targeted meta description, and activating a basic YouTube content strategy could conservatively recover 8 to 15 additional booked appointments per month based on typical med spa conversion rates at this review volume.

audit_report.headline: Where Woodmont Dental is quietly losing new patients it already earned the right to win
audit_report.overallVerdict: Woodmont Dental has an exceptional reputation on Google but a critical gap in how AI assistants and search engines reach the site, meaning the trust they have built with 433 five-star reviews is not converting into the full patient volume it should.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: Google's own rendering engine gave the site a 93/100 performance score with a 2.3s Largest Contentful Paint and a perfect 0 CLS, which is genuinely strong. However, the site is not served over HTTPS, a hard failure that modern browsers flag as 'Not Secure' and that Google uses as a ranking signal, and the site's hosting firewall blocked our scanner entirely, which is worth investigating since crawlers including search engine bots can hit the same wall.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: A page title and meta description are confirmed present by Google's rendered result, which is a meaningful baseline. Beyond those two signals, the site's hosting firewall blocked all further crawling, so schema markup, H1 structure, internal linking, and content depth could not be verified on this run and should be audited directly.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: Because the site's server refused our scanner, we were unable to verify whether a click-to-call number, booking widget, lead form, or clear call to action are present anywhere on the site. That gap in measurement is itself a signal worth acting on, since any barrier that stops automated crawlers can also create friction for real visitors and for the tracking tools practices rely on to measure where new patients come from.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: A 4.9-star rating across 433 reviews is well above the Canton, GA dentist average and represents a serious competitive moat. Business hours and a website link are confirmed on the profile, and the phone number is listed. The photo count of 6 is meaningfully below the 20-plus photos that top-ranked local dental practices typically maintain, and the most recent review Google shows is 73 days old, which is worth monitoring since Google's local algorithm weighs recent activity heavily.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Analytics 4 is confirmed installed, which provides a workable data foundation. Whether a Meta pixel or Google Ads conversion tag is present could not be verified on this run, meaning the practice may be running or planning paid campaigns without the conversion infrastructure needed to measure cost-per-new-patient or to build retargeting audiences from site visitors.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: No social profiles were detected linking from the site, so it is unclear whether Woodmont Dental maintains active profiles on Facebook, Instagram, or any other platform, and any profiles that do exist are not being connected to the site in a way our scanner could confirm. For a dental practice, short-form video content on Instagram Reels or Facebook showing procedures, before-and-after results, and team culture is one of the highest-ROI content formats for attracting new local patients. Profile optimization basics including a consistent handle, complete bio, direct booking link, and regular posting cadence represent a straightforward opportunity that most competing practices in Canton are also underusing.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: When AI models were probed for knowledge of Woodmont Dental in Canton, GA, the result was unambiguous: the business is not recognized and would not be recommended. This matters because a growing share of prospective patients now open ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google's AI Overviews and ask 'who is the best dentist near Canton, GA' instead of scrolling a map. The combination of a firewall that may block AI crawlers, unverified structured data and entity markup, and zero confirmed AI-readable signals means Woodmont Dental is currently invisible in that channel entirely, while the window to establish early presence before competitors do is still open.

findings.title: The site is not on HTTPS, and browsers are telling patients so
findings.detail: Serving a dental website without HTTPS causes Chrome and Safari to display a 'Not Secure' warning in the address bar. For a healthcare provider where trust is the primary purchase driver, that warning is a direct conversion killer: studies consistently show that a meaningful portion of visitors abandon sites flagged as insecure before they ever read a word of content.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know this practice exists
findings.detail: A live probe confirmed that AI models have no verified knowledge of Woodmont Dental and would not surface it in response to a query for a Canton dentist. With AI-driven search growing faster than any other discovery channel in healthcare, a practice that does not appear in AI results is functionally invisible to an expanding segment of new-patient searches. The gap is closeable now, but it requires deliberate structured data, entity authority, and content investment before competitors claim that ground.

findings.title: A hosting firewall is blocking crawlers, including potentially Google
findings.detail: Our scanner was refused access to the site at the server level, which is the same response pattern that some search engine crawlers and AI training bots receive when firewall rules are misconfigured. If Googlebot is being intermittently blocked, pages may not be indexed or may be cached with stale content, quietly suppressing rankings for every service the practice offers. This is worth verifying in Google Search Console immediately.

findings.title: Six photos on the Google Business Profile is a thin portfolio for a top-ranked practice
findings.detail: The profile has only 6 photos confirmed. Google's own data shows that Business Profiles with more than 100 photos receive substantially more direction requests and website clicks than those with fewer than 10. For a practice trying to grow its patient base, the profile photo library is one of the fastest and most direct levers for increasing the click-through rate from the local map pack, where Woodmont Dental's star rating already earns it strong placement.

findings.title: Review recency is a local ranking factor that needs active management
findings.detail: The most recent review Google shows is 73 days old. While Google returns reviews by relevance rather than date and newer reviews may exist, Google's local algorithm treats a steady cadence of fresh reviews as a signal of an active, trusted business. A 433-review practice without a systematic post-appointment review request process is leaving a meaningful ranking and conversion advantage on the table each month.

findings.title: No confirmed paid media conversion infrastructure
findings.detail: Whether a Meta pixel or Google Ads conversion tag is installed could not be confirmed on this run. If the practice ever runs Google Search ads for terms like 'dentist Canton GA' or 'teeth whitening near me' without proper conversion tracking, every dollar spent on clicks produces no attribution data, no cost-per-patient figure, and no retargeting audience. That makes it impossible to optimize campaigns or justify ad spend with real numbers.

findings.title: Social media presence is not connected to the website and may be underbuilt
findings.detail: No social profiles were detected linking from the site. For a dental practice with a 4.9-star reputation, there is an untapped content asset sitting idle: patient testimonials, procedure education, and team culture content on Instagram and Facebook reach local audiences who are not yet actively searching but who will remember a familiar face when they need a dentist. The absence of a visible, optimized social presence also removes a key trust signal for patients who check social channels before booking.

quickWins: Enable HTTPS on the site's hosting account or through the DNS provider, which typically takes under an hour and immediately removes the browser 'Not Secure' warning
Audit the hosting firewall whitelist and confirm that Googlebot and major AI crawler user agents are not being blocked, then verify crawl status in Google Search Console

Upload at least 20 additional photos to the Google Business Profile, including operatory shots, the exterior, the team, and procedure-specific images to close the gap with higher-ranked local competitors
Implement a post-appointment text or email review request sequence to ensure a consistent flow of fresh Google reviews, which protects both the star rating and the local pack ranking
audit_report.summary: Woodmont Dental has the reputation of a market leader and the digital infrastructure of a practice that has not yet invested in turning that reputation into a systematic new-patient engine. The HTTPS failure, the AI invisibility, and the crawler-blocking firewall are each individually costing new patient inquiries every week, and they compound each other. Open Heart Media's audit process goes several layers deeper than what a firewall allowed us to see here, and a single discovery call is enough to map out exactly which gaps are costing the most and which are fastest to close.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the HTTPS issue, AI visibility gap, and GBP photo and review gaps for a practice of this rating and size in a growing market like Canton, GA is a realistic path to 15 to 30 additional new patient inquiries per month, at average dental patient lifetime values that make even a fraction of that return significant.

audit_report.headline: Swords and Phelps Dentistry has a strong reputation it is quietly failing to convert into new patients online
audit_report.overallVerdict: A 4.8-star practice with 251 reviews and a functional website is leaving a measurable number of new patient inquiries on the table because of a slow mobile experience, missing tracking infrastructure, near-zero AI search presence, and an underpowered Google Business Profile.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site is secure, mobile-responsive, and layout-stable (CLS of 0), which are solid foundations, but a mobile PageSpeed score of 68 and a Largest Contentful Paint of 7.0 seconds are well outside the 2.5-second threshold Google considers acceptable. On mobile, where most local dental searches happen, a 7-second load means a meaningful share of prospective patients bounce before they ever see the booking button.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The site has a proper title tag, a single clean H1, a canonical tag, and a substantive 3,740-word content footprint, all of which are genuine strengths. However, the meta description is missing site-wide and local business schema markup is absent, which means Google is auto-generating the search snippet (often poorly) and cannot confidently surface structured details like address, hours, or service categories in rich results.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: The site passes the core conversion checklist: a clickable phone number, a lead capture form, online booking, and a clear call to action are all present. The gaps are live chat (absent) and email or newsletter capture (absent), which means visitors who are not yet ready to book have no low-friction next step and the practice has no owned channel to nurture them back.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: A 4.8 rating across 251 reviews is genuinely strong for a dentist in Canton and well above the typical 4.5 with 80 to 150 reviews that most local competitors show. The profile has hours and a website link, which are table stakes. The critical weakness is photo count: only 4 photos on the profile, where high-performing dental practices typically maintain 50 or more, and studies consistently show that profiles with more photos receive significantly more direction requests and calls. Whether the business description is filled in was not verifiable on this run and should be checked directly in the profile dashboard.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: No analytics platform, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads conversion tag were detected anywhere on the site. This means the practice has no way to know how many people visit, which pages drive bookings, where traffic comes from, or whether any ad spend would be attributable to actual patient appointments. Every marketing decision is currently being made without data.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: Facebook and Instagram are linked from the site and video content is present, which is a real asset for a dental practice where procedure explainers and patient comfort content perform well. However, the practice has no YouTube presence and no TikTok presence, two platforms where dental content routinely reaches new-patient audiences who are not yet actively searching. The opportunity specific to this practice is to translate its existing video assets and strong review sentiment into consistent short-form content, with optimized profile bios, unified branding across handles, and a clear link-in-bio that routes directly to the booking page.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers are allowed, which is the right baseline, and the site has enough content depth for an AI to summarize the practice. But structured data is missing, sameAs entity links connecting the website to the Google Business Profile, Facebook, and Instagram do not exist, and when AI models are asked about dentists in Canton, GA, Swords and Phelps Dentistry is not recognized by name and would not be recommended. This is the single biggest emerging visibility gap in the audit: a growing share of patients now ask ChatGPT or Perplexity which dentist to call before they ever run a Google search, and if the AI has never been given the structured signals to know this practice exists, every one of those queries goes to a competitor.

findings.title: No tracking means no measurable marketing and no ability to run ads profitably
findings.detail: With zero analytics, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads tag in place, the practice cannot attribute a single new patient to any online source. This is not just a reporting problem: it makes it impossible to run retargeting campaigns against the people who visited the booking page but did not complete a form, a segment that typically converts at two to four times the rate of cold traffic. Every dollar of future ad spend will produce unattributable results until tracking is installed.

findings.title: A 7-second mobile load time is costing new patient inquiries every day
findings.detail: The 7.0-second Largest Contentful Paint on mobile exceeds Google's acceptable threshold by nearly three times. Google's own data shows that as page load time goes from 1 second to 7 seconds, the probability of a mobile visitor bouncing increases by 113 percent. For a practice trying to grow its patient base, a slow mobile site is effectively a leaking bucket: paid or organic traffic arrives, and a measurable portion of it leaves before the phone number or booking form ever loads.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know this practice exists, and that gap is widening monthly
findings.detail: A live probe confirmed that AI models have no specific training data about Swords and Phelps Dentistry and would not recommend it when a user asks for a Canton dentist. The contributing technical causes are identifiable: no structured data schema, no sameAs entity links tying the website to its social and map profiles, and no FAQ schema for AI to quote. As AI-assisted search becomes a primary discovery channel for healthcare providers, being absent from it is equivalent to not appearing in the Yellow Pages in 2005.

findings.title: Four photos on a Google Business Profile is a significant competitive disadvantage
findings.detail: Google's own data shows that businesses with more than 100 photos receive 520 percent more calls and 2,717 percent more direction requests than the average listing. At 4 photos, the Swords and Phelps profile looks sparse next to dental competitors who invest in the profile, and it likely contributes to lower click-through rates from the map pack even when the practice ranks well. The practice's 4.8-star reputation earns the click; the profile's thin visual presence then loses it.

findings.title: The missing meta description lets Google write its own search snippet, usually poorly
findings.detail: With no meta description present across the site, Google is pulling arbitrary text from each page to build the snippet shown in search results. That auto-generated text rarely leads with a patient benefit, a differentiator, or a call to action, which directly reduces the click-through rate from organic search. A well-written meta description for a dental practice in Canton, GA functions as a free ad impression in every search result, and right now that impression is being wasted.

findings.title: Local business schema is missing, which limits eligibility for rich search results
findings.detail: Without local business schema markup, Google cannot reliably extract the practice's name, address, phone number, hours, and service categories from the site itself and display them in rich result formats. Schema is also one of the primary structured signals that AI models use to identify and categorize a local business. Its absence compounds both the SEO gap and the AIO gap simultaneously.

findings.title: No email capture means the practice owns no ongoing channel to its web visitors
findings.detail: Dental patients rarely book on their first visit to a practice website, particularly for elective or cosmetic services. Without an email capture mechanism, every visitor who leaves without booking is gone permanently, with no way for the practice to follow up, share a new patient offer, or stay top of mind until they are ready. An owned email list is one of the lowest-cost, highest-return patient nurture tools available to a local dental practice.

quickWins: Add a unique, keyword-rich meta description to every page, starting with the homepage, to immediately improve click-through rates from Google search results.

Upload at least 50 high-quality photos to the Google Business Profile, including the reception area, operatories, staff, and before-and-after cases, to close the most visible gap on the local listing.
Install Google Analytics 4 and a Meta pixel on the site before any other marketing activity so that every future visit, form submission, and booking is measurable.

Add local business schema markup and sameAs entity links connecting the website to the Google Business Profile, Facebook, and Instagram to begin building AI search recognition and improve local rich result eligibility.
audit_report.summary: Swords and Phelps Dentistry has built a genuinely strong reputation, which is the hardest part of local growth, but the infrastructure that turns that reputation into a steady flow of new patients has real, specific gaps that are costing bookings right now. Open Heart Media built this audit before any conversation because the gaps were visible from the outside and worth documenting honestly. The next step is a short discovery call to prioritize which of these issues to close first based on the practice's current patient volume, budget, and growth targets.

audit_report.headline: Where Russell Family Dentistry is quietly losing new patients before they ever pick up the phone
audit_report.overallVerdict: Russell Family Dentistry has a genuinely strong local reputation and solid SEO fundamentals, but a slow-loading site, missing conversion infrastructure, zero ad tracking, and complete invisibility to AI-powered search are creating a steady, preventable leak of new patient opportunities.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site earns a mobile PageSpeed score of 59/100, which is borderline, but the Largest Contentful Paint of 10.5 seconds is the real problem: Google's threshold for a good user experience is 2.5 seconds, meaning the main content takes more than four times longer to appear than it should on a mobile device. HTTPS is active, the layout is stable during load (CLS of 0.008), and the site is mobile-responsive, so the foundation is sound, but the LCP issue alone is enough to push Google to demote the site in mobile search rankings and cause impatient visitors to leave before the page finishes rendering.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The on-page SEO fundamentals are largely in place: the page title is correctly sized at 33 characters, a meta description is present at 158 characters, there is a single clean H1, local business schema markup is implemented, a canonical tag is set, and the site carries 2522 words of content. The one technical flag worth noting is that the site title reads 'Russell Smiles' rather than 'Russell Family Dentistry,' which creates a brand-name mismatch that could confuse both search engines and prospective patients who search for the practice by its actual name.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: Online booking and a call-to-action are present, which is a meaningful baseline, but the site has no clickable phone number anywhere across the five pages scanned, no lead capture form, and no live chat, meaning a visitor who is not ready to book a full appointment has no easy way to make contact. For a dental practice where a meaningful share of prospective patients want to ask a quick question before committing, the absence of a click-to-call number and a simple contact form is a direct conversion gap that pushes undecided visitors toward a competitor who makes it easier.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: The Google Business Profile is genuinely strong: a 5.0 rating across 406 reviews is well above what most Canton-area dental practices carry, a review was posted within the last 31 days confirming active patient engagement, and hours, website, and phone are all listed correctly. The photo count of 10 meets the minimum threshold but is on the low end for a dental practice competing in a suburban Atlanta market, where practices with 30 to 50 photos consistently outperform in the local map pack. Whether the GBP description field is filled in could not be confirmed in this scan and is worth checking directly, as a missing or thin description is a common and easily corrected gap.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Analytics 4 is installed, which means basic traffic data is being collected, but there is no Facebook/Meta pixel and no Google Ads conversion tag anywhere on the site. Without these, the practice cannot run retargeting campaigns to recapture visitors who left without booking, cannot build lookalike audiences from existing patient traffic, and has no way to measure which ad spend, if any, is actually producing new patient appointments.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: The site links only to Facebook, and there is no presence linked for Instagram, YouTube, or TikTok, which are the platforms where Canton-area families in the 25 to 45 demographic most frequently discover local service businesses. There is no video content on the site at all, which is a significant missed opportunity for a dental practice, where short-form video showing the office environment, the team, and patient education content consistently drives both trust and appointment requests. The Facebook profile itself was not audited for posting cadence or bio completeness, but the absence of a cross-platform content footprint means the practice is generating no organic social reach beyond whatever Facebook alone provides.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: When AI models are asked about dentists in Canton, GA, they have no training data on Russell Family Dentistry and cannot verify the practice exists, which means the practice is effectively invisible in the fastest-growing discovery channel in local search. Structured data and sameAs entity links are in place, which gives AI systems the right signals when they can read the site, but at least one AI crawler (Bytespider) is actively blocked, there is no llms.txt guidance file to instruct AI models how to represent the business, and there is no FAQ schema for AI to quote directly in response to patient questions. As AI-powered search tools become the first stop for people asking 'who is the best dentist near Canton GA,' a practice that AI assistants cannot find or confidently recommend loses those referrals entirely to whoever AI does know.

findings.title: A 10.5-second load time is sending mobile visitors straight to competitors
findings.detail: The Largest Contentful Paint of 10.5 seconds is more than four times Google's recommended threshold, and on mobile, where the majority of dental searches now originate, most users abandon a page after 3 seconds. Every prospective patient who searches 'dentist Canton GA' on their phone, clicks the Russell Family Dentistry result, and then waits on a blank screen is a lost appointment before the practice ever had a chance to impress them. Google also uses LCP as a ranking signal, so this speed problem is simultaneously costing the site search position and conversion rate.

findings.title: No click-to-call phone number means the easiest conversion is broken
findings.detail: Across all five pages scanned, including the contact page and the make-an-appointment page, there is no tappable phone number, meaning a mobile user who wants to call cannot do so with a single tap. Dental patients, particularly older demographics and parents calling about a child, frequently prefer to call rather than book online, and removing that path entirely means those callers either hunt for the number elsewhere or move on. Given that the practice's 406-review reputation would otherwise close a lot of these calls, the missing click-to-call is a straightforward revenue leak.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know this practice exists, and that gap is growing
findings.detail: A live probe of AI model knowledge returned no training data on Russell Family Dentistry, meaning if a Canton resident asks an AI assistant to recommend a local dentist, this practice will not be named. AI-powered recommendations are now embedded in Google Search, Bing, and standalone tools that millions of people use daily, and the practices AI learns to recommend first will hold that advantage as the behavior compounds. The combination of a blocked crawler, no FAQ schema, and no llms.txt file means the practice is not just unknown today but is actively making it harder for AI systems to learn about it.

findings.title: No ad tracking means any future paid campaigns are flying blind
findings.detail: Without a Google Ads conversion tag or a Meta pixel, the practice cannot attribute a single booked appointment to a paid ad, cannot retarget the visitors who came to the site and left without booking, and cannot build audience lists from its existing patient traffic. If the practice ever runs Google or Meta ads to attract new patients, every dollar spent will produce data that cannot be connected to outcomes, making it impossible to optimize or even justify the investment. Installing these tags costs nothing and is a prerequisite for any performance-based growth strategy.

findings.title: 14 out of 15 site images have no alt text, hurting both SEO and accessibility
findings.detail: Only 1 of the 15 images on the site carries alt text, which means Google cannot understand what those images depict and cannot credit them toward relevant search queries like 'dental office Canton GA' or 'family dentist near me.' It also means the site scores poorly on accessibility for visually impaired visitors, which is both a missed SEO signal and a patient experience issue. The accessibility audit returned a score of 90, which is good overall, but this single pattern of missing alt text is a fixable drag on both rankings and inclusiveness.

findings.title: No Open Graph tags means every social share looks broken
findings.detail: When a patient shares the Russell Family Dentistry website on Facebook, a text message, or any other platform, there is no Open Graph metadata to generate a preview image, title, or description, so the link appears as a raw URL with no visual context. For a practice with a strong 5-star reputation that presumably benefits from word-of-mouth referrals, every shared link that fails to render a clean preview is a small but real erosion of that referral's impact. This is a one-time technical fix that would immediately improve how the practice looks every time someone shares it.

findings.title: No video content on the site or linked social channels removes a high-trust signal
findings.detail: Dental practices that publish short video content, such as office tours, meet-the-team clips, and procedure explainers, consistently report higher new-patient conversion rates because video addresses the anxiety that keeps prospective patients from committing to a first appointment. The site has no video, and no YouTube or Instagram channel is linked, which means the practice is not participating in the format that most effectively converts a curious browser into a booked patient. Given the warm, family-oriented brand implied by the name and the 5-star rating, video content would likely perform well and directly support the goal of growing the patient base.

quickWins: Add a tappable click-to-call phone number to the site header and contact page so mobile visitors can reach the office in one tap.
Add alt text to all 14 images missing it, using descriptive phrases that reflect the actual content of each image and include relevant local keywords.
Add Open Graph meta tags to every page so links shared on Facebook and elsewhere generate a clean image and title preview.
Remove or configure the Bytespider crawler block and create an llms.txt file so AI systems can read and represent the practice accurately.
audit_report.summary: Russell Family Dentistry has the reputation and the local credibility to grow its patient base significantly, but the digital infrastructure around that reputation has gaps that are quietly redirecting prospective patients to other practices. The speed issue, the missing conversion paths, the ad tracking blind spot, and the AI invisibility are each solvable, and fixing them in the right sequence produces compounding results rather than one-off improvements. OHM's role would be to prioritize and implement these corrections in a way that is directly tied to appointment volume, not just technical scores.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the LCP, conversion, tracking, and AI visibility gaps identified here represents a realistic opportunity to capture 15 to 30 additional new patient inquiries per month at current traffic levels, which at an average new-patient value of $800 to $1,200 over the first year translates to $12,000 to $36,000 in annual revenue that is currently leaving the table.

audit_report.headline: Brothers Wilmot Kitchen is earning 5 stars and losing customers anyway, here is exactly where the gap is
audit_report.overallVerdict: A genuinely well-rated restaurant with a perfect Google score and recent review activity is running a website that converts almost no one, is invisible to AI-powered search, and has zero tracking in place to know how badly the situation is costing them.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site is secure (HTTPS), mobile-responsive, and has near-perfect layout stability (CLS of 0), which are solid foundations. However, a mobile Performance score of 73/100 and a Largest Contentful Paint of 3.9 seconds, well above Google's 2.5-second threshold, means the main content is visibly slow to load on phones, and for a restaurant where hungry people are making fast decisions, that delay alone costs visits.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The site has a valid page title and enough word count (637 words) to give Google something to read, but it is missing an H1 heading entirely, has no canonical tag, and, critically, has no local business schema markup, which means Google cannot cleanly parse the restaurant's name, address, cuisine type, or hours from the site itself. The meta description clocks in at only 68 characters, falling short of the 150-160 character range where search snippets are most persuasive, leaving Google to auto-generate what searchers see before they ever click.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: Every single conversion mechanism on the site is absent: no click-to-call phone number, no reservation or booking tool, no contact form, no newsletter capture, no live chat, and no clear call to action anywhere across the scanned pages. A visitor who finds the site and wants to eat there has no obvious next step, which means the site is functioning as a digital brochure rather than a customer acquisition tool.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: The Google Business Profile is operational with a perfect 5.0 rating and a review as recent as 30 days ago, both strong signals for a local restaurant. At 32 reviews, however, the profile sits meaningfully below the 50-review threshold where local trust and map-pack competitiveness tend to accelerate, and most established restaurants in the Woodstock dining scene will have two to four times that count. Hours, website, and phone are all listed correctly, and the photo count meets the minimum bar, but whether the business description is filled in could not be verified on this run and is worth checking directly in the profile dashboard.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: There is no Google Analytics, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads conversion tag installed anywhere on the site. That means every visitor who lands on the site, every person who finds the menu, and every potential customer who bounces away leaves no trace, there is no data on where traffic comes from, which pages people leave from, or whether any marketing effort produces results. Running any paid campaign in this state would be spending money with no ability to measure, optimize, or retarget.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: No social media profiles, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube, are linked from the website, and the scan detected no connected accounts at all, which for a restaurant is a significant missed channel given that food content consistently outperforms other local business categories on visual platforms. There is no video anywhere on the site, and with only 5 images present (4 of which are missing alt text), the content experience gives visitors and algorithms very little to engage with. For a restaurant, Instagram and TikTok in particular offer a low-cost, high-return way to drive consistent foot traffic through dish photography, behind-the-scenes content, and community engagement, none of which appears to be in play.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) are allowed access to the site, and there is enough content depth for an AI to attempt a summary, which are the two baseline requirements. However, when AI models were tested for knowledge of Brothers Wilmot Kitchen in Woodstock, GA, the business was not recognized at all, no training data, no entity knowledge, no recommendation likelihood. The missing structured data, absent sameAs entity links connecting the website to the Google profile and any social presence, and no FAQ content mean there is nothing for AI systems to latch onto and surface when someone asks for restaurant recommendations in Woodstock. As AI-powered queries through ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google's AI Overviews become a primary discovery channel for diners, being completely unknown to those systems is the single fastest-growing visibility gap the business faces.

findings.title: The website sends interested visitors nowhere
findings.detail: Across every page scanned, home and menus, there is no phone number to tap, no reservation link, no form, and no call to action of any kind. A hungry person who finds the site at 6pm on a Friday has no frictionless path to showing up at the restaurant, and the data strongly suggests a meaningful share of those visitors are leaving and choosing somewhere easier. For a restaurant working to grow its customer base, this is the single highest-leverage gap on the entire site.

findings.title: Zero tracking means zero learning, and zero retargeting
findings.detail: With no analytics, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads tag installed, the restaurant is operating completely blind: there is no way to know how many people visit the site per week, where they come from, or what they do before leaving. Beyond the lost insight, the absence of a Meta pixel means the business cannot run retargeting ads to people who already showed interest, one of the highest-ROI ad formats available to local restaurants, and any future paid campaign would launch with no conversion data and no ability to optimize spend.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know this restaurant exists
findings.detail: A live probe of AI model knowledge returned no recognition of Brothers Wilmot Kitchen in Woodstock, GA whatsoever, the business is absent from AI training data and would not appear in AI-generated restaurant recommendations today. With no structured data on the site, no sameAs entity links connecting profiles, and no FAQ content for AI to quote, there is nothing feeding the systems that an increasing share of diners are using to decide where to eat. Competitors who address this now will build an AI presence advantage that compounds over time.

findings.title: Local search rankings are being left on the table with only 32 reviews
findings.detail: A 5.0 star rating is exceptional and a genuine competitive asset, but at 32 total reviews the profile lacks the volume that Google's local ranking algorithm uses alongside rating to surface businesses in the map pack for competitive queries like 'best restaurant in Woodstock' or 'family dinner Woodstock GA'. Restaurants in comparable markets with 80 to 150 reviews and a similar rating will consistently outrank a lower-volume profile, meaning the perfect score is not yet translating into the visibility it should be driving.

findings.title: No social media presence means no organic discovery or community
findings.detail: With no Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, or YouTube linked or detected, the restaurant has no presence in the channels where Woodstock-area diners are actively discovering new places to eat. Restaurant content, especially dish photography and short-form video, regularly generates free reach on Instagram and TikTok that functions as ongoing, compounding advertising. The complete absence of these channels means Brothers Wilmot Kitchen is relying entirely on people who already know it exists to find it, rather than reaching new customers who do not.

findings.title: The slow main image load is quietly hurting mobile conversions
findings.detail: The Largest Contentful Paint of 3.9 seconds on mobile means the main visual, almost certainly a food photo or hero image, takes over three and a half seconds to fully appear for most phone users. Google research consistently shows that every additional second of load time reduces conversions, and for a restaurant where mobile search is the dominant use case (someone driving around deciding where to eat), a slow-loading page creates the impression of a site that is not maintained. This also directly affects Google's mobile ranking signals.

findings.title: Missing H1, schema, and canonical tags are suppressing search visibility
findings.detail: The site has no H1 heading on any scanned page, no local business schema markup, and no canonical tag, three foundational SEO signals that help Google understand what the page is about, confirm it as the authoritative version of the content, and read structured business data like cuisine type, location, and hours. Without schema in particular, the site cannot qualify for rich results in local search (star ratings, hours, address displayed directly in Google results), which are the enhanced listings that drive the highest click-through rates for restaurant searches.

quickWins: Add a tappable phone number and a 'View Menu / Reserve a Table' button to every page, this single change gives every visitor a clear next step and costs almost nothing to implement.
Install Google Analytics (GA4) immediately so that traffic, source data, and user behavior are being captured from this point forward, without it, every other improvement is unverifiable.
Add an H1 heading to the homepage and embed local business schema markup (name, address, phone, cuisine, hours) in the site code to give Google and AI crawlers clean, structured data to read.
Set up and link at least one active Instagram profile to the website, even posting three to five food photos per week puts the restaurant in front of Woodstock-area diners who have never heard of it.
audit_report.summary: Brothers Wilmot Kitchen has something most restaurants would pay for, a perfect rating and genuine customer satisfaction, but the digital infrastructure around it is not capturing the customers that reputation should be generating. The gaps identified here are not cosmetic: missing conversion paths, absent tracking, zero AI presence, and no social footprint are collectively responsible for a measurable number of potential diners choosing somewhere else every single week. Open Heart Media works with local restaurants to close exactly these gaps in a sequenced, prioritized way, and a short discovery call is the right place to map out what that looks like specifically for Brothers Wilmot Kitchen.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the conversion, visibility, and tracking gaps identified in this audit has a realistic potential to convert 15 to 30 additional monthly diners from traffic that is already reaching the site and profile, at an average spend per visit, that represents a meaningful four-figure monthly revenue increase before accounting for the compounding effect of review growth, social reach, and AI discovery.

audit_report.overallVerdict: Century House has a strong local reputation and solid SEO fundamentals, but a slow-loading site, zero conversion infrastructure, no tracking, and complete invisibility to AI recommendation engines are collectively costing it a measurable number of customers every week.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site is secure, mobile-responsive, and layout-stable (CLS 0.001), which covers the basics, but a mobile performance score of 60/100 and a Largest Contentful Paint of 10.0 seconds are serious problems: Google's threshold for a good LCP is 2.5 seconds, meaning the main content takes four times longer than acceptable to appear on a phone screen. At that load speed, a meaningful share of mobile visitors leave before the page is usable, and those are real potential customers walking out the digital door.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The page has proper H1 structure, local business schema, a canonical tag, and 1,283 words of content, all of which are real positives. However, the page title is only 13 characters ('Century House') with no category or location signal, and the meta description runs to 202 characters when Google typically displays around 155-160, meaning the end of the description is cut off in search results and the opportunity to capture clicks with a tight, compelling pitch is partially wasted.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: There is a click-to-call phone number and a listed address, and that is where the conversion infrastructure ends: the site has no online booking, no lead capture form, no newsletter signup, no live chat, and no clear call to action anywhere across the five pages scanned. For a restaurant trying to bring in more customers, the gap between 'visitor arrived' and 'customer sat down' relies entirely on a phone call the site barely prompts, and every other channel for capturing intent is simply absent.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: The Google Business Profile is genuinely strong: a 4.6-star rating from 1,365 reviews is well above what most American restaurants in Woodstock carry, hours, website, phone, description, and photos are all filled in, and a review came in within the last 48 days showing the profile is active. The one real gap here is that the primary GBP category is listed as 'bar' rather than 'American restaurant', which affects which searches Google shows the profile for and likely suppresses impressions from the highest-volume category searches. On-site, local schema and a listed address reinforce the profile well.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: No website analytics, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads conversion tag are installed anywhere on the site, which means Century House has no idea how many people visit, where they come from, what pages they leave on, or whether any ad spend would convert. Without this foundation, any future paid campaign would be running blind, and the cumulative behavioral data that should have been building for years simply does not exist.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: Facebook and Instagram are linked from the site, which establishes baseline presence on the two most relevant platforms for a full-service American restaurant. However, there is no video on the site, no TikTok, no YouTube, and no Open Graph tags, meaning shared links to the site generate no image or preview in social feeds, which actively reduces click-through when anyone posts or shares the URL. For a restaurant category where short food and atmosphere video consistently drives discovery and reservation intent, the absence of any video content and the lack of a TikTok presence represent a significant missed audience, and the opportunity to tighten bios, consistent branding, and a clear link-in-bio strategy across existing profiles remains open.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: The technical groundwork is partially in place: AI crawlers are allowed, structured data is present, and entity links connecting the site's profiles exist, giving AI models the ability to read and index the business in principle. The critical problem is that when AI models are asked about Century House in Woodstock, GA, they do not recognize it and would not recommend it, and there is no FAQ schema for AI to quote, no llms.txt guidance file, and no content formatted in the question-and-answer structure that AI recommendation engines pull from. Buyers increasingly ask AI assistants where to eat before they ever open Google Maps, and a business that AI has never heard of is completely invisible in that channel regardless of how strong its reviews are.

findings.title: No online booking means reservation intent evaporates
findings.detail: Across all five pages scanned, there is no online booking or reservation tool of any kind. A visitor who arrives outside of business hours, or who simply prefers not to call, has no path to commit to a visit, and that intent almost certainly goes to a competitor who makes it easier. For a restaurant with 1,365 reviews and clear demand, the inability to capture a reservation at 11pm when someone is planning their weekend is a direct, recurring revenue leak.

findings.title: 10-second mobile load time is turning away the highest-intent visitors
findings.detail: A Largest Contentful Paint of 10.0 seconds on mobile means someone searching 'American restaurant Woodstock GA' on their phone, clicking through to Century House, and waiting for the page to load is likely to leave before it renders. Google's own data shows mobile bounce rates climb sharply after 3 seconds; at 10 seconds, a conservative estimate is that 50-70% of mobile visitors abandon before engaging. Given that mobile accounts for the majority of local restaurant searches, this is not a minor technical issue.

findings.title: Zero tracking means there is no data foundation for growth
findings.detail: With no analytics, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads tag installed, Century House cannot measure how many people visit the site, what actions they take, or what converting a visitor actually looks like. This also means retargeting is impossible: people who visited the site and left cannot be shown a follow-up ad. Any investment in paid traffic or social ads made right now would have no measurement layer, making optimization impossible and wasting budget.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know Century House exists
findings.detail: A direct probe of AI model knowledge returned no recognition of Century House in Woodstock, GA, and the AI would not recommend it in its category. As more diners ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews where to eat before opening a map app, businesses that are not in the AI's knowledge base are simply not in the consideration set. With no FAQ schema, no llms.txt file, and no Q&A-formatted content, the site is not giving AI models anything to quote or reason from.

findings.title: GBP primary category 'bar' suppresses restaurant search visibility
findings.detail: The live Google Business Profile shows the primary category set to 'bar' rather than 'American restaurant' or 'restaurant'. Google uses the primary category as the strongest signal for which searches to show a listing in, so Century House is likely appearing less often for the high-volume searches ('dinner Woodstock GA', 'American food near me') that represent its core customer base, while appearing for bar searches that may not match the experience it actually delivers.

findings.title: No calls to action or email capture means the site collects nothing
findings.detail: The site has no clear call to action, no newsletter signup, and no form of any kind across five pages. Every visitor who is not ready to call right now leaves without any relationship being established. A restaurant with over 1,300 satisfied reviewers has a proven customer base that would respond to a well-positioned email list, whether for weekly specials, events, or reservation reminders, and that channel is currently generating zero value.

findings.title: No video content and no Open Graph tags reduce social reach
findings.detail: The site has no video content, and Open Graph share tags are missing, which means any link shared on Facebook, Instagram, or text message generates a blank or broken preview rather than an image and description. For a restaurant where atmosphere and food visuals are among the strongest drivers of visit intent, this is a practical suppression of word-of-mouth amplification. The absence of any TikTok presence also leaves a fast-growing food discovery channel completely untouched.

quickWins: Install Google Analytics 4 and a Meta pixel this week so every future decision has data behind it and retargeting becomes possible.
Change the Google Business Profile primary category from 'bar' to 'American restaurant' to immediately improve visibility in the searches that match actual customer intent.
Add Open Graph meta tags to the site so that every shared link on Facebook, Instagram, or iMessage generates a proper image and description preview.
Add FAQ schema markup and a short Q&A section to the site so AI models have structured, quotable content to pull from when recommending restaurants in Woodstock.
audit_report.summary: Century House has earned a genuinely strong local reputation, and the core SEO and GBP signals are mostly working in its favor. The gaps, a 10-second mobile load time, no booking or conversion tools, no tracking infrastructure, and no presence in AI recommendation engines, are not minor polish items; they are the specific reasons customers who searched, arrived, and were almost convinced either bounced or went somewhere easier. Open Heart Media can close each of these gaps with a clear sequence and measurable outcomes, and the discovery call is where we walk through which ones to prioritize first based on fastest revenue return.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the booking, tracking, speed, and AI visibility gaps for a restaurant with Century House's review volume and rating realistically points to 15-30 additional covered tables per week within 90 days, with a direct email and retargeting list that compounds in value every month after that.

audit_report.headline: Where Rally Point Grille is quietly losing customers before they ever walk in the door
audit_report.overallVerdict: Rally Point Grille has a genuinely strong local reputation and solid SEO bones, but a critically slow mobile site, no paid retargeting infrastructure, and zero presence in AI-powered search are bleeding real foot traffic every week.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: Google PageSpeed scores the mobile site at 36 out of 100, with a Largest Contentful Paint of 12.2 seconds and a Cumulative Layout Shift of 0.386, both of which are severe failures against Google's thresholds of 2.5 seconds and 0.1 respectively. The site is securely on HTTPS and renders correctly on mobile, so the foundation is intact, but the speed and stability problems mean a large share of mobile visitors are bouncing before the page finishes loading.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The on-page SEO fundamentals are well executed: a properly sized title tag, a 156-character meta description, a single clean H1, local business schema markup, a canonical tag, and over 2,500 words of indexable content are all confirmed present. The one meaningful gap in this category is the absence of FAQ schema, which limits how much structured information search engines and AI systems can surface directly in results.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: Online booking and a visible call to action are confirmed present, and the click-to-call phone number is accessible, which covers the basics. However, there is no lead capture form, no email or newsletter signup, and no live chat anywhere across the scanned pages, meaning visitors who are not ready to book immediately have no way to stay connected, and the business has no mechanism to build a first-party audience for repeat marketing.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: With a 4.6-star rating across 2,546 reviews, Rally Point Grille sits well above the typical bar and grill in the Woodstock area in both volume and score, which is a genuine competitive asset. Business hours, website link, phone number, and description are all filled in on the Google Business Profile. The one flag worth noting is that the most recent review Google shows us is 148 days old, which, regardless of whether newer reviews exist, is the signal Google's interface is currently presenting to prospective customers researching the restaurant.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Analytics 4 is installed, so baseline traffic data is being collected. However, neither a Meta pixel nor a Google Ads conversion tag is present anywhere on the site, which means the business cannot run retargeting campaigns to re-engage visitors who browsed the menu but did not book, cannot build lookalike audiences from its web traffic, and has no conversion signal to optimize paid campaigns against if it ever runs them.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: Facebook and Instagram are both linked from the site, and the site itself includes video content, which is a positive signal. However, there is no confirmed presence on YouTube or TikTok, the two platforms where short-form food and bar content consistently drives discovery for restaurants in 2024 and 2025. Without knowing the current state of profile completeness, posting frequency, or bio optimization on the existing channels, there is a clear opportunity to audit whether the Instagram and Facebook profiles have consistent branding, a direct link to the booking page, and a content cadence that would convert a casual scroller into a first-time guest.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers including GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot are all permitted to access the site, and structured data is in place, which means the technical door is open. However, when AI models were tested on their knowledge of Rally Point Grille in Woodstock, GA, the result was explicit: the business is not recognized and would not be recommended in its category. The missing pieces that explain this gap are the absence of sameAs entity links connecting the website to its social profiles and directory listings, no FAQ schema for AI to quote directly, and no llms.txt guidance file. Buyers are increasingly asking AI assistants where to eat or grab drinks in Woodstock rather than scrolling Google, and a business that AI has never heard of is simply invisible in that channel.

findings.title: A 12-second load time is turning away the majority of mobile visitors
findings.detail: Google's own research shows that 53 percent of mobile users abandon a page that takes longer than 3 seconds to load. At 12.2 seconds LCP and a layout shift score of 0.386, Rally Point Grille's mobile site is losing well over half of its mobile traffic before a single menu item is seen. For a bar and grill where the majority of hungry or thirsty customers are searching on their phones while deciding where to go right now, this is the single highest-cost technical problem on the site.

findings.title: No Meta pixel means every past visitor is gone forever from a marketing standpoint
findings.detail: Without a Meta pixel installed, Rally Point Grille cannot retarget the people who visited the menu page and left, cannot build a lookalike audience from its web traffic to find new customers in Woodstock who look like its current regulars, and cannot measure whether any organic social content is actually driving visits. Given that Facebook and Instagram are already linked from the site, the retargeting infrastructure is one missing tag away from being usable.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know this business exists, and that gap is growing weekly
findings.detail: A live probe of AI model knowledge returned a clear result: Rally Point Grille is not recognized and would not be recommended when someone asks an AI assistant for bar and grill options in Woodstock, GA. The contributing factors confirmed in the scan are the absence of sameAs entity links, no FAQ schema, and no llms.txt file. As more local searches shift to AI-powered answers in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews, an unrecognized business loses that traffic entirely to whichever competitors AI does know about.

findings.title: No email capture means the business is building no owned audience
findings.detail: There is no newsletter signup or lead capture form anywhere across the website, including the food menu and locations pages. Every visitor who does not book immediately is lost with no way to re-engage them for a happy hour special, a weekend event, or a seasonal menu launch. An owned email list is the only marketing channel that is immune to algorithm changes and platform policy shifts, and Rally Point Grille is currently collecting zero of it.

findings.title: No Google Ads conversion tag means paid search is not a usable growth channel right now
findings.detail: The absence of a Google Ads conversion tag means that if Rally Point Grille ever runs or has run Google Search ads targeting high-intent queries like 'bar and grill Woodstock GA' or 'sports bar near me', there is no way to know which clicks led to a reservation or a phone call. Without conversion data, Google's algorithm cannot optimize toward the clicks most likely to produce a customer, making any ad spend significantly less efficient than it could be.

findings.title: TikTok and YouTube absence leaves the highest-reach food discovery channels untouched
findings.detail: Bar and grill content, specifically food reveals, drink specials, game-day atmosphere, and behind-the-bar clips, performs exceptionally well on TikTok and YouTube Shorts and is a primary driver of new customer discovery for independent restaurants in 2024 and 2025. Rally Point Grille has no confirmed presence on either platform, which means it is not reaching the segment of potential customers who discover restaurants through short-form video rather than Google search.

findings.title: The review recency signal on the Google profile deserves attention
findings.detail: The most recent review Google is currently surfacing on the profile is 148 days old. Whether or not newer reviews have been submitted, this is the signal Google is showing prospective customers who research the restaurant before deciding where to eat. A competitor with a more recent visible review cadence can appear more actively monitored and more popular in the moment, even with fewer total reviews, which matters in a market where trust signals drive the final decision.

quickWins: Install the Meta pixel on the site immediately so every future visitor can be retargeted and audience-building begins from this week forward.

Add sameAs entity links in the site's structured data connecting the website to its Google Business Profile, Facebook, and Instagram URLs so AI models and search engines can verify and recognize the business as a single consistent entity.
Add a simple email capture to the site, even a one-field 'get our specials' bar in the footer, to begin building a first-party audience that can be marketed to directly.
Create and claim a TikTok business profile and a YouTube channel under the Rally Point Grille brand now, even before posting, to secure the handles and signal presence to AI indexing systems.
audit_report.summary: Rally Point Grille has the raw ingredients of a strong local brand: a 4.6-star rating at scale, solid on-page SEO, and confirmed booking capability. What is costing it customers right now is a mobile experience that loses most visitors before the page loads, a complete absence of paid retargeting infrastructure, and invisibility in the AI-powered search channel that is reshaping how diners discover local restaurants. Open Heart Media can quantify exactly how much traffic is being lost at each of these gaps and build the specific remediation plan to close them.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the mobile speed gap alone typically recovers 20 to 40 percent of lost mobile sessions; adding retargeting and email capture to a site already receiving organic traffic can realistically convert an additional 15 to 25 visitors per week into customers, representing meaningful incremental revenue for a bar and grill with strong average check values.

categories.name: Website & Speed

A mixed-content warning on an otherwise secure site adds a credibility flag that browsers surface to cautious health-conscious visitors, compounding the first-impression problem.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The site has local business schema, a canonical tag, a reasonable word count of 1,864 words, and a properly sized page title, which are real strengths for a local chiropractic practice. categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: This is the most commercially damaging section in the entire audit: across every page scanned, there is no clickable phone number, no lead capture form, no online booking or scheduling tool, and no live chat, meaning a visitor who arrives ready to book an appointment has no frictionless way to act on that intent. The site has a call-to-action present, which prevents the score from hitting zero, but a CTA with nowhere to go is a signpost on a road with no destination, and every motivated visitor who leaves without contacting the practice is a patient Revive will never know it lost.

categories.name: Local Visibility

categories.name: Tracking & Data

categories.name: Social & Content

The profiles that do exist have not been audited for complete bios, consistent branding, a direct booking link in bio, or a regular posting cadence, all of which are the difference between a social profile that generates patient inquiries and one that simply exists.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)

The critical problem is that when AI models are asked about chiropractic and wellness options in Woodstock, GA, they do not recognize Revive Health Center and Spa by name and would not recommend it, meaning the practice is currently invisible in the fastest-growing new referral channel for local health services. There is also no FAQ schema for AI to quote directly and no llms.txt guidance file, both of which are increasingly used by AI systems to identify authoritative, recommendable local businesses.

findings.title: No phone, no form, no booking: the site cannot convert anyone
findings.detail: The scan confirmed that across the homepage and contact page, there is no clickable phone link, no intake or inquiry form, and no scheduling integration. A prospective patient who finds the site through Google, reads about the services, and wants to book an appointment has no direct action available to them except manually copying a number if they can even find one, a friction point that the majority of mobile users will not tolerate. Conservative industry data suggests that local health service sites without online booking lose 30 to 50 percent of mobile visitors who had genuine purchase intent.

findings.title: Zero tracking means zero ability to measure or scale growth
findings.detail: With no analytics, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads tag installed, Revive cannot answer the most basic marketing questions: how many people visit the site each week, which services generate the most interest, or whether the social posts and any word-of-mouth traffic are actually converting into contact attempts. This also means that if Revive were to run a Google or Meta ad campaign tomorrow to bring in more patients, every dollar spent would be untrackable, and warm website visitors could not be retargeted, effectively doubling or tripling the cost per acquired patient compared to a properly instrumented competitor.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know Revive exists
findings.detail: A direct probe of AI model knowledge returned no recognition of Revive Health Center and Spa in Woodstock, GA, which means when a potential patient asks ChatGPT, Perplexity, or a voice assistant for a chiropractor or wellness spa recommendation in the area, Revive is not in the answer. This gap is not theoretical: AI-assisted search is already influencing local health and wellness decisions, and businesses that build AI visibility now will hold a durable advantage as the channel matures. The absence of FAQ schema and an llms.txt file are specific, addressable reasons the site is not being surfaced.

findings.title: A 7.6-second load time is turning away mobile patients before the page renders
findings.detail: Google's threshold for a good Largest Contentful Paint is 2.5 seconds; Revive's is 7.6 seconds on mobile, which is three times the failing threshold and in the bottom tier of performance for local health businesses. This also suppresses Google's ranking of the site in mobile-first indexing.

findings.title: Two photos on the Google Business Profile in a visually competitive local market

With only 2 photos, Revive's profile looks thin next to competitors who show their treatment rooms, staff, and patient environment, and Google's local ranking algorithm weights photo activity as a signal of an engaged, active business.

findings.title: 49 reviews and a 199-day-old visible review are leaving the profile short of its potential

A consistent, systematic review generation process tied to the post-appointment experience would turn this from a marginal gap into a clear competitive lead.

findings.title: No video on the site or linked video channel limits trust-building and search reach
findings.detail: Health and wellness decisions are among the highest-trust purchases a local consumer makes, and video is the format that builds the fastest rapport between a practice and a prospective patient who has never walked through the door. audit_report.summary: Revive Health Center and Spa has the reputation and the clinical credibility to grow significantly faster than it currently is, but the digital infrastructure connecting that reputation to new patients is broken in several specific and fixable ways. Open Heart Media has mapped exactly where the patient journey breaks down, which platforms are failing to carry Revive's story, and what it would take to make AI assistants and Google work as active referral sources rather than missed opportunities. findings.title: Zero photos on the Google Business Profile is actively suppressing map pack rankings

findings.title: No phone number on the Google Business Profile means direct calls from Google are impossible
findings.detail: Google Business Profile allows customers to call a business directly from the search result without ever visiting the website, and that tap-to-call button is one of the highest-converting touchpoints in local search. Two specific structural gaps are contributing to this: there are no sameAs entity links connecting the website to external profiles that would help AI models build a confident knowledge graph entry for the business, and there is no FAQ schema giving AI a quotable question-and-answer layer to surface. As buyers increasingly ask AI assistants for local service recommendations instead of scrolling search results, being unrecognized at this stage is the single most urgent emerging visibility gap the business faces.

findings.title: Zero tracking means zero accountability for every dollar spent on growth

findings.title: AI assistants do not know this business exists

findings.title: A 5.8-second mobile load is driving away visitors before they see the offer

Traffic arriving from Google or social ads and bouncing on load time is traffic that was paid for in time or money and produced nothing.

findings.title: No email capture means the business owns none of its audience
findings.detail: There is no newsletter signup or email capture mechanism anywhere on the site, which means every visitor who does not book on the first visit is gone with no recovery path. findings.title: The missing canonical tag creates a quiet SEO leak
findings.detail: Without a canonical tag, Google cannot determine which version of any given page is the one that should accumulate ranking authority when the same content is reachable through multiple URLs. For a site that already has good content depth and schema in place, this is a structural inefficiency that can cause ranking signals to be split rather than concentrated, depressing search positions that the content quality would otherwise deserve.

findings.title: Review velocity needs monitoring as a local ranking signal
findings.detail: The most recent review Google shows is 84 days old across a base of 75 reviews, and while Google may be surfacing reviews by relevance rather than chronology, review velocity is a confirmed factor in local pack rankings. audit_report.summary: Ingrid's Spa and Wellness has the raw ingredients of a strong local business: a real rating, a functional website, and an actual booking system. findings.title: Missing Local Business schema is leaving rich search results on the table
findings.detail: Local Business schema markup is completely absent from the site, which means Google cannot reliably extract structured signals about the practice's name, address, phone, service categories, or hours directly from the website's code. This reduces eligibility for rich results in local search and weakens the trust signal that supports the Google Business Profile, particularly for queries around specific services like pet dentistry or veterinary surgery where structured data helps Google match the site to intent-based searches.

findings.title: No Meta pixel or Google Ads tag means paid advertising cannot be turned on effectively
findings.detail: Neither the Facebook/Instagram pixel nor a Google Ads conversion tag is installed on the site. This matters even if Affordable Vet Center is not running paid ads today: every day without the pixel is a day the retargeting audience is not being built from organic visitors. When a campaign is eventually launched, or when a competitor targets the same zip codes, this practice will start from zero audience data while competitors with pixels installed will already have warm audiences built from months of site traffic.

findings.title: No lead capture or contact form removes any fallback for visitors not ready to book
findings.detail: The site has online booking, which serves clients ready to commit, but there is no form, no chat, and no email capture for the larger segment of visitors in research mode, comparing vets, checking pricing, or asking a quick question about a service. In a local services category like veterinary care, a significant portion of new clients make contact two or more times before booking. Without any middle-of-funnel capture mechanism, those visitors are lost permanently.

findings.title: No video content on site or linked social channels is a missed trust-building opportunity
findings.detail: Video is the highest-trust content format for healthcare-adjacent decisions, and veterinary practices that publish short walkthroughs of their clinic, introductions to their veterinarians, or basic pet wellness content consistently outperform text-only sites in both time-on-site and conversion rate. The practice has neither video on the website nor a YouTube or TikTok presence, which means it is competing entirely on written content and reviews against practices that may already be building visual trust with Woodstock pet owners.

quickWins: Add a tap-to-call phone number to the site header and footer on every page, this is the single fastest conversion fix given the mobile traffic most veterinary sites receive.
Install the Meta pixel and Google Ads conversion tag immediately, even before running any paid campaigns, so that a retargeting audience starts building from today's organic visitors.
Add Local Business schema markup to the homepage and key service pages to improve Google's ability to parse and surface the practice in local and rich-result searches.

Check and complete the Google Business Profile description if it is not already filled in, it is the one GBP field that was not measurable in this scan and it directly influences how Google presents the practice in local results.
