audit_report.headline: Where DirtyDoggy Dog Wash is quietly losing customers before they ever book
audit_report.overallVerdict: DirtyDoggy Dog Wash has a real foundation to build on, but a slow mobile site, invisible AI presence, zero tracking, and disconnected social channels are letting warm, ready-to-book pet owners slip away to competitors every single day.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: Google's PageSpeed scores the mobile site at 50/100, which is technically a pass on the check but a genuine user experience problem: the Largest Contentful Paint clocks in at 7.2 seconds, nearly three times the 2.5-second threshold Google considers acceptable, meaning a typical dog owner on their phone waits seven seconds before the page even looks loaded. HTTPS is active, the layout is stable (CLS 0.019), and the site is mobile-responsive, but a 590ms Total Blocking Time tells Google that interactive elements are sluggish, which suppresses search rankings and drives impatient visitors to hit the back button.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The page title is present and correctly sized, local business schema is in place, and there is a canonical tag, which are real positives. However, the meta description is completely missing site-wide, meaning Google writes its own snippet for every search result, which typically underperforms a crafted one, and there is not a single H1 heading anywhere on the site, removing one of the clearest on-page signals Google uses to understand what a page is about.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: The site has a contact form, an online booking tool, and a call to action, which gives visitors a path to book, but there is no click-to-call phone number anywhere on the site, which is a significant friction point for mobile users who want to ask a quick question before committing. There is no live chat and no email or newsletter capture, so visitors who are not ready to book immediately have no low-friction way to stay connected, and the business has no mechanism to follow up with them later.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: A 4.7-star rating across 44 reviews is genuinely strong and reflects well on the quality of service, but the review count sits just below the 50-review threshold that noticeably shifts how Google ranks local businesses in a competitive grooming market like Woodstock. The most recent review Google surfaces is 104 days old, and while Google may be holding back newer reviews due to its relevance ranking, that visible gap in freshness can signal stagnation to both Google and prospective customers comparing profiles. Hours, website, and phone are all listed correctly, and the profile has photos, but whether the business description and primary category are filled in could not be confirmed on this run and should be checked directly.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: There is no Google Analytics, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads conversion tag installed anywhere on the site, which means the business is operating entirely without data: it cannot see how many people visit, where they come from, which pages they leave from, or whether a booking was ever completed. Without a pixel or ads tag, paid advertising campaigns cannot be retargeted or optimized, so any future ad spend would be flying blind, and every visitor who does not book immediately is gone forever with no ability to re-engage them.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: No social media profiles are linked anywhere on the site, meaning Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube are all unconnected from the web presence, which is a serious gap for a pet grooming business where before-and-after photos and short dog videos are among the highest-performing content types on the internet. The site does include a video, which is a genuine positive, but that asset is essentially isolated and not amplified through any social channel. For a business trying to bring in more local customers, a well-optimized Instagram or TikTok profile with consistent grooming content, a clear link to the booking page, and complete contact information in the bio represents one of the most cost-effective customer acquisition channels available.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers including GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot are all allowed access to the site, and structured data is in place, both of which are positive starting points. However, when AI models are asked about DirtyDoggy Dog Wash in Woodstock, GA, they return nothing: the business is not recognized by name, not recommended in the pet grooming category, and there are no entity links (sameAs connections to Google Business Profile, social pages, or directories) that help AI systems understand this is a real, established local business. Buyers are increasingly asking AI assistants to recommend local services, and a business that AI has never heard of is completely invisible in that channel, which is becoming a meaningful source of new customer discovery that competitors will occupy first if this gap is not addressed.

findings.title: A 7.2-second load time is costing bookings on mobile
findings.detail: Google's own research shows that 53% of mobile visitors abandon a page that takes longer than 3 seconds to load, and DirtyDoggy's mobile LCP of 7.2 seconds is nearly three times that threshold. For a grooming business where most local searches happen on a phone while someone is deciding right now, every second of delay is a direct reduction in the number of people who ever reach the booking button. The 590ms Total Blocking Time compounds this by making the page feel frozen even after content starts to appear.

findings.title: No analytics means the business cannot see what is working or broken
findings.detail: With no Google Analytics, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads tag in place, there is no way to know how many people visit the site each month, which search terms bring them in, what percentage make it to the booking page, or how many abandon before completing a reservation. This is not just a reporting gap: without conversion data, any money spent on ads in the future cannot be optimized, retargeting audiences cannot be built, and there is no baseline to measure whether any marketing improvement actually drives more customers. The business is currently making decisions based entirely on guesswork.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know this business exists
findings.detail: A live probe of AI models found that DirtyDoggy Dog Wash in Woodstock, GA is completely unrecognized: no training data, no recommendation in the pet grooming category, and no entity connections that would let an AI confidently surface this business when a local resident asks for grooming recommendations. The site lacks FAQ schema, has only 331 words of content (too thin for AI to generate a meaningful summary), and has no sameAs entity links connecting the website to the Google Business Profile or any directories. As AI-powered search tools become a primary discovery channel for local services, being absent from this layer is the equivalent of not appearing in Google Maps five years ago.

findings.title: No social presence means zero organic reach from the highest-engagement content category in pet care
findings.detail: Dog grooming content, specifically before-and-after transformations, bath reactions, and breed-specific styling, consistently generates outsized organic reach on Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook without paid promotion. No social profiles are linked from the site, which means the business has no presence in the channels where Woodstock pet owners are actively discovering local services through content. A single well-executed short video per week could reach thousands of local pet owners at zero media cost, and the business is currently capturing none of that.

findings.title: Missing meta description and zero H1 tags are limiting search click-through
findings.detail: When DirtyDoggy appears in Google search results, Google is auto-generating the snippet text because no meta description was written, which typically results in a lower click-through rate than a crafted description that speaks directly to what a searching pet owner wants to know. The complete absence of an H1 heading across the entire site also removes a foundational ranking signal: Google uses H1 tags to confirm what a page is about, and without one, the site is competing for grooming-related searches with one hand tied behind its back.

findings.title: 44 reviews and a 104-day visible gap put the profile at a competitive disadvantage
findings.detail: The 4.7-star average is a genuine asset, but the review count of 44 sits just below the 50-review level where Google's local algorithm begins to treat a business as more authoritatively established, and the most recent review Google surfaces is 104 days old. In a local grooming market where a competitor with 80 recent reviews will rank above a business with 44 older ones regardless of star rating, this is a gap that costs visibility and new customer calls every week. Closing this gap does not require exceptional service, it requires a systematic process for asking satisfied customers to share their experience.

findings.title: No click-to-call phone number eliminates the fastest path to a booking
findings.detail: A mobile visitor who wants to ask whether a specific breed is accepted, how long an appointment takes, or what a full groom costs cannot tap a phone number anywhere on the site because none is linked as a clickable tel: link. This is the single highest-intent action a local service customer takes on mobile, and the friction of having to copy a number manually or navigate elsewhere means a meaningful percentage of those visitors will call a competitor whose number is one tap away. A phone number is listed on the Google Business Profile, but it does not carry over to the website.

quickWins: Add a click-to-call phone number to the site header and footer so mobile visitors can reach the business in one tap.
Write and publish a meta description of 140 to 155 characters for the homepage that names the service, city, and a reason to choose DirtyDoggy over a competitor.
Add a single clear H1 tag to the homepage, something like 'Professional Dog Grooming in Woodstock, GA', to give Google and visitors an immediate signal about what the page is.
Install Google Analytics 4 immediately so the business can begin measuring how many visitors arrive, where they come from, and whether they complete a booking.
audit_report.summary: DirtyDoggy Dog Wash has the raw ingredients of a high-performing local business: a strong star rating, a booking system, and a service that generates naturally shareable content. What is missing is the infrastructure that turns online visibility into a predictable stream of new customers: a fast, optimized site, a tracking foundation, an AI-ready content layer, and a social presence that keeps the business in front of Woodstock pet owners between appointments. Open Heart Media has mapped exactly where the drop-off is happening and what closing each gap is realistically worth.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the speed, SEO, tracking, social, and AI visibility gaps identified in this audit represents a realistic path to 30 to 60 additional booked appointments per month at current conversion rates, based on the volume of local grooming searches in the Woodstock area and the friction points currently in the way.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: Online booking and a click-to-call number are present, which is genuinely good, but there is no lead capture form, no live chat, and no email or newsletter capture anywhere across all five scanned pages, so any visitor who is not ready to book on the spot has no lower-commitment way to stay connected. The physical address is also absent from the site, which removes a basic local trust signal that many pet owners use to verify a business before handing over their dog.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: A 4.6-star rating across 104 reviews is a genuine competitive asset for a pet groomer in Acworth, placing My Groomer INC above the median for local trust signals. The profile description and primary category could not be verified in this scan and should be checked directly, because missing or thin descriptions are a known factor in lower local pack rankings. The most recent review Google surfaces is 491 days old, and while Google may be holding back newer ones, any real gap in review velocity is a risk because Google's local algorithm actively rewards businesses generating consistent fresh reviews.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: No analytics platform, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads conversion tag were detected anywhere on the site, meaning there is currently no way to know how many people visit, where they come from, which pages they abandon, or whether a booking actually resulted from any marketing effort. Without this data, any future ad spend is essentially unaccountable, and there is no baseline to measure growth against.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: No Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, or TikTok profile is linked from the site, and no video content exists on any scanned page, which is a significant gap for a pet grooming business where before-and-after photos and short grooming clips are among the highest-performing content types in the category. The absence of linked social profiles also means the site cannot pass brand authority signals outward, and any social presence that does exist offline is completely disconnected from the web footprint. For a business that depends on local word-of-mouth, a consistent Instagram or TikTok presence with optimized bios, a clear booking link, and regular posts is one of the fastest organic channels available.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers are open and structured data plus an FAQ schema are in place, which means the technical door is unlocked, but when AI models are asked about pet groomers in Acworth, GA, they have no training data on My Groomer INC and would not recommend the business. The missing piece is entity links: without sameAs connections tying the website to the Google Business Profile, social profiles, and directory listings, AI systems cannot confidently identify this as a real, established local business. As more pet owners turn to ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews to ask 'who should groom my dog in Acworth,' being invisible in that channel is a growing revenue leak that will compound as AI-assisted search continues to take share from traditional results.

findings.title: An 8.3-second load time is bleeding mobile bookings
findings.detail: Google's threshold for a good Largest Contentful Paint is 2.5 seconds. My Groomer INC's mobile LCP of 8.3 seconds puts it in the bottom performance tier, and Google's own data shows that mobile bounce rates rise sharply beyond 3 seconds. For a service where a pet owner searching 'dog groomer near me' on their phone makes a decision in under a minute, losing them to a slow load means losing a booking worth $50 to $100 or more, potentially repeatedly if they would have become a regular client.

findings.title: Zero tracking means zero accountability for every marketing dollar
findings.detail: With no Google Analytics, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads tag, My Groomer INC has no visibility into how many people visit the site each month, which source sends the most traffic, or how many visitors actually complete a booking. This is not just a data gap: it means any investment in ads, SEO, or social cannot be measured or optimized, and the business has no way to know which growth efforts are working.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know this business exists
findings.detail: A direct probe of AI models returned no recognition of My Groomer INC in Acworth, GA, and confirmed the business would not be recommended in the pet grooming category. The cause is traceable: there are no sameAs entity links connecting the website to the Google Business Profile or any directory, so AI systems cannot verify the business as a real local entity. As a growing share of local service searches move to AI-assisted queries, this invisibility is a customer acquisition gap that does not yet exist for most small pet groomers but is closing fast.

findings.title: No social presence means no organic discovery channel
findings.detail: Pet grooming is one of the most visually shareable service categories: before-and-after photos, breed-specific cuts, and short grooming videos routinely generate organic reach on Instagram and TikTok without ad spend. No social profiles are linked from the site, and no video exists on any page, meaning My Groomer INC is entirely absent from the channel where many local pet owners discover new service providers. A competitor with even a modest posting cadence is capturing that audience by default.

findings.title: No lead capture means one-time visitors are gone for good
findings.detail: Across all five scanned pages, there is no contact form, no email capture, and no newsletter option. A visitor who lands on the site but is not ready to book immediately has no path to stay connected, and My Groomer INC has no way to follow up. For a recurring service like grooming, the lifetime value of a retained client is significant, making the absence of even a simple 'book your first appointment' email capture a compounding revenue loss.

findings.title: Review velocity is a ranking risk if it has slowed
findings.detail: The most recent review Google surfaces for My Groomer INC is 491 days old. While Google may be surfacing older reviews by relevance rather than date, any real slowdown in review generation is a direct local ranking factor: Google's local algorithm favors businesses with consistent, recent review activity. A groomer seeing 10 or more clients per day has the volume to be generating reviews at a pace that reinforces its position in the local pack, and that opportunity appears to be underused.

findings.title: Mixed content and a duplicate H1 create quiet SEO drag
findings.detail: Mixed content, where insecure HTTP assets load on a secure HTTPS page, can suppress trust indicators in browsers and is flagged by Google as a security issue. Combined with two H1 tags on the same page, which splits the page's primary topic signal, these are the kinds of technical issues that do not break a site but consistently hold rankings just below where they could be, costing organic positions to competitors who have cleaner setups.

quickWins: Install Google Analytics 4 immediately: it is free, takes under 30 minutes to add, and every growth decision made from this point forward depends on having baseline data.
Consolidate the two H1 tags into one clear, keyword-specific headline on the homepage to sharpen Google's understanding of the page's primary topic.
Add the physical address as visible text on the website, ideally in the footer and on the contact page, to restore the local trust signal it is currently missing.

Claim and optimize at least one social profile (Instagram is the highest-return starting point for a pet groomer) and link it from the site to begin building entity connections that both search engines and AI systems use to verify business identity.
audit_report.summary: My Groomer INC has earned real customer trust with a 4.6-star rating, but the infrastructure around that reputation is leaving significant growth on the table: slow page loads are losing mobile visitors before they book, no tracking means the business is operating without any data, social and AI channels are completely dark, and there is no system to capture or re-engage visitors who are not ready to book on first contact. Open Heart Media works with local service businesses to close exactly these gaps in a structured sequence, prioritizing the fixes with the fastest and largest return first. The gaps here are real but fixable, and the upside from closing them is directly tied to the volume of new clients My Groomer INC is trying to add.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the speed, tracking, social, and AI visibility gaps identified here could realistically add 15 to 30 new client inquiries per month at current traffic levels, with compounding upside as organic and AI-driven discovery grow over the following two to three quarters.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site earns full marks for HTTPS, a stable layout (CLS of 0), and mobile responsiveness, but the mobile PageSpeed score of 55/100 is well below the 70+ threshold Google uses to favor sites in search rankings. The Largest Contentful Paint of 14.9 seconds is the real damage: Google's own benchmark for a good user experience is under 2.5 seconds, meaning the average mobile visitor is staring at a loading screen for nearly 15 seconds before the page is usable, and most will leave before it finishes.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The basics are covered: the page title is a clean 61 characters, the meta description is present at 155 characters, there is a single clear H1, a canonical tag is set, and the page has a respectable 1,401 words of content. categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: The site does have a click-to-call phone number, a lead capture form, and a visible call to action, which is a workable baseline for capturing intent. However, there is no online scheduling, no live chat, no email or newsletter capture, and no address listed anywhere on the site across all three scanned pages, all of which are meaningful friction points for a local insurance shopper who wants a fast, low-commitment first step before committing to a phone call.

A profile with minimal photos and low review volume signals to Google that the business is less active than competitors, suppressing local rankings regardless of the star rating.

categories.name: Tracking & Data

categories.name: Social & Content

For an insurance agency, the opportunity sits in profile optimization: consistent branding across handles, a clear link-in-bio routing to a quote form, and a regular cadence of short educational content (coverage tips, rate-shopping advice, local weather and risk reminders) that builds trust before a buyer ever picks up the phone. Six of the eighteen site images are also missing alt text, which is both a search and accessibility gap.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers are open and allowed, which is the right starting position, and FAQ schema and sameAs entity links are in place, but there is no structured data for the business itself and no llms.txt guidance file to help AI models understand what this agency does and who it serves. Being unknown to AI today is the fastest-growing visibility gap in local search, and competitors who close it first will claim that channel before others realize the window has passed.

findings.title: A 14.9-second load time is sending mobile shoppers straight to competitors
findings.detail: The mobile Largest Contentful Paint of 14.9 seconds is nearly six times slower than Google's acceptable threshold of 2.5 seconds. Insurance is a high-intent, high-comparison category: a shopper who hits a slow page on their phone while sitting in a parking lot or waiting at a light will hit the back button and click the next result within seconds, and that competitor gets the quote request instead. At any meaningful volume of paid or organic traffic, this one metric represents a direct, measurable transfer of leads to faster sites.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know this business exists, and that gap is growing daily
findings.detail: A direct probe of AI model knowledge returned no verified information about Woodstock Car Insurance, meaning that when a prospective customer asks an AI assistant to recommend a car insurance agency in Woodstock, GA, this business is not in the conversation. This channel is still early enough that moving now would establish a durable advantage, but the window is shorter than most local business owners realize.

findings.title: 31 reviews is holding back map pack rankings in a competitive suburban market
findings.detail: Cherokee County and the Woodstock corridor are growing fast, and the agencies appearing in the top three Google map pack results for 'car insurance Woodstock GA' almost certainly carry review counts that are two to four times higher. Google's local ranking algorithm weighs review volume and recency as direct signals of business activity and trustworthiness, and a profile with 31 reviews and the most recent review Google surfaces being 309 days old reads as dormant by comparison. Every map pack position this agency does not hold is a position a competitor does.

findings.title: No Local Business schema means Google is guessing at the agency's core details
findings.detail: Schema markup is how websites formally communicate structured facts: name, address, phone number, service area, business type, and hours directly to search engines in a format they can act on with confidence. Without it, Google is inferring those details from unstructured text, which reduces the strength of local signals and lowers the probability of appearing in rich results and knowledge panels. findings.title: The physical address does not appear anywhere on the site, which hurts local trust and rankings

For a local business, a visible NAP (name, address, phone) is both a ranking signal for local SEO and a basic trust signal for the visitor: insurance buyers want to know they are dealing with a real, findable business in their community before they hand over personal information for a quote. The absence of the address on the site also creates an inconsistency between the site and the Google Business Profile that search engines penalize in local ranking calculations.

findings.title: Two photos on the Google Business Profile is well below the threshold for a competitive local profile
findings.detail: Google's own data shows that business profiles with more than 100 photos receive significantly more direction requests and website clicks than those with fewer than 10. With only 2 photos, the profile looks sparse and unverified to a prospective customer browsing the map pack, and it signals low engagement to Google's ranking algorithm. For an insurance agency, photos of the office exterior, the team, and community involvement are direct credibility builders that cost nothing to add.

findings.title: No live chat or online scheduling creates friction for the growing segment of buyers who will not call first
findings.detail: A meaningful and growing portion of insurance shoppers, particularly younger buyers, will not make a phone call as their first step: they want to start a conversation on their own terms and their own schedule. With no live chat and no online booking option, the site forces every visitor into a phone call or a form submission with no acknowledgment of when they will hear back, and a meaningful share of those visitors will choose a competitor who offers a lower-commitment entry point. The tracking infrastructure is already in place to measure this, which makes the absence of these tools a strategic gap rather than a technical one.

audit_report.summary: Woodstock Car Insurance has a real foundation to build on: a perfect rating, the right ad tracking in place, and enough site content to compete. findings.title: No AI model knows Locklin Capital exists, and that gap is widening every month

categories.name: Tracking & Data

audit_report.headline: Where Envoy Mortgage Ltd. is quietly losing customers before they ever make contact
audit_report.overallVerdict: Envoy Mortgage Ltd. has real strengths in reputation and technical fundamentals, but a critically slow mobile site, a dormant Google Business Profile, zero AI recognition, and thin conversion infrastructure are collectively costing them mortgage leads every single week.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: Google's PageSpeed audit scores the mobile site at 50/100, with a Largest Contentful Paint of 7.1 seconds, nearly three times the 2.5-second threshold Google considers acceptable, and a Total Blocking Time of 500ms that makes the page feel unresponsive on phones. The site does pass on HTTPS, mobile viewport, and layout stability (CLS 0.031), but the mixed-content flag is a real security warning that browsers surface to visitors, and the LCP alone is severe enough to push prospects to a competitor before the page finishes loading.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: On-page fundamentals are solid: the title tag is properly sized at 42 characters, a meta description is present at 127 characters, there is a single clean H1, canonical tags are set, local business schema is implemented, and the site carries 6,211 words of indexable content. The one structural gap is that the page title reads 'Find Your Branch Location, Envoy Mortgage' rather than leading with a locally targeted value proposition, which is a missed opportunity to capture searchers using intent-driven queries like 'mortgage lender Woodstock GA'.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: The site does have a phone number, a lead form, and a call to action present across all scanned pages, which provides a baseline conversion path. However, there is no online scheduling tool, no live chat, and no email or newsletter capture, meaning the only moment a visitor can act is in real time, and anyone who arrives outside business hours or who is not yet ready to call has no friction-free way to raise their hand and stay in the funnel.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: The Google Business Profile is operational with a strong 4.8-star rating across 58 reviews, hours and phone are listed, and the website is linked, all above average for a local mortgage lender. The concern is recency: the most recent review Google shows us is 407 days old, which signals to both Google's algorithm and to prospective borrowers that the business may be less active than it actually is, and only 8 photos are on the profile, which is thin for a financial services business trying to build trust at a glance. Whether the business description is filled in was not measurable on this run, but it is worth verifying directly in Google Business Profile Manager, as a missing description is a common gap at this profile level.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Tag Manager, the Meta pixel, and a Google Ads conversion tag are all confirmed present, which means the infrastructure for paid retargeting and conversion attribution is in place and is more mature than most local mortgage offices at this size. The remaining risk is that without confirming what events are actually firing inside GTM, such as form submissions, phone call clicks, and scroll depth, the tags may be collecting sessions without capturing the loan-inquiry conversions that justify ad spend.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: Envoy Mortgage links to Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and LinkedIn from the site, and video content is present, which is a better starting position than most local competitors. TikTok is absent, which matters because short-form video is now a primary discovery channel for first-time homebuyers in the 25-40 demographic, the exact borrower profile that drives purchase mortgage volume in a market like Woodstock. The broader opportunity is profile optimization across the existing four platforms: consistent branding, complete bios with a clear local value proposition, and a reliable posting cadence around rate content, buyer tips, and local market commentary would meaningfully increase reach without requiring any paid spend.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers are open, structured data is implemented, and the site has enough content depth for AI to summarize, those are the right foundations. The critical failure is that when AI models are asked about mortgage lenders in Woodstock, GA, they do not recognize Envoy Mortgage Ltd. as a distinct local business, and they would not currently recommend it. This gap is compounded by missing sameAs entity links that would connect the website to the business's social profiles and directory listings for AI to cross-reference, no FAQ schema for AI to quote directly, and no llms.txt guidance file. As more buyers begin their mortgage search by asking an AI assistant for recommendations rather than running a Google search, being unknown to those models is the fastest-growing blind spot in local mortgage marketing right now.

findings.title: A 7.1-second page load is sending mobile borrowers to competitors
findings.detail: The mobile LCP of 7.1 seconds is nearly three times Google's acceptable threshold, and Google's own data shows that 53% of mobile users abandon a page that takes longer than 3 seconds to load. For a mortgage lender where a single closed loan is worth thousands in revenue, even a handful of bounced visitors per week compounds into a material lead loss over a quarter. This is not a cosmetic issue, it is the first thing a prospect experiences, and right now that experience is failing more than half of them.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know Envoy Mortgage exists
findings.detail: A live probe of AI models found zero recognition of Envoy Mortgage Ltd. in Woodstock, GA as a distinct local business, meaning the office is completely invisible in what is rapidly becoming a primary discovery channel for borrowers. Missing sameAs entity links, no FAQ schema, and no llms.txt file mean there is nothing connecting the website to the rest of the business's digital footprint in a way AI can parse and trust. Competitors who establish AI recognition now will accumulate a compounding advantage as AI-assisted search continues to grow.

findings.title: No scheduling tool means after-hours visitors leave without a next step
findings.detail: The site has a form and a phone number, but no online booking or scheduling capability, which means any prospect who arrives on a weeknight or weekend, when mortgage research actually peaks, has no low-friction way to claim a time with a loan officer. In a purchase market driven by urgency, a borrower who cannot immediately schedule will move to a lender who makes it easy. This is a direct, measurable conversion gap on a site that already has Google Ads and Meta pixels running, meaning paid traffic is flowing to a destination that does not capture it efficiently.

findings.title: The most recent Google review visible is 407 days old
findings.detail: The most recent review Google shows is 407 days old, which matters both algorithmically and psychologically: Google's local ranking system rewards review velocity, and a prospect comparing two 4.8-star lenders will gravitate toward the one that shows recent client activity. A mortgage lender closing loans every month should have a steady stream of fresh reviews, and the gap between actual loan volume and visible review recency suggests there is no systematic process in place to request them at close.

findings.title: Mixed content warning is an active trust signal to browsers and visitors
findings.detail: The site loads over HTTPS but the mixed-content flag indicates that some resources, images, scripts, or other assets, are still being called over HTTP. Modern browsers display security warnings or silently block these resources, which can break page elements and, more damaging for a financial services business, visibly undermine the security credibility that borrowers need to feel before submitting personal and financial information.

findings.title: No live chat or email capture means the middle of the funnel leaks
findings.detail: A borrower researching mortgage options may visit the site three or four times before they are ready to call. Without live chat or email capture, each of those visits produces no lead data and no way to re-engage. The Meta pixel and Google Ads tag are in place for retargeting, but retargeting alone requires the prospect to return on their own initiative, an email sequence or a chat interaction would actively pull them back and position Envoy as the lender they already have a relationship with.

findings.title: Only 8 photos on the Google Business Profile for a trust-dependent financial service
findings.detail: Eight photos is below the threshold where a Google Business Profile starts to perform competitively in local search and map pack results. For a mortgage lender, photos of the team, the office, and community involvement serve as credibility signals for borrowers who are making one of the largest financial decisions of their lives with someone they have never met. Google's own data indicates that profiles with more photos receive significantly more direction requests and website clicks than those with minimal visual content.

quickWins: Implement an online scheduling link (Calendly or equivalent) on every page and inside the Google Business Profile's booking button field, this captures after-hours intent immediately.
Launch a post-close review request process: a simple text or email sent to borrowers at closing asking for a Google review would directly address the review recency gap within weeks.
Add sameAs schema markup connecting the website to Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, and any directory profiles, this is the single fastest step toward AI recognition and entity disambiguation.
Audit and resolve the mixed-content HTTP resources flagged in the PageSpeed report, this removes a browser-level security warning and is typically a same-day fix for a developer.
audit_report.summary: Envoy Mortgage Ltd. has a genuine reputation asset in that 4.8-star rating and the tracking infrastructure to run effective paid campaigns, but the site's mobile performance, conversion gaps, and complete absence from AI-assisted search are actively suppressing the lead volume those assets should be generating. The gaps identified here are specific, addressable, and directly tied to borrower behavior, which is exactly what OHM's growth audit process is built to turn into a prioritized action plan. A 30-minute discovery call is the logical next step to walk through which of these gaps is costing the most right now and what a realistic 90-day improvement looks like.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the mobile speed, scheduling, review velocity, and AI visibility gaps identified here represents a realistic opportunity to increase qualified mortgage inquiry volume by 25 to 40 percent from existing traffic and local search, before any increase in ad spend.

audit_report.overallVerdict: A genuinely strong local reputation built on 224 five-star reviews is being undermined by a slow mobile site with no lead capture form, no clear call to action, and near-total invisibility to AI assistants that are fast becoming the first stop for mortgage shoppers.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site is secure, mobile-responsive, and free of mixed content, which covers the basics, but a mobile PageSpeed score of 51/100 and a Largest Contentful Paint of 5.5 seconds are well outside Google's recommended 2.5-second threshold, meaning a significant portion of mobile visitors abandon the page before they ever read a word. Layout shift is acceptable at 0.071 and Total Blocking Time of 450ms adds further friction, making the overall experience noticeably sluggish on the devices most mortgage shoppers are using.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: Live chat is present and a phone number is listed, but across every page scanned, including the contact page, there is no lead capture form, no online scheduling, and no clear call to action, which means a visitor who is not ready to pick up the phone has no frictionless next step and simply leaves. For a mortgage broker where the average closed loan represents thousands of dollars in commission, even a modest improvement in on-site conversion rate would have an outsized revenue impact.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: The Google Business Profile is a genuine asset: a 5.0 rating across 224 reviews is exceptional for a mortgage broker in Woodstock, hours and phone are listed, the website is linked, and 10 photos are on the profile. Whether the business description field is populated could not be confirmed in this scan and should be checked directly in Google Business Manager, since a missing or thin description is a commonly overlooked ranking factor.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Tag Manager and a Google Ads conversion tag are both installed, which means paid search campaigns have at least a foundation for conversion tracking. However, the Facebook pixel is entirely absent, making it impossible to build retargeting audiences from site visitors or to run cost-efficient Meta campaigns that follow warm prospects who visited the site but did not call, a gap that is particularly costly for a high-consideration purchase like a mortgage where most buyers research for weeks before committing.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: No social profiles are linked from the site and none were detected across the scan, meaning there is no Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, or TikTok presence connected to the business at all, which is a significant missed channel for a mortgage broker category where educational short-form video on topics like rate comparisons, first-time buyer tips, and refinance timing drives both trust and referral traffic. The site does include video, which shows an understanding of the format's value, but without distribution channels, that content reaches only people who already found the site. Optimized social profiles with consistent branding, a clear link in bio pointing to a lead form, and a regular posting cadence would open an organic audience-building channel that costs nothing beyond time.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers are permitted access to the site, which is the necessary starting point, but every other AI readiness signal is missing: there is no structured data, no sameAs entity links connecting the business across the web, no FAQ schema for AI to quote, and no llms.txt guidance file. Most critically, when AI models were probed for knowledge of Capital Mortgage Solutions in Woodstock, GA, the business was entirely unrecognized, meaning that when a prospective buyer asks an AI assistant to recommend a mortgage broker in Woodstock, this business does not appear in the answer at all. This is the single fastest-growing visibility gap in local search: AI-driven recommendations are already influencing high-value purchase decisions, and being unknown to those models today means ceding ground to competitors who move first.

findings.title: No lead capture form anywhere on the site, including the contact page
findings.detail: Across all pages scanned, including /contact/, there is no form for a visitor to submit their name, loan interest, or contact details, meaning any prospect who arrives outside business hours or who is not yet ready to call has no way to raise their hand. For a mortgage broker where a single closed loan can generate $3,000 to $10,000 or more in commission, even capturing two additional leads per month through a simple form would produce meaningful annual revenue.

findings.title: Mobile site takes 5.5 seconds to load its main content, losing visitors before they see the value
findings.detail: A Largest Contentful Paint of 5.5 seconds is more than double Google's passing threshold of 2.5 seconds, and Google's own data shows that mobile bounce rates increase by roughly 32% as page load time goes from 1 to 3 seconds, with far steeper drop-off beyond that. Given that the Google Ads tag is active, meaning paid traffic is already being driven to this site, every second of excess load time is converting ad spend into exits rather than inquiries.

findings.title: AI assistants do not recognize the business, making it invisible in the fastest-growing referral channel
findings.detail: A direct probe confirmed that AI models have no knowledge of Capital Mortgage Solutions in Woodstock, GA, and would not recommend it in a category search, despite the business having no crawl blocks in place. The absence of structured data, sameAs entity links, and FAQ content means AI systems have no reliable signal to associate this business with its service category and location, and that gap will compound as more buyers begin their mortgage search by asking an AI rather than typing into a search bar.

findings.title: No social media presence connected to the business, eliminating an entire organic acquisition channel
findings.detail: No Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, or TikTok profiles are linked from the site or detected in the scan, which means there is no channel for distributing the educational content that builds trust with first-time buyers and refinance candidates before they are ready to call. Mortgage brokers who post consistently on short-form video platforms report that rate update videos, buyer FAQ content, and local market commentary generate inbound inquiries from audiences who would never have found them through search alone.

findings.title: No call to action exists anywhere across the scanned pages
findings.detail: The site has content, a phone number, and live chat, but no button, banner, or prompt directing visitors toward a specific next step anywhere on the site. Without a clear CTA, conversion is entirely dependent on the visitor's own initiative, which behavioral research consistently shows reduces the rate at which even interested visitors make contact.

findings.title: Facebook pixel is missing, preventing retargeting of warm prospects who did not convert
findings.detail: Mortgage shoppers rarely contact a broker on their first visit: they compare options over days or weeks, which makes retargeting one of the highest-ROI tools available. Without the Meta pixel, there is no way to serve follow-up ads to the people who already visited the site and showed intent, and no ability to build lookalike audiences from past visitors to reduce the cost of acquiring new ones through Meta platforms.

findings.title: LocalBusiness schema markup is absent, reducing eligibility for rich local search results
findings.detail: The site has no structured data of any kind, which means search engines and AI systems must infer the business name, category, service area, and contact details from unstructured text rather than reading it from clean machine-readable markup. This reduces the likelihood of appearing in rich result formats in Google Search and is a direct contributing factor to the business being unrecognized by AI models.

quickWins: Add a simple contact and pre-qualification interest form to the homepage and /contact/ page so visitors outside business hours have a way to express interest without calling
Install the Meta pixel immediately so the existing site traffic starts building retargeting audiences even before any Meta campaigns are launched
Add LocalBusiness schema markup with name, address, phone, hours, and service area to close the structured data gap for both Google and AI systems
Create and link a Facebook or Instagram business profile and post the video already on the site as a first piece of content, establishing a distribution channel at zero incremental production cost
audit_report.summary: Capital Mortgage Solutions has a rare and genuinely strong foundation in its 5-star reputation and Google Business Profile, but the site is currently structured to inform visitors rather than capture them, and the business is invisible in AI search, social, and retargeting channels that competitors will move into quickly. Open Heart Media has already identified seven specific, data-backed gaps in this audit: closing them is a systematic process, and the sequence in which they are addressed determines how fast the revenue impact compounds.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the conversion, speed, AI visibility, and retargeting gaps identified here could reasonably double the rate at which existing site traffic turns into booked conversations, and adding social distribution opens a second acquisition channel entirely, representing a realistic path to 15 to 30 additional qualified leads per month depending on current traffic volume.

audit_report.headline: Where Sierra Construction and Remodeling is quietly losing customers to contractors with a weaker product but a stronger digital footprint
audit_report.overallVerdict: Sierra has a clean, reachable site and a perfect Google rating, but a slow mobile experience, near-zero tracking, no AI recognition, and a thin review base are collectively routing ready-to-hire homeowners in Woodstock straight to competitors who show up first and look more established.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site is secure, mobile-responsive, and layout-stable (CLS 0.034), which are solid foundations, but the Largest Contentful Paint of 8.1 seconds is more than three times Google's 2.5-second threshold and directly causes visitors to abandon the page before it finishes loading. A mobile PageSpeed score of 71 is passable but leaves meaningful performance on the table, and with no analytics installed there is no way to measure how many people are already leaving because of it.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The page title is present and correctly sized, there is a single clean H1, and the site has enough word count to index, but the meta description is entirely missing site-wide, which means Google writes its own snippet for every page and that snippet is rarely compelling enough to earn the click. Local business schema markup is also absent, so Google cannot confidently associate the site with a specific service area or category, which weakens rankings for the high-intent 'general contractor Woodstock GA' searches that drive real jobs.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: A click-to-call number, a lead form, and a CTA are present, which covers the basics, but there is no online scheduling, no live chat, and no email capture anywhere across the four scanned pages. For a general contractor where most jobs are four-to-six figure decisions, visitors who are not ready to call immediately have no low-friction next step, and without retargeting pixels there is no way to bring those hesitant visitors back after they leave.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: Sierra carries a perfect 5-star rating and a review as recent as 24 days ago, both of which are genuine strengths, but 11 total reviews is significantly below the 50-plus count that established general contractors in the Woodstock and Cherokee County market typically show, and a thin review count causes Google to rank the profile lower regardless of star quality. Hours and a website are linked on the profile, and photos meet the 10-image threshold, but the absence of local business schema on the site and no NAP address visible anywhere on the site pages weakens the local trust signals Google uses to rank contractors in the map pack. Whether the Google Business Profile description is filled in was not measurable on this run and should be verified directly.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: No analytics platform, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads conversion tag are installed anywhere on the site, meaning Sierra is running its entire digital presence completely blind. Every dollar that could go toward paid ads, every page that gets traffic, and every form submission that comes in cannot be attributed, optimized, or scaled because there is no data infrastructure in place to measure any of it.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: No social profiles of any kind are linked from the site, and the scan detected no active presence on Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, or TikTok, which are the four platforms where homeowners in the Atlanta suburbs research and vet contractors before making contact. Sierra does have video on its website, which is a real asset and a stronger signal than most local contractors bother with, but that content is siloed to the site rather than distributed to platforms where it would compound over time. For a general contractor, before-and-after project content on Instagram and short-form video on TikTok or YouTube Shorts are among the highest-ROI ways to build the local trust that turns a browsing homeowner into a booked job, and right now that entire channel is unused.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers are allowed and an llms.txt file exists, which puts Sierra ahead of many small contractors on the technical access side, but structured data and sameAs entity links are both absent, meaning AI models cannot reliably parse who Sierra is, what they do, or where they serve. When AI assistants were queried about Sierra Construction and Remodeling in Woodstock, GA, the business was not recognized at all, and AI models would not recommend them in the general contractor category, making them completely invisible in the channel where a growing share of homeowners are now starting their contractor search. This is the single biggest emerging visibility gap in the audit: as buyers increasingly ask AI for recommendations, a business that AI has never heard of loses those inquiries entirely, and that gap will only widen as AI-driven search continues to grow.

findings.title: 8.1-second load time is sending mobile visitors straight to a competitor
findings.detail: Google's threshold for a good mobile experience is 2.5 seconds for the Largest Contentful Paint. Sierra's site takes 8.1 seconds, which is more than three times that benchmark. Research consistently shows that conversion rates drop by roughly 20 percent for every additional second of load time on mobile, and most homeowners searching for a contractor are doing it from a phone while standing in a damaged kitchen or a flooded bathroom.

findings.title: 11 reviews is the number that keeps Sierra off the short list
findings.detail: In a market like Woodstock and Cherokee County where established general contractors show 50 to 200-plus Google reviews, Sierra's 11 reviews cause Google's algorithm to rank the profile lower in the local map pack regardless of the perfect star rating. A homeowner comparing two contractors on Google will almost always choose the one with more social proof, meaning Sierra is losing jobs to contractors who may do inferior work but have a more convincing review presence.

findings.title: Zero tracking means zero ability to grow intentionally
findings.detail: With no Google Analytics, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads tag installed, Sierra cannot identify which pages or traffic sources produce inquiries, cannot retarget visitors who left without calling, and cannot run any paid advertising with conversion measurement in place. This is not just a data problem: it means any marketing investment made today, paid or organic, cannot be attributed or optimized, so every dollar spent is a guess.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know Sierra exists
findings.detail: A live probe of what AI models know about Sierra Construction and Remodeling in Woodstock returned no recognition and no willingness to recommend the business. As homeowners increasingly ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews to recommend a contractor, Sierra is absent from every one of those conversations while competitors with better-structured web presences are being named.

findings.title: No meta description means Google writes the pitch for you, and it rarely converts
findings.detail: The meta description is missing across all four scanned pages, which means every time Sierra appears in Google search results, Google auto-generates a snippet by pulling random text from the page. Auto-generated snippets rarely include a service area, a value proposition, or a call to action, so Sierra's click-through rate from search is almost certainly lower than it should be for a business with a strong rating. This is a direct loss of traffic that the site has already earned the ranking for.

findings.title: No social presence means no compounding trust with Woodstock homeowners

Sierra has no linked profiles on any platform, which means that trust-building channel is completely unused and any homeowner who searches for Sierra on social media after finding them on Google will find nothing, which can be enough to send them to a competitor who at least looks active.

findings.title: No address on the site weakens local search credibility

The address is absent site-wide across all four scanned pages, which creates a mismatch between the on-site signals and the Google Business Profile and reduces Google's confidence in associating Sierra with a specific service area. Add the full business address to the site footer on every page to create consistent NAP signals that reinforce local search ranking.
Ask the last 20 satisfied clients directly for a Google review with a one-tap link: getting from 11 to 30-plus reviews in the next 60 days is achievable and will visibly improve map pack placement.
audit_report.summary: Sierra has genuine competitive strengths: a perfect rating, recent reviews, video on the site, and a clean technical foundation, but the gaps identified in this audit are actively redirecting homeowners who are ready to hire toward contractors who simply show up better online. Open Heart Media has already mapped exactly where the revenue is leaking and what it would take to close those gaps in a way that compounds over time rather than requiring constant ad spend to maintain. The logical next step is a conversation about which of these gaps to close first and what a realistic 90-day trajectory looks like for a contractor at Sierra's stage.

audit_report.headline: Where 5 Stones Renovation Inc. is quietly losing customers to competitors who show up and they do not

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site earns full marks for HTTPS security, mobile responsiveness, and layout stability (CLS of 0), but the mobile PageSpeed score of 61/100 and a Largest Contentful Paint of 7.4 seconds are a serious problem. Google's threshold for a good LCP is 2.5 seconds, meaning the main content on a phone takes nearly three times longer to appear than it should, and on mobile is exactly where most homeowners searching for a kitchen remodeler will land first.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The on-page SEO fundamentals are mostly solid: local business schema is present, a canonical tag is set, there is one clear H1, the meta description is properly sized, and the site carries 6,197 words of content across scanned pages. The page title at 72 characters is slightly over Google's recommended limit and risks being truncated in search results, which reduces click-through rates on what is otherwise a well-structured page.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: The site has the core conversion tools in place: a clickable phone number, a lead capture form, an online booking option, and a clear call to action, which puts it ahead of many local contractors. However, there is no live chat anywhere on the site and no physical address displayed, both of which are meaningful trust signals for homeowners considering a five-figure kitchen renovation, and the absence of an email or newsletter capture means there is no way to nurture leads who are not ready to book today.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: A live scan of Google found no Google Business Profile for 5 Stones Renovation Inc., which is the single most disqualifying gap in the entire audit. categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Analytics 4 and a Google Ads conversion tag are both present, which means paid search campaigns can be measured for ROI. categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn are all linked from the site, giving 5 Stones a presence on the platforms most relevant to homeowners in their demographic. There is no video anywhere on the site or linked YouTube or TikTok channel, which is a significant missed opportunity for a kitchen remodeler, where before-and-after transformation content routinely generates organic reach and builds the kind of visual trust that converts a browsing homeowner into a phone call. The opportunity to optimize existing profiles with consistent branding, a clear link in bio pointing to a booking page, and a regular cadence of project posts is substantial and largely untapped based on what the scan can see.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: The technical groundwork for AI visibility is real and worth acknowledging: AI crawlers are permitted, structured data is in place, entity links connecting profiles exist, FAQ schema is present, and an llms.txt guidance file has been added, which puts 5 Stones ahead of most local contractors on setup. The critical problem is that when AI models are asked about this business by name, they return no knowledge of it whatsoever, and when asked to recommend kitchen remodelers in the area, the business does not appear. findings.title: No Google Business Profile: the Map Pack is being handed to competitors
findings.detail: A live Google Places scan found no Business Profile for 5 Stones Renovation Inc. The Google Map Pack, the three local results that appear above organic listings for searches like 'kitchen remodeler Woodstock GA', is where the majority of high-intent local clicks go, and without a profile, 5 Stones cannot appear there at all. Every homeowner who searches for kitchen remodeling in the area on Google and clicks a Map Pack result is a lead that a competitor is collecting instead.

findings.title: 7.4-second mobile load time is losing visitors before they see a single project photo
findings.detail: The Largest Contentful Paint on mobile is 7.4 seconds, nearly three times Google's recommended threshold of 2.5 seconds. Competitors who have built enough online presence to be referenced in AI training data or real-time retrieval are already receiving those referrals.

findings.title: No Meta pixel means ad retargeting is off the table entirely
findings.detail: Kitchen renovation is a considered purchase with a long decision cycle, and most homeowners visit multiple contractor websites before committing to a call. Without a Facebook or Instagram pixel, 5 Stones cannot run retargeting ads to the people who already visited their site and showed clear interest, which is typically the most cost-efficient audience in paid social. Given that Facebook and Instagram are already linked from the site, the advertising infrastructure exists but the tracking connection needed to act on it is absent.

findings.title: No video content on the site or linked video channel is a missed trust builder
findings.detail: Kitchen remodeling is an inherently visual and high-trust purchase, and video is the format that most efficiently conveys both the quality of the work and the personality of the team before a homeowner ever picks up the phone. There is no video anywhere across the nine pages scanned, and no YouTube or TikTok channel is linked from the site. For a business with 12 reviews and no Google presence to rely on, video content showing real project walkthroughs would do significant work in establishing credibility and differentiating from competitors.

findings.title: No address displayed on the site reduces local trust
findings.detail: The site has a phone number, form, and booking option, but no physical address is shown anywhere across the scanned pages including the contact page. audit_report.headline: Where Shedd's Construction is quietly losing customers before they ever make contact
audit_report.overallVerdict: Shedd's Construction has a genuinely strong foundation in ratings and site structure, but a cluster of conversion, tracking, and AI visibility gaps means a meaningful share of ready-to-hire prospects are slipping away undetected every month.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site earns a solid 84/100 on Google PageSpeed for mobile, with a perfectly stable layout (CLS of 0) and zero thread-blocking time, which is better than most local contractors. The one real drag is a Largest Contentful Paint of 3.6 seconds, above Google's 2.5-second threshold, meaning the main content loads too slowly for roughly half of mobile visitors and signals a sub-par experience to Google's ranking algorithm.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: Core on-page SEO is genuinely well handled: the 59-character title tag, 96-character meta description, local business schema, canonical tag, and 2,596 words of content all pass cleanly, which is ahead of most local construction sites. The one structural error is two H1 tags appearing on the site rather than one, which dilutes the primary keyword signal Google uses to categorize the page and can suppress rankings for the exact searches Shedd's most needs to win.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: The site has a form, an online booking option, and a visible CTA, which gives it more conversion infrastructure than most local competitors. However, there is no clickable phone number anywhere across the homepage, about page, or contact page, which is a critical failure: mobile visitors who want to call immediately hit a dead end, and in construction, phone-ready buyers are often the highest-intent leads in the pipeline. Live chat and email capture are also absent, removing two additional contact pathways that keep fence-sitting prospects engaged rather than sending them to a competitor.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: The Google Business Profile is genuinely strong: a 4.9-star rating across 103 reviews puts Shedd's well above the typical Woodstock contractor, and hours, website, and phone are all correctly listed. The profile has 10 or more photos, which clears the minimum threshold. The most recent review Google shows is 93 days old, and whether the profile description is filled in was not measurable on this run and should be verified directly in the dashboard, as a missing or thin description leaves a content gap that competitors with complete profiles can exploit.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Website analytics, a Meta pixel, and a Google Ads conversion tag are all absent, meaning Shedd's is operating its entire digital presence completely blind: there is no record of how many visitors come, which pages they view, where they drop off, or which sources drive contact form submissions. Without this data, any future ad spend on Google or Meta cannot be optimized, attributed, or even measured for return on investment, making it impossible to scale what works or cut what does not.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: Only Facebook is linked from the site, and Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok are entirely absent, which is a significant gap for a construction company where before-and-after project photography and walkthrough video are among the highest-performing content formats available. There is no video anywhere on the site, and 17 of 45 images are missing alt text, which weakens both accessibility compliance and image search visibility. The opportunity to build a consistent cross-platform presence with complete bios, a unified brand identity, and short-form project video content is wide open and would directly support the goal of reaching more homeowners and builders in the Woodstock and greater Atlanta market.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: The technical groundwork for AI visibility is partially in place: AI crawlers are allowed, structured data exists, entity links connect the site to its profiles, content depth is sufficient, and an llms.txt file is present, all of which are meaningful advantages over most local contractors. However, when AI models are asked about Shedd's Construction in Woodstock, GA, they return no recognition whatsoever, and they would not recommend the business in a category search, which is the part that actually matters to someone asking an AI assistant for a contractor recommendation. FAQ schema is also missing, removing the quotable, question-and-answer content that AI assistants most readily surface when recommending a specific business to a user: as more buyers start their contractor search by asking ChatGPT or Perplexity rather than typing into Google, being invisible to those models is an emerging revenue gap that will compound each month it goes unaddressed.

findings.title: No clickable phone number anywhere on the site
findings.detail: Across every page scanned, including the contact page, there is no tap-to-call phone link present. In the construction category, research consistently shows that inbound phone calls convert to booked jobs at a significantly higher rate than form submissions, because callers are typically decision-ready. Every mobile visitor who wants to call immediately is hitting a wall and likely hitting the back button to find a competitor who makes it easy.

findings.title: Zero tracking installed: the business is flying completely blind
findings.detail: There is no analytics platform, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads conversion tag on the site. This means Shedd's has no idea how many people visit each week, which traffic sources send the most visitors, or whether any of those visitors fill out the contact form. Without this baseline, any future investment in paid advertising or SEO cannot be measured, and there is no way to identify which parts of the funnel are losing the most potential customers.

findings.title: AI assistants have never heard of Shedd's Construction
findings.detail: A direct probe of AI model knowledge returned zero recognition of Shedd's Construction in Woodstock, GA, and AI models would not recommend the business in a contractor category search. Homeowners increasingly open ChatGPT or Perplexity and ask for contractor recommendations before they ever open Google, and a business that does not exist in that layer of the search ecosystem gets no consideration. The technical infrastructure to be found is partially in place, but the content signals that cause AI to cite a specific business by name are missing.

findings.title: LCP of 3.6 seconds is failing Google's Core Web Vitals threshold
findings.detail: Google's threshold for a passing Largest Contentful Paint score is 2.5 seconds, and the site is loading its primary visible content in 3.6 seconds on mobile. This directly factors into Google's page experience ranking signal, meaning Shedd's is conceding ranking positions to technically faster competitors on the exact mobile searches that drive the most construction inquiries in the Woodstock and Atlanta metro area.

findings.title: Duplicate H1 tags are diluting the site's primary keyword signal
findings.detail: Two H1 headline tags were found across the scanned pages rather than the single H1 that Google's crawlers expect. The H1 is the strongest on-page signal telling Google what a page is primarily about, and splitting it across two instances weakens the authority of both. For a contractor competing for high-value searches like 'construction company Woodstock GA' or 'Atlanta remodeling contractor', this is a structural disadvantage that a single code fix could close.

findings.title: No video content on the site or linked video platforms
findings.detail: The site has 45 images but zero video, and neither YouTube nor TikTok are linked from the site or mentioned in the social profile inventory. For a construction business, project walkthrough videos, transformation reveals, and client testimonial clips are among the most effective trust-building formats available and are the content type most likely to keep a prospect on the page long enough to submit a form. The absence of video also means the business is invisible on the two largest video discovery platforms used by homeowners researching contractors.

findings.title: 17 of 45 images are missing alt text, hurting both SEO and accessibility
findings.detail: Just over a third of the site's images have no descriptive alt text, which means Google's image search index cannot categorize those photos and screen reader users cannot access that visual content. For a construction company whose strongest proof of quality is project photography, missing alt text on nearly half the image library represents forfeited image search traffic and a compliance gap that would fail a basic accessibility review.

quickWins: Add a tap-to-call phone number link in the site header and on the contact page so mobile visitors can reach Shedd's in one tap
Install Google Analytics 4 immediately so the business has baseline traffic and conversion data before spending a dollar on ads
Consolidate the two H1 tags across the site down to one per page to restore the primary keyword signal Google uses for ranking
Add FAQ schema markup to the site covering common contractor questions so AI assistants have structured, quotable content to cite when recommending a construction company in Woodstock
audit_report.summary: Shedd's Construction has the ingredients that most local contractors never build: a near-perfect rating, triple-digit reviews, a structured site, and working booking infrastructure. The gaps identified here are not about starting from scratch but about closing the specific conversion and visibility holes that are silently redirecting ready-to-hire customers to competitors. Open Heart Media can prioritize and close these gaps in a sequenced way that ties every change to measurable lead volume, and the discovery call is the right place to map out which gaps are costing the most right now.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the phone, tracking, AI visibility, and speed gaps identified here could realistically increase qualified monthly leads by 20 to 40 percent based on industry conversion benchmarks for a construction company with Shedd's existing rating and traffic infrastructure.
