audit_report.headline: Where Davinci Supreme Remodeling is quietly losing customers before they ever make contact
audit_report.overallVerdict: Davinci Supreme Remodeling has a functional online footprint but is missing nearly every mechanism that turns website visitors and Google searchers into booked kitchen remodeling jobs, and the gaps compound each other in ways that cost real revenue every week.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site is secure over HTTPS and loads correctly on mobile, which are both baseline requirements met, but Google's own performance scoring puts the mobile experience at 60/100, and the Largest Contentful Paint of 5.3 seconds is more than double Google's 2.5-second threshold, meaning most mobile visitors are staring at a partially loaded page for over five seconds before they see the main content. There is also mixed content flagged on the site, where some resources load over an insecure HTTP connection despite the HTTPS certificate, which undermines trust signals and can trigger browser warnings.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The page title, meta description, canonical tag, and local business schema are all correctly in place, and the site clears the minimum word-count threshold at 616 words, which gives Google enough text to index and rank pages against kitchen remodeling queries in Woodstock. The one structural issue hurting search clarity is three H1 tags appearing on the site rather than one: search engines use the H1 to understand the primary topic of a page, and multiple H1s dilute that signal and can cause Google to rank the page for the wrong intent.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: This is the most damaging section in the entire audit: the site has a call to action present, and that is the only conversion mechanism in place across the homepage, services page, and contact page. There is no clickable phone number, no lead capture form, no online scheduling, no live chat, and no address listed anywhere on the site, which means a visitor who is ready to hire a kitchen remodeler right now has no fast, frictionless path to actually reach the business.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: The Google Business Profile is live, operational, and has hours and a website linked, which is a solid starting point, but the review count of 4 at a 5-star rating puts Davinci Supreme at a severe credibility disadvantage against established kitchen remodelers in the Woodstock area who typically carry 40 to 150-plus reviews. The most recent review was posted 205 days ago, which is over six months of silence on the profile, a pattern Google's local ranking algorithm treats as a signal of reduced activity. The profile also has only 4 photos uploaded, which is far below the 25 to 50 photo standard that competitive local service businesses maintain, and the business is categorized as a general contractor rather than a kitchen remodeler, which likely costs it ranking positions on the most valuable local searches.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: No analytics platform, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads conversion tag are installed anywhere on the site, which means there is currently zero visibility into how many people visit, where they come from, what pages they read, or whether any action they take results in a lead. Without this data, any money spent on paid advertising would have no conversion measurement, making it impossible to know which campaigns are producing customers and which are wasting budget.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: Facebook and Instagram are both linked from the site, which shows an intent to maintain a social presence, but there is no video content anywhere on the site or linked from it, which is a significant missed opportunity for a kitchen remodeler where before-and-after footage and project walkthroughs are among the highest-performing content formats on both platforms. There is no TikTok or YouTube presence detected, both of which are increasingly where homeowners discover contractors before they search Google. The opportunity here is specific to kitchen remodeling: profile optimization with consistent branding, a direct booking link in bio, and even a modest cadence of short project videos would differentiate the business visually in a category where most competitors show finished photos but almost none show the process.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers including GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot are all allowed to access the site, and structured data is in place, both of which are correct foundational steps. However, when AI models are asked about kitchen remodelers in Woodstock, GA, Davinci Supreme is not recognized and would not be recommended, which is the outcome that matters most to the business. The missing pieces driving that outcome are: no sameAs entity links connecting the website to the Google Business Profile, Yelp, or social profiles so AI can confirm the business is a single coherent entity; no FAQ schema content that AI can quote as an authoritative answer to homeowner questions; and no llms.txt guidance file to instruct AI models on how to represent the business. As AI-assisted search becomes the first place homeowners ask for contractor recommendations, being invisible to those models is an emerging gap that compounds with every month the profile goes unaddressed.

findings.title: The contact page collects nothing and the phone number is not clickable
findings.detail: Across all three scanned pages, including the dedicated contact page, there is no functional lead capture form and no click-to-call phone number. A homeowner on a mobile device who wants to book a kitchen remodel estimate has no one-tap way to reach the business and no form to submit their information, which means the most motivated visitors, the ones who have already navigated to the contact page, are hitting a dead end. For a kitchen remodel business where a single job can be worth $20,000 to $80,000, losing even two or three ready-to-buy visitors per month to this friction represents a significant and entirely preventable revenue gap.

findings.title: Four reviews and six months of silence on Google is costing local ranking positions
findings.detail: In the Woodstock, GA market, a kitchen remodeler with 4 reviews and the most recent posted 205 days ago will consistently rank below competitors who have 50-plus reviews and a steady flow of recent feedback, because Google's local ranking algorithm weights both volume and recency of reviews heavily for service businesses. A homeowner searching 'kitchen remodeler near me' or 'kitchen remodeling Woodstock GA' is highly unlikely to choose a business with 4 reviews over one with 80 reviews and a review from last week, regardless of star rating. Getting more customers depends directly on this number improving, because the profile's current state is actively suppressing the business's position in the Local Pack results that drive the majority of high-intent local searches.

findings.title: The business is categorized as a general contractor, not a kitchen remodeler
findings.detail: The Google Business Profile primary category is set to 'general contractor' rather than 'kitchen remodeler' or 'kitchen & bath remodeler', which directly affects which searches the profile appears in and how prominently it ranks for the queries most likely to produce booked jobs. Google uses the primary category as one of the strongest signals for local search matching, and a business categorized as a general contractor competes in a broader and more crowded pool while potentially missing high-intent category-specific searches entirely. This is a configuration issue on the profile that has a direct effect on how many people ever see the business listed.

findings.title: No tracking means no way to measure what is working or justify ad spend
findings.detail: With no Google Analytics, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads tag installed, the business is operating without any data on website traffic, visitor behavior, or lead source attribution. This means that if any paid advertising were started today, there would be no way to know which campaigns, keywords, or ad placements produced an actual inquiry versus which ones burned budget. Beyond paid ads, the absence of analytics also means there is no visibility into whether the SEO improvements or Google Business Profile changes are driving more traffic over time.

findings.title: AI assistants cannot identify or recommend the business, and that gap is growing
findings.detail: A tested probe of AI models found that Davinci Supreme Remodeling is not recognized by name and would not be recommended to a homeowner asking for kitchen remodelers in Woodstock, GA. The specific technical gaps causing this are the absence of sameAs entity links in the structured data, no FAQ schema content for AI to cite, and no llms.txt file. As a growing share of homeowners, particularly higher-income homeowners more likely to spend on full kitchen remodels, begin using AI assistants as their first research step before opening a browser, invisibility in that channel becomes a real and compounding customer acquisition gap.

findings.title: The site's main image loads in 5.3 seconds on mobile, and most visitors leave before it does
findings.detail: Google's data consistently shows that mobile page abandonment rises sharply after 3 seconds of load time, and the Largest Contentful Paint of 5.3 seconds on this site means the primary visual content, likely the hero image or section that communicates what the business does, is not visible for over five seconds on a typical mobile connection. For a kitchen remodeler whose website needs to make an immediate visual impression with photos of quality work, a slow-loading page works directly against the first impression that converts a visitor into a lead. The mobile performance score of 60 out of 100 confirms this is a broad issue across multiple page elements, not just a single image.

findings.title: Only 6 of 21 images have alt text, which hurts both SEO and accessibility
findings.detail: Fifteen of the 21 images on the site are missing alt text, which means search engines cannot read what those images depict and cannot use them to reinforce the page's relevance for kitchen remodeling search queries. For a visual trade like kitchen remodeling where project photos are a primary trust signal, untagged images are also invisible to Google Image Search, which is a secondary discovery channel where homeowners actively browse before choosing a contractor. The 98 accessibility score confirms the site is otherwise well-structured, making the missing image alt text a straightforward and high-return fix.

quickWins: Add a click-to-call phone number on every page and a simple name, phone, and project-type form to the contact page so visitors have an immediate path to reach the business.
Change the Google Business Profile primary category from 'general contractor' to 'kitchen remodeler' and upload at least 20 project photos to the profile this week.
Email or text the last 15 to 20 completed clients a direct link to leave a Google review, which is the fastest way to close the review-count gap against local competitors.
Install Google Analytics 4 on the site before making any other changes so that every improvement made going forward can be measured against a baseline.
audit_report.summary: Davinci Supreme Remodeling has real quality signals, including a perfect 5-star rating and a technically sound site structure, but the business is systematically invisible at every stage where a potential customer tries to take action: the Google profile ranks poorly due to category misconfiguration and almost no reviews, the website has no way to capture or even receive a lead, and there is zero tracking to show what is and is not working. Open Heart Media has mapped the full gap between where the business is now and what it would take to compete seriously for kitchen remodeling jobs in the Woodstock market, and the conversation worth having is about closing those gaps in the right order with the right strategy.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the conversion, local visibility, and tracking gaps identified in this audit positions Davinci Supreme to realistically capture 4 to 10 additional qualified kitchen remodel inquiries per month, representing $80,000 to $500,000 or more in annual project revenue depending on close rate and average job size.

audit_report.headline: Where Art Design & Construction LLC is quietly losing customers before they ever make contact
audit_report.overallVerdict: Art Design & Construction LLC has a functional website and a perfect star rating, but a 7.3-second load time, three reviews in its entire history, zero AI recognition, and no social presence means the business is effectively invisible to the majority of kitchen remodel shoppers in Woodstock and the broader Atlanta market.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site earns credit for HTTPS, a stable layout (CLS of 0.036), and a responsive mobile viewport, but a PageSpeed score of 68 on mobile and a Largest Contentful Paint of 7.3 seconds are severe problems. Google's own threshold for a good LCP is 2.5 seconds, meaning the page takes nearly three times longer than acceptable to show its main content, and on mobile, where most remodel research begins, that cost is paid in bounced visitors who never return.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The page title runs 80 characters and the meta description runs 306 characters, both outside the ranges search engines display cleanly, and three separate H1 tags on the same page send Google a confused signal about what the page is actually about. The single most damaging gap is the complete absence of local business schema markup, which means Google cannot reliably extract the business name, service area, or category from the site to power local search features that drive kitchen remodel leads.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: The site does the basics correctly: a clickable phone number, a lead form, an online booking option, and clear calls to action are all present across the scanned pages. The gaps that cost real leads are the absence of live chat (a growing expectation for higher-ticket home services where shoppers want fast answers) and no email or newsletter capture, which means every visitor who does not convert immediately is gone forever with no way to follow up.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: A 5-star rating is genuinely strong, but only three total reviews and the most recent one arriving 234 days ago make that rating statistically invisible and untrustworthy to a prospective customer comparing multiple contractors. A typical kitchen remodeler with real local traction in a market like Woodstock has 40 to 100-plus reviews and receives new ones regularly, and Google's local ranking algorithm weighs both review volume and recency heavily. Hours, a website link, and photos are present, which prevents this score from being lower, but the review deficit alone is enough to push the business off the first page of local results against any moderately active competitor.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Analytics 4 and a Facebook Pixel are both installed, which is a real foundation, but there is no Google Ads conversion tag present, meaning any paid search campaign run today would be bidding blind with no ability to tie ad spend to actual form submissions or calls. Without conversion tracking in Google Ads, the business cannot optimize toward the leads that matter, which makes paid customer acquisition significantly more expensive and less effective than it should be.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: No Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, or TikTok profile is linked anywhere on the site, and no video content exists on any scanned page, which is a significant missed opportunity for a kitchen remodeler where before-and-after visuals are the primary driver of emotional decision-making and sharing. Kitchen renovation content on Instagram and TikTok consistently generates organic reach and referral traffic that costs nothing, and the absence of any social presence means the business is not visible in the channels where Woodstock homeowners are actively browsing and sharing remodel inspiration. The opportunity here is not just posting content, it is building optimized profiles with consistent branding, a clear link back to the booking page, and short-form video of completed projects that can do selling work around the clock.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers are correctly allowed access to the site, and an llms.txt file is in place, which shows awareness of the AI channel, but the absence of structured data and sameAs entity links means AI models have no reliable machine-readable signal to build a confident understanding of the business. When AI models were probed about Art Design and Construction LLC in Woodstock, they returned no specific knowledge of the business and would not recommend it in the kitchen remodeler category, which is the single most urgent emerging visibility gap in the scan. Buyers are increasingly asking AI assistants for contractor recommendations by location and specialty, and a business that AI has never heard of is simply not in the conversation at the moment the purchase decision is forming.

findings.title: 3 reviews in the lifetime of the business is the biggest single barrier to new customers
findings.detail: A 5-star average built on 3 reviews does not signal quality to a homeowner spending $30,000 to $80,000 on a kitchen remodel. It signals that almost nobody has used this contractor, and the last person who did was 234 days ago. Competitors with 60 or 80 reviews at 4.7 stars will consistently win the click, the call, and the job, regardless of actual work quality.

findings.title: A 7.3-second LCP means Google is already penalizing the site in rankings, and visitors are leaving before seeing the offer
findings.detail: Google's Core Web Vitals directly influence organic search rankings, and a 7.3-second Largest Contentful Paint is nearly three times the threshold for a good score. On mobile, where the majority of 'kitchen remodeler near me' searches happen, a significant portion of visitors will abandon the page before it finishes loading, representing real leads that were found but immediately lost.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know this business exists, and that gap is widening every month
findings.detail: When AI models are asked to recommend kitchen remodelers in Woodstock or the Atlanta area, Art Design and Construction LLC does not appear. There is no structured data for AI to read, no sameAs entity connections to tie the business to its Google profile or any directory listing, and no FAQ content for AI to surface in response to common homeowner questions. As AI-driven search continues to grow, businesses without AI recognition lose consideration at the earliest stage of the buying process.

findings.title: 49 of 50 images on the site are missing alt text, hurting both SEO and accessibility
findings.detail: Every image on a kitchen remodeling website is a potential ranking signal for searches like 'kitchen cabinet installation Woodstock' or 'open concept kitchen renovation Atlanta', but alt text is missing on 49 of the 50 images scanned across all service pages. Search engines cannot read images, only their text descriptions, so nearly the entire visual portfolio of the site is contributing nothing to organic discovery.

findings.title: Three H1 tags and an oversized meta description are sending mixed signals to Google on every key page
findings.detail: Multiple H1 headings on a single page tell search engines there is no single clear topic, which weakens keyword relevance signals for competitive terms like 'kitchen remodeler Woodstock GA'. The 306-character meta description is also more than double the display limit, meaning Google will rewrite it with its own text, removing the business's control over the first impression in search results.

findings.title: No social profiles means zero organic referral traffic and no visual trust channel for a visual business
findings.detail: Kitchen remodeling is among the most visually driven home services categories, and platforms like Instagram and TikTok consistently deliver organic reach for before-and-after content at no ad cost. With no linked social profiles anywhere on the site, the business is absent from the discovery channels where homeowners spend time before they ever search Google, and there is no community presence to reinforce trust when a potential customer looks the business up after a referral.

findings.title: No Google Ads conversion tag means paid advertising cannot be optimized and is likely unprofitable if run today
findings.detail: The Facebook Pixel is installed, but there is no Google Ads conversion tag, which is the primary channel for high-intent searches like 'kitchen remodeler near me' or 'kitchen renovation company Woodstock'. Running Google Ads without conversion tracking means the campaign cannot learn which keywords and ads produce actual leads, resulting in wasted spend and no path to improving return on ad spend over time.

quickWins: Submit a review request by text or email to every completed project client from the past two years, even a handful of new reviews arriving in the next 30 days will meaningfully lift local search rankings and conversion rate.
Add descriptive alt text to all 50 images across the site, prioritizing kitchen project photos with location and service keywords in the descriptions.
Reduce the meta description on each key service page to under 155 characters and consolidate the three H1 tags on any page down to one clear, keyword-specific headline.
Install the Google Ads conversion tag and configure at minimum a form submission and phone call conversion event so any future paid campaign has the data it needs to optimize from day one.
audit_report.summary: Art Design and Construction LLC has real strengths to build on, including a perfect rating, a content-rich site, and basic tracking infrastructure, but the combination of a slow mobile load time, almost no review presence, zero AI recognition, and no social visibility means the business is losing a measurable share of Woodstock kitchen remodel leads to competitors who are easier to find and easier to trust at first glance. The gaps identified here are specific, fixable, and tied directly to the volume of new customers the business is trying to build. A focused growth engagement with OHM would address these gaps in priority order, starting with the ones driving the largest and most immediate lead loss.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the review gap, fixing Core Web Vitals, and establishing AI and social visibility in this market could realistically recover 8 to 15 qualified kitchen remodel inquiries per month that are currently going to competitors, representing $240,000 to $600,000 or more in addressable annual project revenue at typical kitchen remodel contract values.

categories.name: Tracking & Data

TikTok is absent, and short-form video of pool cleanings, before-and-after transformations, and seasonal tips is one of the highest-return organic content formats available to a local service business right now.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers including GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot are allowed access to the site, which is the right starting position, but structured data, sameAs entity links, FAQ schema, and an llms.txt guidance file are all absent, meaning AI models have almost no machine-readable signals to build an understanding of this business from. When we tested what AI models know about Datz Pool and Spa Care in Woodstock, GA, the answer was nothing, the business is not recognized, would not be recommended, and has no entity presence in the knowledge layer that AI assistants draw from when a homeowner asks 'who cleans pools in Woodstock.' findings.title: A 21-second load time is turning paid and organic traffic away before the site appears

Google's own data shows that mobile bounce rates increase dramatically past three seconds, so a meaningful share of every visitor the business earns through search, ads, or referrals is leaving before seeing any content, pricing, or contact option. With a Google Ads tag already in place, this is an active money drain: ad spend is generating clicks that evaporate before converting.

findings.title: No website analytics means the business cannot see who is visiting or where leads come from
findings.detail: With no analytics platform installed, Datz Pool and Spa Care has no visibility into traffic volume, traffic sources, page behavior, or conversion rates, every marketing dollar spent is going into a black box. This matters specifically for growing the customer base because without knowing which channels drive inquiries, there is no principled way to invest more in what works or cut what does not. It also means there is no baseline data to measure improvement against, which makes future marketing decisions expensive guesses.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know this business exists, a blind spot that will grow as AI search grows
findings.detail: A live probe of AI model knowledge returned no recognition of Datz Pool and Spa Care in Woodstock, GA, no description, no recommendation, no entity awareness. Homeowners are increasingly asking AI assistants to recommend local service providers by name and location, and a business with no structured data, no sameAs entity links, and no FAQ content gives AI models nothing to work with when building a response. Competitors who are structured correctly right now are being recommended in AI answers while this business is absent from that conversation entirely.

findings.title: 33 reviews and a 205-day review gap leave trust on the table for high-consideration buyers
findings.detail: A 4.9-star rating is a powerful asset, but in a category where homeowners are handing someone access to their backyard and trusting them with expensive equipment, review volume and recency are both scrutinized. The most recent review Google surfaces is 205 days old, which can signal to a cautious buyer that business activity has slowed, even if that is not the case. Closing the gap between 33 and 50-plus reviews, which is where most consumers perceive a business as established in the local services space, is one of the highest-leverage reputation moves available.

findings.title: No online booking means leads generated at night and on weekends have nowhere to convert
findings.detail: Pool care decisions are often made outside business hours, after a homeowner notices green water or a malfunctioning pump on a weekend afternoon. With no scheduling tool on the site, a motivated visitor who does not want to wait for a phone callback has no way to claim a slot and commit, so that intent evaporates. For a recurring service like weekly pool cleaning, losing even a handful of booking opportunities per month compounds into thousands of dollars in missed annual contract value.

findings.title: The site page title still references Palm Coast, not Woodstock
findings.detail: The HTML title tag reads 'Datz Pool and Spa Care - Pool Cleaning Palm Coast,' but the business operates in Woodstock, GA. This is the single most visible SEO signal on any page, and it is pointing Google toward the wrong geography, actively suppressing the site's ability to rank for Woodstock pool cleaning searches. For a local service business where geography is everything, a mismatched title tag in the wrong city is directly costing organic search visibility and the leads that come from it.

findings.title: 17 of 18 images have no alt text, hurting both accessibility and image search visibility
findings.detail: Across the entire site, only one of eighteen images carries alt text, which means search engines cannot read what those images depict and visually-impaired visitors get no description. For a pool and spa service where before-and-after photos and clean water visuals are a primary trust-builder, missing alt text means none of those images are indexed or surfaced in Google Image search, a real organic traffic channel for home services that is currently being forfeited entirely.

quickWins: Fix the page title from 'Palm Coast' to 'Woodstock, GA' across all pages, this is a single text change that immediately corrects the geographic targeting for every organic search in the actual service area.
Add a single H1 heading to each page that names the service and location clearly, such as 'Pool Cleaning Service in Woodstock, GA', zero H1s site-wide is a straightforward SEO gap with a direct fix.

Install Google Analytics (or any analytics platform) immediately so there is at minimum a baseline record of traffic, sources, and behavior going forward, every day without it is data permanently lost.
Add alt text to the 17 images currently missing it, descriptive alt text on pool cleaning photos opens the door to Google Image search traffic and costs nothing but time.
audit_report.summary: Datz Pool and Spa Care has the reputation to grow significantly, a 4.9-star rating and an established service in a high-demand market are real advantages, but a combination of a misfired page title, a site that takes 21 seconds to load on mobile, no analytics, and zero AI visibility means the business is winning despite its digital presence rather than because of it. categories.name: Website & Speed

categories.name: Social & Content

findings.title: A 12-second load time is sending mobile visitors straight to a competitor

findings.title: Ten reviews in a high-stakes category is a conversion killer

findings.title: No analytics means no ability to diagnose or improve what is already broken

The meta description at 175 characters is also being cut off in search results before the full value proposition is visible, meaning the pitch to click is incomplete for every search impression the site earns. These are not catastrophic on their own, but in a competitive local market they represent ranking and click-through rate percentage points that belong to the business and are currently being left on the table.

audit_report.headline: Where Lusk Pools is quietly losing customers before they ever make contact

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The mobile PageSpeed score of 61/100 is below the threshold where Google begins suppressing pages in mobile search results, and the Largest Contentful Paint of 10.4 seconds is more than four times Google's recommended 2.5-second ceiling, meaning a prospective customer on a phone waits over ten seconds to see the main content before they can decide to call. The site does pass HTTPS and mobile viewport checks, but mixed content is present, which browsers flag as a security warning, and a Cumulative Layout Shift of 0.13 means elements visibly jump as the page loads, both of which erode trust at the exact moment a visitor is deciding whether to book.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The page title is properly set and sized at 46 characters, and the site carries nearly 6,000 words of content, which is a real asset, but every page scanned is missing a meta description, there is not a single H1 tag anywhere on the site, and no canonical tag is set, which means Google is reading a structurally incomplete site and has no clear signal about which page to rank for which intent. The absence of local business schema markup is particularly costly for a service-area business: Google cannot programmatically confirm the business name, service area, phone number, or service type from structured data, which reduces eligibility for rich local results that competitors with schema will win.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: The site has a lead capture form, an online booking option, a newsletter signup, and a visible call to action, which is a stronger conversion foundation than most local service businesses, but there is no click-to-call phone number anywhere on the site, which is a direct revenue leak: mobile visitors, who represent the majority of local search traffic, cannot tap to call without manually copying a number, and industry data consistently shows that removing one friction point from that action meaningfully increases contact rates. The absence of live chat also means after-hours visitors, who are often the most motivated, have no immediate path to engage and will move on to a competitor who does.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: The Google Business Profile is operational with hours, a website link, a phone number, and 10 photos, which clears the minimum threshold, but a 4.4-star rating sits just below the 4.5 floor that most consumers and Google's own local ranking signals treat as a trust marker, and that gap is meaningful in a category like pool services where homeowners are making a high-trust decision about their property. The most recent review Google shows is 184 days old, which signals to both the algorithm and prospective customers that the business may not be actively engaged, and the GBP primary category is listed as 'general contractor' rather than a pool-specific category, which reduces relevance for the high-intent searches Lusk Pools actually wants to win. Whether the business description field is filled in was not confirmed on this run and should be checked directly, as a missing description is a straightforward gap in a competitive local pack.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Analytics 4 is installed, which means baseline traffic data is being collected, but there is no Facebook/Meta pixel and no Google Ads conversion tag anywhere on the site, which means the business cannot run retargeting campaigns, cannot build custom audiences from site visitors, and cannot measure which ad spend is actually producing phone calls or form submissions. For a pool cleaning service with a recurring revenue model, the inability to retarget a visitor who looked at the services page but did not book represents a compounding revenue loss every single week, and without conversion tracking, any future ad spend is operating completely blind.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: Lusk Pools maintains a presence on Facebook, YouTube, LinkedIn, and X, which is a broader platform footprint than many local competitors, but Instagram is not linked from the site at all, which is a notable gap for a pool service business where before-and-after visuals and clean water content perform extremely well with homeowners in the 30-55 demographic that makes pool service decisions. There is no video content on the website itself, and YouTube, though linked, is not being used to support the site's authority or conversion funnel. The specific opportunity here is not just being on more platforms, it is optimizing what already exists: consistent branding and handles across profiles, a clear link-in-bio structure, and a regular cadence of short-form visual content showing clean Canton pools would differentiate Lusk in a market where most competitors are posting nothing.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers including GPTBot and ClaudeBot are allowed to access the site, and the content depth of nearly 6,000 words gives AI models something to read, but a live probe confirmed that AI assistants do not recognize Lusk Pools by name, would not recommend them in their category, and return no specific knowledge of the business, which means when a Canton homeowner asks an AI assistant for pool cleaning recommendations, Lusk Pools does not exist in that answer. There is no structured data, no sameAs entity links connecting the website to the Google Business Profile or social profiles, no FAQ schema, and no llms.txt guidance file, all of which are the specific signals AI systems use to build confidence in a business's identity and expertise before surfacing it in a response. This is the fastest-growing customer discovery channel in home services right now, and being absent from it while competitors begin optimizing for it is not a minor gap, it is a strategic window that closes as AI results solidify around the businesses that act first.

findings.title: A 10-second load time is sending mobile searchers directly to competitors
findings.detail: The mobile Largest Contentful Paint of 10.4 seconds means the average Canton homeowner searching 'pool cleaning near me' on their phone sees a blank or partially loaded screen for ten seconds before they can read anything, and Google's own research shows that 53% of mobile visits are abandoned if a page takes longer than three seconds to load. For a business that wants more customers, this is not a design problem, it is a lead volume problem: every organic ranking Lusk Pools has earned is being partially negated by a site that visitors leave before it finishes loading. The performance score of 61/100 also directly suppresses Google rankings, meaning Lusk is both ranking lower and converting fewer of the visitors it does receive.

findings.title: No meta description and no H1 tag means Google is guessing what this business does
findings.detail: A missing meta description on every page means Google writes its own snippet in search results, typically pulling random text from the page that may not reflect the service being searched for, and a poorly written auto-generated snippet measurably reduces click-through rates even when the page ranks well. The complete absence of H1 tags site-wide removes the primary on-page signal that tells search engines what each page is about, which affects ranking for every service-specific keyword including 'pool cleaning Canton GA', 'pool maintenance Canton', and related terms that represent the highest-intent traffic Lusk Pools needs to grow its customer base. These are among the most foundational SEO elements and their absence is suppressing visibility that the site's 5,895 words of content has already done the work to earn.

findings.title: No click-to-call means mobile visitors cannot contact the business in one tap

findings.title: AI assistants do not know Lusk Pools exists, and that gap is growing

findings.title: The GBP is listed under the wrong primary category, costing local pack rankings

This is a single-field change on the profile that has an outsized effect on which searches Lusk Pools appears in.

findings.title: No retargeting infrastructure means warm leads are lost permanently
findings.detail: With no Facebook/Meta pixel and no Google Ads conversion tag on the site, every visitor who browses the services page, reads pool cleaning FAQs, or starts a booking and abandons is gone with no way to reconnect. For a pool cleaning business with recurring seasonal revenue, a customer who was interested enough to visit the site but did not convert represents not just one missed transaction but potentially years of repeat service value, and retargeting campaigns specifically targeting those visitors typically show significantly higher conversion rates than cold traffic. Without the pixel in place, that audience is building up and being lost every single day.

findings.title: The most recent Google review visible is 184 days old, which signals inactivity to both algorithms and homeowners
findings.detail: Google's local ranking algorithm treats review recency as a freshness signal, and a six-month gap in the reviews Google surfaces when ranking the profile puts Lusk at a disadvantage versus competitors who are actively generating reviews. For a prospective customer reading the profile, the visible absence of recent reviews raises a reasonable question about whether the business is still actively operating or performing at the level the 4.4-star average suggests. A consistent review generation process tied to completed service visits would address both the algorithmic signal and the social proof gap, and pushing the rating above 4.5 would cross a meaningful trust threshold for new customers.

audit_report.summary: Lusk Pools has a genuine 40-year reputation and enough content on its site to rank well, but structural gaps in SEO, site speed, tracking, and AI visibility are quietly redirecting ready-to-buy customers to competitors who have cleaned up these exact issues. Open Heart Media built this audit without being asked because the opportunity to grow the customer base here is real and specific, and the path to closing these gaps is clear. For a pool and spa supply store where seasonal urgency drives purchase decisions, the absence of self-serve scheduling and real-time chat means that visitors who are ready to act but not ready to call are simply leaving without a way to be followed up with.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: The Google Business Profile is genuinely strong by any local standard: a 4.9-star average across 464 reviews is exceptional for a pool supply store in a competitive Atlanta suburb, hours and website are linked, a phone number is listed, and a review came in within the last 36 days showing the profile is active. The photo count of 10 is the visible weak point, pool and spa retailers that dominate local pack results typically carry 50 to 100 photos showing showroom inventory, installations, and branded lifestyle imagery, and whether the business description field is filled in could not be confirmed in this scan and is worth checking directly in Google Business Profile manager. The missing LocalBusiness schema on the website also means the profile and the site are not reinforcing each other the way they could be.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Tag Manager, a Facebook/Meta pixel, and a Google Ads conversion tag are all confirmed present, which puts this business ahead of most local independents and means paid campaigns can actually attribute leads and optimize toward real conversions. The infrastructure is solid; the opportunity now is ensuring the events firing through GTM are granular enough to distinguish form submissions, phone clicks, and video views so that ad spend is optimized against the actions that actually produce customers rather than just site visits.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube are all linked from the site, and video content is present, a meaningful advantage for a category like pools and spas where visual storytelling drives purchase intent. TikTok is absent entirely, which matters because short-form vertical video is now one of the highest-reach organic channels for home improvement and backyard lifestyle content, and competitors who post there are capturing discovery from a younger homeowner audience that Basements and Backyards is currently not reaching. Profile optimization, consistent branding, complete bios, a single clear link-in-bio destination, and a predictable posting cadence, was not verifiable from this scan, but for a business with this much visual product inventory, those profiles represent a significant untapped distribution channel.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers including GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot are allowed access to the site, and the content depth of 15,000 words gives AI models something to read, both positive signals. However, there is no structured data, no sameAs entity links connecting the website to the Google Business Profile or social profiles, no FAQ schema, and no llms.txt guidance file, which means AI systems are piecing together an incomplete and unconfirmed picture of this business. Most critically, when AI models are asked about pool and spa stores in the Woodstock or Atlanta area, Basements and Backyards, Inc does not surface as a known or recommended business, in a world where a growing share of buyers open ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google AI Overviews and ask for recommendations before they ever run a traditional search, that invisibility is a direct and accelerating revenue gap that will only widen as AI-assisted search becomes the default.

findings.title: A 19.8-second load time is functionally a closed door for mobile shoppers
findings.detail: Google's own research shows that 53% of mobile users abandon a page that takes longer than 3 seconds to load. At 19.8 seconds LCP, the Basements and Backyards site is not just slow, it is losing the majority of mobile visitors before they see a single product, read a single review, or find the phone number. For a store that runs Google Ads and has a Facebook pixel in place, this means paid traffic is being sent to a page that discards most of it before conversion is even possible, turning ad spend into wasted impressions.

findings.title: AI assistants have never heard of this business, and that gap is growing
findings.detail: A direct probe of AI model knowledge found no recognition of Basements and Backyards, Inc in Woodstock, GA, meaning that when a homeowner asks an AI assistant to recommend a pool supply store near Woodstock, this business does not appear in the answer. The site has no structured data, no entity links, and no FAQ content for AI systems to quote or cite. As AI-assisted discovery replaces a meaningful share of traditional Google searches, being absent from that channel is equivalent to having no Google ranking in 2015.

findings.title: LocalBusiness schema is missing, which undermines both SEO and AI visibility simultaneously
findings.detail: There is no LocalBusiness schema markup anywhere on the site, confirmed across all five pages scanned. Schema markup is how search engines and AI systems confirm the business name, address, phone, hours, service categories, and rating with high confidence rather than inferring it from text, and its absence means both Google's local ranking algorithm and AI recommendation engines are working with less reliable signals than competitors who have it implemented. This is a single technical fix with compounding benefits across organic search, the local map pack, and AI-generated answers.

findings.title: No online scheduling means motivated visitors leave without converting
findings.detail: The site has a form and a phone number but no online booking or scheduling tool across any of the five pages scanned, including the contact and service plan pages. Pool and spa purchases and service appointments are high-consideration decisions, and a significant portion of buyers research during evenings and weekends when calling feels intrusive, those visitors need a self-serve path to book a consultation or service visit. Every week without scheduling is a week of after-hours intent that converts to nothing.

findings.title: Nine images are missing alt text, and the Google Business Profile has only 10 photos
findings.detail: Nine of 31 site images lack alt text, which reduces both accessibility compliance and the keyword signals that search engines use to understand visual content on a product-heavy site. Separately, the Google Business Profile carries only 10 photos, pool and spa stores that rank at the top of local pack results in competitive markets typically show 50 or more images of showroom inventory, water features, game room setups, and installations, because photo volume is a confirmed factor in local search prominence and directly influences click-through rate from the map pack.

findings.title: No email or newsletter capture means the marketing list is not growing
findings.detail: Across all five pages scanned, there is no email opt-in or newsletter signup, confirmed site-wide. A pool and spa supply store has a natural seasonal marketing calendar, opening kits, chemical reminders, winter closing services, new spa arrivals, and an owned email list turns one-time buyers into repeat customers and referral sources. Without a capture mechanism, every visitor who leaves without buying is gone permanently, and the business is entirely dependent on paid or organic channels to re-engage them.

findings.title: TikTok is absent from a business category where short video drives purchase decisions
findings.detail: Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube are all linked, but TikTok is not present, and it is not a small omission for this category. Pool and backyard lifestyle content performs exceptionally well on TikTok's algorithm because it is visual, aspirational, and tied to homeownership, the exact audience buying pools and spas in Woodstock. Competitors who post installation walk-throughs, before-and-after reveals, and chemical tutorials are building organic reach and brand familiarity with homeowners at the exact moment they are dreaming about their backyards.

quickWins: Compress and properly size the images driving the 19.8-second LCP, this single change typically cuts load time by 40 to 60 percent and is the fastest path to recovering mobile conversions

Add LocalBusiness schema markup to the homepage and contact page with name, address, phone, hours, geo-coordinates, and aggregate review rating, this fixes the SEO schema failure and begins building AI visibility at the same time

Upload at least 40 additional photos to the Google Business Profile showing showroom displays, pool and spa inventory, game room setups, and branded signage to increase local map pack click-through rate
Add alt text to the 9 images confirmed missing it, a one-hour task that closes an accessibility gap and adds keyword signals to product imagery across the site
audit_report.summary: Basements and Backyards, Inc has built something genuinely rare in local retail: a 4.9-star reputation with nearly 500 reviews, real ad infrastructure, and a content-rich site. What is holding back customer growth is a set of specific, fixable technical and strategic gaps, a mobile site that loses the majority of visitors before they load, zero presence in AI-assisted search where buying decisions are increasingly starting, and conversion paths that have no fallback when a visitor is not ready to call. audit_report.headline: Bairds Pool Co LLC has a 4.9-star reputation and nowhere online to send it
audit_report.overallVerdict: A strong local reputation is being completely wasted by a broken website, a missing Google Business Profile, and a total absence of lead capture, meaning nearly every prospective customer who searches online finds nothing, or finds a dead end.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site returns a 403 Forbidden error, meaning it is effectively unreachable to visitors despite HTTPS being active and the mobile viewport being correctly configured. Even setting aside the access failure, a mobile PageSpeed score of 63 and a Largest Contentful Paint of 8.9 seconds, more than three times the 2.5-second threshold Google considers acceptable, would cost meaningful rankings and visitor patience on their own.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The page that loads contains only 15 words of content, no local business schema markup, and no canonical tag, giving search engines almost nothing to index or rank for service-area searches like 'pool cleaning near me' in Georgia. Without schema or substantive content, Google cannot confirm what the business does, where it operates, or who it serves, the foundational signals that determine whether a local service business appears in organic results at all.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: Every conversion signal on the site fails: there is no phone number, no contact form, no booking tool, no call to action, no live chat, and no address listed anywhere on the site. A prospective customer who somehow reaches the site has no path to becoming a lead, they arrive and leave with no way to contact the business.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: No Google Business Profile was found for Bairds Pool Co LLC in a live search, which is the single most damaging visibility gap a local service business can have. The Google Maps pack, the three listings that dominate local search results for queries like 'pool cleaning service Georgia', is completely inaccessible to them without a profile, meaning competitors with even mediocre profiles are capturing all of that intent-driven traffic. The 4.9-star rating across 74 reviews is a genuine competitive asset, but it exists on a platform the business cannot currently be found through, so that social proof is invisible to anyone searching.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Analytics 4, a Facebook/Meta pixel, and a Google Ads conversion tag are all present and firing, which is a meaningful foundation, someone has clearly done prior ad or tracking work. The critical gap is that with no working landing page and no conversion actions on the site (no form, no phone click, no booking), the tags are collecting session data but recording zero conversions, meaning any ad spend is running blind with no signal for optimization.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: No social profiles are linked from the site, not Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, or TikTok, and there is no video content anywhere in the scanned presence. For a pool cleaning service, short-form video showing before-and-after cleans, water chemistry checks, or equipment walkthroughs performs exceptionally well on Instagram Reels and TikTok and drives direct service inquiries. The opportunity to build optimized profiles with consistent branding, a clear service-area bio, a booking link, and a regular posting cadence exists entirely untouched right now.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers are allowed to access the site, which is the one positive signal here, but there is no structured data, no entity links connecting business profiles, no FAQ content for AI to quote, and the site contains only 15 words, far below the content depth needed for any AI model to summarize or recommend this business. When AI models are asked to recommend pool cleaning services in Georgia, Bairds Pool Co LLC does not appear: a direct test of what AI assistants know about this business returned no recognition whatsoever. As more consumers skip Google entirely and ask AI tools for local service recommendations, being unknown to those models is an accelerating visibility gap that compounds every month it goes unaddressed.

findings.title: No Google Business Profile, the local search door is closed
findings.detail: A live search found no Google Business Profile for Bairds Pool Co LLC, which means the business does not appear in the Google Maps local pack for any pool cleaning searches in their service area. The local pack receives the majority of clicks for service-area searches, and competitors with even basic profiles are capturing every one of those leads by default. With 74 reviews and a 4.9 rating, Bairds has the credibility to dominate local results, but that credibility is completely invisible to anyone searching right now.

findings.title: The website returns a 403 error, it turns visitors away
findings.detail: The site is technically live and secured with HTTPS, but it returns a 403 Forbidden response, which means any visitor who clicks through from an ad, a referral, or a search result hits a blank error page. This makes every dollar of past or future ad spend, and the Google Ads and Meta pixel tags that are already installed, functionally wasted until the site is accessible. A broken website does not just fail to convert visitors; it actively signals to Google that the site is unreliable, which suppresses any remaining organic rankings.

findings.title: Zero lead capture on the site, no path from interest to contact
findings.detail: There is no phone number, contact form, booking widget, or call to action anywhere on the site, every single conversion mechanism is absent. For a pool cleaning company, the difference between a visitor and a booked customer is often a single friction-free action like clicking a phone number or submitting a quick quote request. Without any of those, visitors who somehow reach the site have no choice but to leave and call a competitor who makes it easier to get in touch.

findings.title: 8.9-second load time loses mobile visitors before the page appears
findings.detail: The Largest Contentful Paint on mobile is 8.9 seconds, Google's threshold for a good user experience is 2.5 seconds, and research consistently shows that more than half of mobile users abandon a page that takes longer than 3 seconds to load. Since most local service searches happen on mobile, a load time this slow is directly costing visitor sessions and, by extension, potential service inquiries. This is compounded by the current 403 error, but it will need to be addressed even after the access issue is resolved.

findings.title: AI models have no knowledge of this business, an emerging but urgent gap
findings.detail: A probe of what AI models know about Bairds Pool Co LLC returned no recognition at all, and the site provides none of the signals, structured data, entity links, FAQ content, or content depth, that would allow AI systems to identify and recommend the business. Consumers in Georgia increasingly use tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews to find local services, often bypassing traditional search results. Any competitor that establishes AI recognition now will hold a durable advantage as this channel grows.

findings.title: Tracking infrastructure exists but records nothing actionable
findings.detail: GA4, the Meta pixel, and the Google Ads tag are all installed and firing, which represents real prior investment. But with no working pages and no conversion events configured, the data being collected is session-level noise, there are no form submissions, phone clicks, or booking completions to optimize toward. This means any ad campaigns run through these tags are optimizing toward nothing, and budget is almost certainly being wasted on audiences that never convert.

findings.title: No social presence or video content, a channel competitors are using
findings.detail: No social profiles are linked from the site and no video content exists anywhere in the scanned presence. Before-and-after pool cleaning content, especially short-form video on Instagram and TikTok, generates consistent organic reach for service businesses in this category and frequently drives direct quote requests. The absence of any social footprint also weakens AI and search entity recognition, since platforms like Facebook and Instagram are among the signals AI models use to verify and surface local businesses.

quickWins: Claim and fully complete a Google Business Profile with the service area, hours, phone number, and a link to the site, this alone can put the business in front of local searches within days.
Fix the 403 error so the website is actually reachable, then add a visible phone number and a simple contact or quote request form on the homepage.
Add local business structured data (schema markup) to the site so Google and AI systems can correctly identify the business type, location, and services.

Create and link an Instagram profile with a service-area bio and a booking or contact link, even five before-and-after posts establish a social presence that supports both human trust and AI entity recognition.
audit_report.summary: Bairds Pool Co LLC has genuinely strong raw material, a near-perfect rating and a meaningful review count, but the infrastructure needed to turn that reputation into a steady flow of new customers simply does not exist yet. The website is unreachable, there is no Google Business Profile, no way for visitors to contact the business, and no recognition from the AI tools that are increasingly driving local service decisions. Closing these gaps in the right order and building a connected local presence is exactly the kind of work OHM does, and a discovery call is the fastest way to see what a prioritized fix looks like for this specific situation.
audit_report.estimate: A functioning website, an active Google Business Profile, and basic lead capture could realistically add 15 to 30 qualified local inquiries per month, at typical pool cleaning service values, that represents several thousand dollars in new recurring monthly revenue.

audit_report.headline: Where PalmSet Pools is quietly losing customers before they ever make contact
audit_report.overallVerdict: PalmSet Pools has a strong reputation and a real web presence, but critical gaps in site speed, AI visibility, conversion tracking, and structured data are costing them qualified leads every week in one of Georgia's most active pool-building markets.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: Mobile PageSpeed scores 58 out of 100, which places the site in Google's 'needs improvement' range, but the real problem is the Largest Contentful Paint of 12.4 seconds, nearly five times the 2.5-second threshold Google considers acceptable and a near-certain trigger for mobile visitors to leave before the page finishes loading. HTTPS is active, the mobile viewport is correctly set, and layout stability is perfect with a CLS of zero, so the foundation is sound but the load speed issue alone is enough to suppress rankings and burn paid traffic.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The page title and meta description are present and correctly sized, and the site carries nearly 4,000 words of content, which gives Google enough to read. However, three H1 tags exist across the scanned pages where each page should have exactly one, local business schema markup is entirely absent, and nine of fourteen images are missing alt text, all of which reduce how confidently Google can classify and rank the site for high-intent searches like 'pool contractor Woodstock GA'.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: The site has a phone number, a contact form, an online booking option, and a clear call to action, which is a solid conversion baseline that many contractors lack. The gaps are the absence of live chat, which matters for the significant share of visitors who browse in the evening or on weekends when calling feels awkward, and no email or newsletter capture, which means every visitor who does not convert immediately is lost with no path to re-engage them.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: A 5-star rating across 49 reviews is genuinely strong and well above average for a pool contractor in a market like Woodstock, and a review posted just 31 days ago signals an active reputation. The profile has hours, a linked website, and a phone number in place, and at 10 photos it meets a basic threshold, though pool contractors with active profiles in competitive suburban Atlanta markets routinely carry 30 to 50 photos showing finished builds, which is a meaningful trust gap. The business description field could not be verified in this scan and should be checked directly, because it is prime real estate for keyword-rich copy that influences both Google ranking and first impressions.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Analytics 4 is installed, so basic traffic data is being collected, but there is no Facebook pixel and no Google Ads conversion tag anywhere on the site. Without these, PalmSet Pools cannot run retargeting campaigns to recapture visitors who looked but did not book, cannot build lookalike audiences from past customers, and cannot measure which ad spend, if any is running, is actually producing calls or form submissions.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: PalmSet Pools is linked to four platforms, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, which is a broader footprint than most local pool contractors maintain, and that breadth is a real asset. However, there is no video on the website itself, which is a missed opportunity given that pool construction is one of the most visually compelling categories in home services, and short build-process or before-and-after clips would perform strongly on both TikTok and Instagram Reels. Profile optimization, consistent branding and handles across all four platforms, a clear link in bio directing traffic to a quote page, complete business bios with service areas, and a reliable posting cadence tied to the Georgia pool season, represents meaningful untapped reach that the current setup is not capturing.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers are allowed to access the site, which is the right starting point, but structured data is entirely absent, there are no sameAs entity links connecting the website to the business's social profiles or directory listings, and there is no llms.txt guidance file to help AI models understand who PalmSet Pools is and what they do. When AI models were tested on knowledge of this business, the result was explicit: the business is not recognized and would not be recommended to someone asking an AI assistant for a pool contractor in Woodstock. This is the single most urgent emerging visibility gap in the entire audit, a growing share of high-intent buyers now ask AI assistants directly for contractor recommendations, and a business that AI has never heard of is completely invisible in that channel while competitors who have structured their data correctly are already capturing those referrals.

findings.title: A 12.4-second load time is turning away mobile visitors before they see a single photo
findings.detail: Google's own threshold for an acceptable Largest Contentful Paint is 2.5 seconds. PalmSet Pools clocks in at 12.4 seconds on mobile, meaning the main content does not appear for nearly half a minute on a typical phone connection. Pool buyers are comparison shopping across multiple contractors simultaneously, and research consistently shows that over half of mobile users abandon a site that takes longer than 3 seconds to load, every one of those exits is a lead that went to a competitor.

findings.title: No Google Ads or Meta pixel means every visitor who does not convert on the first visit is gone permanently
findings.detail: Without a Facebook pixel or Google Ads conversion tag, PalmSet Pools has no ability to retarget the visitors who browse the portfolio, check pricing, or start a form and then leave without contacting. In a category where a single closed job is worth $50,000 to $150,000 or more, the inability to re-engage warm visitors through follow-up ads is a significant and quantifiable revenue leak. It also means any ad spend currently running cannot be tied to actual leads or booked jobs.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know PalmSet Pools exists, and that gap is growing in urgency
findings.detail: A direct probe of AI model knowledge returned an explicit non-recognition result: the business is not known and would not be recommended. With no structured data, no sameAs entity links, and no llms.txt file, there is nothing on the site that helps AI assistants confidently identify, describe, or cite PalmSet Pools when a buyer asks for pool contractors in Woodstock or Cherokee County. This channel is still early enough that moving now creates a durable competitive advantage before it becomes table stakes.

findings.title: Missing local business schema leaves Google guessing about what and where PalmSet Pools actually is
findings.detail: Schema markup is the structured signal that tells Google, Bing, and AI crawlers precisely that this is a pool contractor, located in Woodstock, GA, with a specific service area, phone number, and hours. Its complete absence means the site relies entirely on Google interpreting unstructured text correctly, which reduces eligibility for rich results in local search and weakens the site's position against competitors who have implemented it. For a business trying to pull more customers from nearby cities and suburbs, schema is a foundational ranking signal that is simply not working for them right now.

findings.title: Three H1 tags and nine images without alt text send mixed signals to search engines
findings.detail: Search engines use the H1 heading to understand the primary topic of each page. Having three on a single page dilutes that signal and can cause Google to be less confident about which term the page should rank for. Separately, nine of fourteen images have no alt text, which means those images contribute zero SEO value and create accessibility barriers, both of which are factors in how Google evaluates overall page quality.

findings.title: Ten Google Business Profile photos is the floor, not the goal, for a pool contractor in this market
findings.detail: Pool construction is one of the highest-ticket and most visually evaluated purchases a homeowner makes. Profiles for competing contractors in the greater Atlanta suburbs with 30 to 50 photos of completed pools, in-progress builds, and finished backyards consistently outperform thin profiles in local pack rankings and convert better when buyers are comparing options. At 10 photos, PalmSet Pools is meeting the minimum but not taking advantage of the 5-star portfolio they have clearly already built.

findings.title: No live chat and no email capture mean after-hours interest has nowhere to go
findings.detail: Pool research happens heavily on evenings and weekends when homeowners are at home and thinking about their backyard. Without live chat, a visitor who has a quick question at 9pm has only the form or a phone call as options, both carry friction at that hour. Without any email capture, there is no way to nurture the visitors who are interested but not ready to request a quote yet, which in a $60,000-plus purchase category represents a meaningful share of the pipeline.

quickWins: Add the Google Ads conversion tag and Facebook pixel to the site immediately so that warm traffic can be retargeted and any future ad spend can be measured against actual leads
Fix the three-H1 issue and add alt text to the nine untagged images, both are straightforward code edits that clean up real SEO signals without a site redesign
Upload 20 to 30 additional photos to the Google Business Profile, prioritizing finished pool builds, aerial or elevated shots of completed backyards, and in-progress construction images

Verify and complete the Google Business Profile description with keyword-rich copy covering service area, pool types built, and what makes PalmSet Pools the right choice, this field was not confirmed in this scan and is worth checking today
audit_report.summary: PalmSet Pools is sitting on a genuinely strong foundation, a 5-star rating, solid content, four active social platforms, and a conversion-ready site structure, but a 12.4-second mobile load time, zero tracking pixels, no structured data, and complete invisibility to AI assistants are suppressing lead flow in ways that compound each other. Open Heart Media has already identified the specific gaps and the order in which closing them produces the fastest return. The discovery call is where we walk through what a prioritized fix sequence looks like for a pool contractor in this market and what realistic lead volume growth looks like over 90 days.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the speed, tracking, schema, and AI visibility gaps identified here puts a pool contractor in a position to capture an additional 8 to 15 qualified quote requests per month in a market where a single closed job commonly generates $60,000 to $120,000 in revenue.

findings.title: A 2,800 ms page freeze is turning mobile visitors into competitor leads

findings.title: No call to action means visitors have nowhere obvious to go next

findings.title: AI assistants do not know Anthem exists, and pool shoppers are increasingly asking them first

As more homeowners begin pool research with a prompt like 'best pool contractors near Woodstock GA' typed into an AI assistant, being invisible in that channel while competitors build AI-readable authority is a gap that compounds over time and becomes harder to close.

findings.title: No local business schema means Google is guessing at what Anthem does and where
findings.detail: The site has zero structured data markup, which means Google cannot programmatically confirm Anthem's service area, business category, service offerings, or contact details from the website itself, it has to infer all of that from plain text. Without schema, Anthem is unlikely to appear in the rich result formats and local service packs that pool shoppers see at the top of results pages, and the business is effectively handing those premium placements to competitors who have taken the time to implement markup.

findings.title: 42 reviews is eight short of the threshold that changes buyer behavior
findings.detail: Pool construction is a high-trust, high-stakes purchase, and the psychological credibility of a contractor's review count is well documented: buyers treat businesses with 50 or more reviews differently from those just below that mark, even when the star rating is identical. At 4.8 stars, Anthem has the quality signal, but at 42 reviews it does not yet have the volume signal that pushes a hesitant homeowner from 'considering' to 'calling.' findings.title: No video anywhere on the site for a category that sells through visual transformation

findings.title: Two H1 tags split the SEO authority that should be concentrated on a single keyword target

For a pool contractor competing in a metro Atlanta suburb with established competitors, every on-page optimization point matters, and this is a structural issue that slightly suppresses the page's ability to rank for its primary target terms.

findings.detail: A live probe of AI models found zero recognition of Royal Kitchen & Bathroom in Woodstock, GA. With homeowners now routinely asking ChatGPT and Perplexity for contractor recommendations before they open Google Maps, a business that does not exist in AI training data or real-time retrieval indexes is completely invisible in that channel. The structured data and content depth are already in place, but the entity signal is not strong enough yet to break through, and there is no llms.txt file to guide AI crawlers on how to represent the business.

findings.title: No retargeting audience is being built from site traffic
findings.detail: The Facebook/Meta pixel is not installed, which means every potential customer who visits the site, browses the gallery, and leaves without filling out a form disappears permanently from a marketing standpoint. For a service where the average consideration cycle spans several weeks and multiple research sessions, retargeting those warm visitors on Facebook and Instagram with project photos or a special consultation offer is one of the highest-ROI ad strategies available to local remodelers. Without the pixel, that audience is being discarded every day.

findings.title: No mid-funnel conversion path for buyers who are not ready to call
findings.detail: The site offers a phone number and a contact form, but nothing in between for the majority of remodel shoppers who are still in the comparison phase. Online scheduling for a no-pressure design consultation, or even a simple email capture tied to a 'Woodstock Kitchen Remodel Cost Guide', would capture prospects who will not call until they have compared three more companies. Right now those visitors leave without a trace, and the business has no way to follow up with them.

findings.title: Page title is optimized for materials, not for the service buyers are searching
findings.detail: The current page title is 'Royal Kitchen & Bathroom - Quartz and Granite Countertops', which targets countertop material searches rather than the remodeling service searches where buying intent is highest. A homeowner planning a full kitchen renovation is searching 'kitchen remodeler Woodstock GA', not 'quartz countertops', and the title tag is the single most weighted on-page SEO signal. This framing may be limiting organic ranking potential for the service terms that generate the largest average project values.

findings.title: Missing canonical tag creates duplicate content risk across URL variants
findings.detail: The site does not set a canonical tag, which means if the same pages are accessible at multiple URLs (www vs. non-www, trailing slash vs. no trailing slash, or URL parameters from campaign tracking), Google may split the ranking authority across those versions instead of consolidating it on the preferred URL. Over time this dilutes the SEO equity that 4,066 words of content and quality inbound links should be building, and it is a straightforward technical fix with a disproportionate upside.

findings.title: Largest Contentful Paint of 2.9 seconds sits outside Google's 'good' threshold
findings.detail: Google's Core Web Vitals benchmark for a 'good' LCP is 2.5 seconds; the site is measuring at 2.9 seconds on mobile, putting it in the 'needs improvement' band. While the overall PageSpeed score of 94 is strong, LCP is one of the three signals Google uses directly in its page experience ranking factor, and in a competitive local market where two or three remodelers are vying for the same search placement, a sub-threshold LCP is a tiebreaker working against this business.

quickWins: Correct the Google Business Profile primary category from 'furniture_store' to 'Kitchen remodeler' and add 'Bathroom remodeler' as a secondary category, this single change can restore local 3-pack visibility for the business's highest-value search terms.
Install the Facebook/Meta pixel on the site immediately so that retargeting audiences start accumulating from today's traffic, even before any paid social campaigns are running.
Add a canonical tag to every page pointing to the preferred URL version to consolidate ranking authority and protect the SEO value of existing content.

Create and publish an llms.txt file and strengthen entity signals (consistent business name, address, and category across all directories) to accelerate recognition by AI assistants before competitors establish that ground first.
audit_report.summary: Royal Kitchen & Bathroom has real strengths, a fast site, solid reviews, and a broad social footprint, but the findings above show a business that is structurally underperforming where buyer decisions are actually being made: Google's local pack, AI recommendation engines, and mid-funnel remarketing. Open Heart Media built this audit before any conversation to show exactly what that gap looks like in specific, measurable terms. The next step is a focused discovery call to map which of these gaps is costing the most leads right now and what a phased plan to close them looks like.
audit_report.estimate: Correcting the GBP category alone could restore local 3-pack exposure for searches that represent the business's highest average ticket size; combined with retargeting infrastructure and AI visibility, the realistic upside is capturing a materially larger share of the estimated 200 to 400 monthly searches for kitchen and bathroom remodeling services in the Woodstock and Cherokee County market.
