audit_report.headline: Where Home Pools is quietly losing customers before they ever make contact
audit_report.overallVerdict: Home Pools has the technical bones of a serious local business, secure site, tracking tags, and schema in place, but a 9.5-second load time, a thin 181-word site, zero lead capture forms, a below-threshold Google rating, and a complete block on AI crawlers are actively bleeding customers to competitors who are easier to find, faster to load, and quicker to trust.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site earns credit for HTTPS, stable layout (CLS of 0), and a responsive mobile viewport, but a Google PageSpeed mobile score of 54/100 and a Largest Contentful Paint of 9.5 seconds, more than three times Google's 2.5-second threshold, means the average pool owner on a phone is staring at a blank screen long enough to hit the back button. A 430ms Total Blocking Time compounds this, signaling heavy render-blocking resources that delay interactivity and directly reduce the share of visitors who stay long enough to become leads.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The page title at 77 characters and the meta description at 229 characters both exceed recommended character limits, risking truncation in search results and diluting the click-through signal Google uses to rank local pages. Structural elements like a single H1, local business schema, and a canonical tag are correctly in place, but with only 181 words of content across the entire site, there is almost nothing for Google to evaluate as topical authority for high-intent searches like 'pool pump repair Canton GA' or 'pool heater service near me.'

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: The site has a phone number with click-to-call and a visible CTA, which covers the bare minimum, but there is no contact form, no online booking, and no live chat, meaning every conversion depends entirely on a visitor being ready to call at that exact moment. Pool repair customers frequently want to submit a request after hours or get a quote without a phone call, and without any of those capture mechanisms, every one of those visitors leaves with no way for Home Pools to follow up.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: The Google Business Profile is operational with hours, a website link, a phone number, and 10 photos checked, which is a functional baseline. However, a 4.2-star rating falls below the 4.5-plus threshold where most consumers give automatic trust, and 35 total reviews is well below the 50-plus benchmark that signals credibility for a home-services business competing in a market where pool repair decisions involve significant spend. The most recent review Google surfaces is 327 days old, which signals to both the algorithm and prospective customers that the business may not be actively engaged, whether or not newer reviews exist that Google is not surfacing.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Tag Manager, a Facebook/Meta pixel, and a Google Ads conversion tag are all present and accounted for, which puts Home Pools ahead of most local service businesses from a data infrastructure standpoint. The meaningful gap is that without a lead form or booking tool on the site, the conversion events these tags are designed to track are limited almost entirely to phone clicks, which underreports actual customer interest and makes ad optimization significantly less effective.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: No social profiles, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, or TikTok, are linked anywhere on the site, and no video content exists on the site itself, representing a near-total absence from the channels where homeowners in Canton, GA are actively researching pool service companies. For a Swimming pool repair service, short video content showing a technician diagnosing a pump failure or walking through a heater repair is among the highest-converting organic content available, and none of it is being produced or distributed. The opportunity to build complete, consistently branded profiles with a clear link back to the site, regular service-focused posts, and before-and-after visual content is entirely untouched.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: Home Pools is actively blocking every major AI crawler, including GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and Google-Extended, which means ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Apple Intelligence are structurally prevented from reading the site and cannot recommend the business in response to queries like 'best pool repair service in Canton GA.' A direct probe of what AI models know about this business confirmed they have no knowledge of Home Pools by name, making it invisible in a channel where buyer behavior is shifting fast. Structured data and FAQ schema are present, which would be genuine assets the moment crawlers are allowed in, but without entity links connecting the site to external profiles and directories, AI models have no way to build a reliable knowledge graph around the business even if access were restored today.

findings.title: A 9.5-second load time is sending mobile visitors straight to competitors
findings.detail: Google's own threshold for an acceptable Largest Contentful Paint is 2.5 seconds, Home Pools clocks in at 9.5 seconds on mobile, which is where the majority of pool repair searches happen. Research consistently shows that mobile bounce rates spike sharply after 3 seconds, meaning a significant portion of paid and organic traffic is likely leaving before the page is usable, turning ad spend and SEO effort into wasted budget.

findings.title: No lead form means after-hours interest disappears with no record
findings.detail: Pool equipment failures happen on weekends, in the evening, and during holidays, exactly when people are least likely to make a phone call to a business they have never used before. With no contact form or booking widget anywhere on the site, every visitor who is not ready to call at that exact moment is permanently lost, and Google Tag Manager has no conversion event to record that they were ever interested.

findings.title: AI crawlers are blocked, making the business invisible to the fastest-growing search channel
findings.detail: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, and three other AI crawlers are explicitly blocked in the site configuration, and a live test confirmed that AI models have no knowledge of Home Pools. As more homeowners ask AI assistants for pool repair recommendations in Canton, Home Pools cannot appear in those answers at all, not because the AI chose a competitor, but because it has been technically locked out of the site.

findings.title: 35 reviews at 4.2 stars is losing the trust battle before the first call
findings.detail: In home services, the research consistently shows that consumers treat roughly 50 reviews as a credibility threshold and 4.5 stars as a trust floor. Home Pools sits below both numbers, and the most visible recent review Google surfaces is nearly a year old. A prospective customer comparing Home Pools to a competitor with 80 reviews at 4.7 stars will almost always choose the higher-volume, fresher-reviewed option, regardless of actual service quality.

findings.title: 181 words of site content cannot compete for high-value local search terms
findings.detail: Search queries like 'pool pump repair Canton GA,' 'pool heater not working Woodstock,' and 'swimming pool service near me' represent high-intent traffic from people ready to spend money. With only 181 words across the entire site, Google has almost no text to match against those queries, no service-specific pages to rank, and no topical signals to build authority around pool repair in Cherokee County.

findings.title: Zero social media presence removes a major trust and referral channel
findings.detail: When a Canton homeowner hears about Home Pools from a neighbor and goes to look them up, finding no Facebook page, no Instagram profile, and no YouTube channel is a quiet trust killer, it suggests a business that is not active or established. Beyond trust, platforms like Facebook and Nextdoor are where local pool owners ask for recommendations, and without a presence, Home Pools is excluded from those conversations entirely.

findings.title: Title and meta description length overruns are trimming click-through rates in search results
findings.detail: The page title at 77 characters exceeds Google's roughly 60-character display limit, and the meta description at 229 characters is nearly double the recommended 155-character cap, both are being cut off in search results, which means the service area, key offer, and trust signals in those tags may not be visible to searchers before they click. For a business relying on organic search to bring in new customers, every lost click compounds over thousands of monthly impressions.

quickWins: Remove the robots.txt or meta rules blocking GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and Google-Extended so AI crawlers can immediately begin indexing the site and building business knowledge.
Trim the page title to under 60 characters and the meta description to under 155 characters so both display fully in Google search results without being cut off.
Add a simple contact form with name, phone, and service type fields so after-hours and non-phone leads have a capture path and the Google Ads tag has a form-submission conversion to optimize against.

Set up a structured post-service review request, via text immediately after job completion, to push the review count past 50 and the rating toward 4.5, the thresholds where local trust visibly shifts.
audit_report.summary: Home Pools is running paid tracking infrastructure on a site that cannot load fast enough to keep visitors, cannot capture leads who are not ready to call, and is invisible to the AI assistants and social channels where its next customers are actively searching. The gaps identified here are specific, measurable, and fixable, but each one left open is a recurring daily cost in leads handed to competitors. Open Heart Media works with local service businesses to close exactly these gaps in a sequenced, data-driven way, and a 30-minute conversation is enough to map out what that would look like for Home Pools.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the speed, lead capture, review, content, and AI visibility gaps identified here could realistically convert 20 to 40 percent more of the traffic Home Pools is already paying to attract, for a pool repair business averaging several hundred dollars per service call, that represents thousands of dollars in recoverable monthly revenue from existing traffic alone, before any increase in ad spend or reach.

audit_report.headline: Where London Floors is quietly losing customers before they ever pick up the phone
audit_report.overallVerdict: London Floors has the raw ingredients of a strong local business, a perfect 5-star rating, active ad tracking, and a content-rich site, but a 23-second mobile load time, zero AI recognition, and structural SEO gaps are costing them leads every day from buyers who bounce before the page finishes painting.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: Google PageSpeed scores the mobile site at 38 out of 100, with a Largest Contentful Paint of 23.1 seconds, nearly ten times slower than Google's 2.5-second threshold and well into the range where most mobile visitors abandon the page entirely before seeing a single product. HTTPS is active, the layout is stable (CLS 0.001), and the viewport is mobile-responsive, so the foundation is solid, but the speed failure is severe enough to negate those wins and actively suppress paid and organic traffic quality scores.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The page title, meta description, and canonical tag are all present and correctly sized, and 4,800 words of on-site content gives search engines genuine material to index, meaningful advantages over many local competitors. However, two H1 tags exist where only one should, which dilutes topical focus and sends a confusing signal to crawlers, and the complete absence of Local Business schema markup means Google cannot confidently surface structured information like address, service area, or category in rich results, leaving ranking potential on the table.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: The site covers the essential conversion bases, a click-to-call number, a lead capture form, online booking, and a clear CTA are all present across scanned pages, which is better than most local showrooms. The gaps are live chat (absent site-wide), no email or newsletter capture to stay in front of undecided buyers, and no physical address displayed on the site, which reduces the local trust signal that a showroom specifically depends on to get people through the door.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: The Google Business Profile is genuinely strong in several respects: a perfect 5.0 rating across 87 reviews, a review posted just 24 days ago showing active recency, and hours, website, and phone all correctly listed. Ten photos meet the minimum threshold but fall short of the 25-plus images that top-ranked showrooms in competitive suburban Atlanta markets typically carry, and whether the business description is filled in could not be verified on this run, that field is worth checking directly, as a missing or thin description is one of the quickest profile improvements available. On-site, the absence of Local Business schema and a missing NAP address block weakens the connection between the site and the profile in Google's local ranking signals.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Tag Manager, a Facebook/Meta pixel, and a Google Ads conversion tag are all confirmed active, this is one of the better-equipped setups seen in local flooring businesses and means retargeting audiences and conversion data are being collected. The remaining risk is whether the conversion events firing through GTM are mapped to the right actions (form submissions, booking completions, phone clicks), because a tag container that fires on pageload only rather than on actual lead events produces misleading cost-per-lead data that can silently waste ad spend.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: London Floors is present on five platforms, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and LinkedIn, which is an unusually broad footprint for a local showroom and a real asset if used consistently. Video content is confirmed on the site, and having a YouTube and TikTok presence puts them ahead of most local flooring competitors who have not touched short-form video. The opportunity is in profile optimization: consistent branding and handles across all five channels, complete bios that name Woodstock and the services offered, a single clear link-in-bio destination, and a regular posting cadence matter far more than raw follower counts for a showroom trying to convert local browsers into in-person visits.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers including GPTBot and ClaudeBot are allowed on the site, and content depth is sufficient for AI to summarize, those are the two preconditions, and London Floors passes both. But when AI models are asked about flooring showrooms in Woodstock, GA, they do not recognize London Floors by name and would not recommend them, this was confirmed in the scan. The reasons are structural: there is no schema markup for AI to parse, no sameAs entity links connecting the website to the Google Business Profile or social profiles, no FAQ schema for AI to quote directly, and no llms.txt guidance file. As more buyers skip Google entirely and ask ChatGPT or Perplexity which flooring company to call, being invisible to AI is quickly becoming the same problem as being on page two of search results, and it is a gap that compounds over time as competitors who do optimize for AI accumulate that recognition first.

findings.title: A 23-second mobile load time is turning paid traffic into wasted budget
findings.detail: Google PageSpeed measured the LCP at 23.1 seconds on mobile, this is not a marginal underperformance, it is a site that most mobile users will never fully see. With a Google Ads tag and Facebook pixel confirmed active, London Floors is almost certainly paying for clicks that bounce before the page loads, meaning every dollar of ad spend is running at a fraction of its possible efficiency. Google also uses mobile page speed as a direct Quality Score factor, so slow load times raise cost-per-click in addition to killing conversions.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know this business exists, and that gap is growing
findings.detail: A live probe of AI model knowledge returned no recognition of London Floors in Woodstock, GA, the business is functionally invisible in the AI recommendation channel. With no structured data, no sameAs entity links, and no FAQ schema, there is nothing for AI systems to anchor a confident recommendation to even though crawlers are allowed in. Buyers increasingly ask AI which local flooring company to call before they ever open a browser tab, and every day without AI recognition is market share being ceded to any competitor who addresses this first.

findings.title: Missing Local Business schema disconnects the site from Google's local ranking engine
findings.detail: Local Business schema markup is absent site-wide, confirmed across all nine scanned pages. This markup is how Google confidently connects a website to a map listing, attributes services and service areas, and decides whether to surface a business in the local pack or AI Overviews for queries like 'hardwood floor installation near Woodstock GA.' Without it, even a strong Google Business Profile is working harder than it needs to, and the site's 4,800 words of content are less useful to local ranking algorithms than they could be.

findings.title: No physical address on the site weakens the local trust signal a showroom depends on
findings.detail: The site-wide scan confirmed no NAP (name, address, phone) address block anywhere across the homepage, services pages, or contact areas, just a phone number. For a flooring showroom where the goal is to get qualified buyers to walk through the door in Woodstock, the absence of a visible address removes a fundamental trust signal and breaks NAP consistency between the site and the Google Business Profile, which is a local SEO ranking factor. Buyers researching where to go will often abandon a site that does not tell them where the business physically is.

findings.title: Two H1 tags split the page's topical authority and confuse crawlers
findings.detail: Every scanned page was checked and two H1 elements were found where SEO best practice requires exactly one, a clear, keyword-bearing headline that tells search engines what the page is about. Duplicate H1s dilute the relevance signal for the primary keyword target and can cause Google to misread the page's topic, which matters most on high-intent service pages like hardwood floor installation where ranking in the top three results directly correlates with phone call volume.

findings.title: Four images missing alt text hurt both SEO and accessibility scoring
findings.detail: Of the ten images detected on the site, four are missing alt text, a gap confirmed across the full page scan, not just the homepage. For a flooring showroom, product and installation images are high-value SEO assets when tagged correctly because they can rank in Google Image Search and add keyword relevance to service pages. Untagged images are also an accessibility failure (the accessibility score is 89, not 100), which matters for ADA compliance exposure as well as ranking.

findings.title: No email capture means the marketing funnel has no middle layer
findings.detail: The site has a form and booking tool for buyers who are ready to act, but no newsletter or email capture for the larger group of visitors who are still comparing options. Flooring is a considered purchase, most buyers research for weeks before committing, and without a way to stay in contact with that audience, London Floors has no mechanism to influence them during that window. Every visitor who leaves undecided is gone for good, with no retargeting possible through email even though the Meta pixel is active for paid retargeting.

quickWins: Add the showroom street address in text to the site footer and contact page to restore NAP consistency and local trust signals immediately.
Consolidate to a single H1 tag on each service page, leading with the primary keyword (e.g., 'Hardwood Floor Installation in Woodstock, GA') to sharpen search relevance without any content rewrite.
Write alt text for the four images currently missing it, this takes under an hour and improves both image search visibility and the accessibility score in one pass.

Verify and complete the Google Business Profile description directly in the dashboard, making sure it names Woodstock, lists core services, and includes a call to action, this field costs nothing and influences local pack placement.
audit_report.summary: London Floors is a 5-star business with a strong local reputation, active ad infrastructure, and more content than most competitors, but a catastrophically slow mobile site, zero AI recognition, and missing structural signals are creating a ceiling on how many of the right people actually find them, stay long enough to see that reputation, and decide to call. Open Heart Media has already identified the specific gaps costing leads and the order in which closing them produces the fastest revenue impact. A discovery call is the step where we show exactly how to prioritize the fix sequence for London Floors specifically, not a generic flooring client.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the mobile speed, schema, and AI visibility gaps alone could realistically recover 20 to 40 percent of current bounce-driven lead loss and meaningfully lower cost-per-lead on active ad campaigns, for a flooring showroom averaging even 8 to 12 jobs per month, that represents material top-line growth without increasing ad spend.

audit_report.headline: Where FFC Fast Flooring is quietly losing customers it already earned the right to win

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site earns real credit: HTTPS is active, the mobile viewport is configured correctly, layout shift is negligible at 0.004 CLS, and the overall mobile performance score of 81/100 is above average for local contractors. The drag is the Largest Contentful Paint of 3.3 seconds, which clears Google's 2.5-second threshold for a 'good' rating and is the single biggest speed penalty sitting between FFC and a faster, higher-converting page experience.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The page title and meta description are present and properly sized, canonical tags are set, and with 3,081 words the site gives search engines real content to index. Two structural problems undercut that foundation: the page carries two H1 tags instead of one, which splits the topical signal Google uses to rank the page, and local business schema markup is entirely absent, meaning Google cannot confirm business type, service area, or hours from structured data alone.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: The essentials are covered: a click-to-call phone number, a lead capture form, a clear call to action, and live chat are all present site-wide. What is missing is an online scheduling option, which for a flooring contractor is the difference between a visitor who books now and one who means to call back later and never does; there is also no email or newsletter capture, so every visitor who does not convert immediately is lost with no way to follow up.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: A 5.0 rating across 102 reviews is a genuine competitive asset and well above what most flooring contractors in the Acworth area carry. The Google Business Profile has hours, a website link, a phone number, and at least 10 photos, which clears the basic completeness bar. The profile is categorized as 'general contractor' rather than a flooring-specific category, which directly limits how often it surfaces in flooring-intent searches, and on-site local business schema is missing, which weakens the reinforcement loop between the site and the profile.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Tag Manager is installed, which shows intent to track, but neither a Facebook/Meta pixel nor a Google Ads conversion tag is firing. That means every visitor who does not convert on the first visit disappears permanently: FFC cannot run retargeting ads to bring them back, cannot build lookalike audiences from past visitors, and cannot measure which ad spend actually produces booked jobs versus which produces wasted clicks.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: Facebook and Instagram are linked from the site and the site does include video, which is a real head start for a flooring contractor where before-and-after visual content performs strongly. YouTube and TikTok are not connected, and short-form video on those platforms is where flooring transformation content consistently earns organic reach and inbound inquiries right now. Beyond platform gaps, the Open Graph tags that control how the site previews when shared on social are missing entirely, meaning any link shared to Facebook or Instagram shows up as a blank or broken card rather than a polished, click-worthy preview.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers are open, FAQ schema is present, entity links connecting FFC's profiles exist, and the site has enough content depth for an AI to summarize the business: those are real positives. The critical problem is that when AI models are asked about flooring contractors in Acworth, GA, they do not recognize FFC Fast Flooring at all, structured data is absent so AI systems cannot confidently extract and cite business details, and there is no llms.txt guidance file to help AI models understand what the business does and who it serves. Buyers are already using AI assistants to ask 'who should I hire for flooring in Acworth' and right now FFC is completely invisible in that answer, while the window to establish that presence before competitors do is still open.

findings.title: Wrong Google Business Profile category is filtering out flooring-intent searches
findings.detail: The live profile is categorized as 'general contractor', not as a flooring contractor or floor refinishing service. Google uses the primary category as one of its strongest local ranking signals, so when someone in Acworth types 'flooring contractor near me' or 'hardwood floor installation Acworth', FFC is competing in the wrong pool and is likely ranked below specialists who have the correct category set. For a business where a single booked job can be worth thousands of dollars, ranking two or three positions lower in the local pack on category-specific searches is a direct and recurring revenue cost.

findings.title: No online booking means warm leads go cold before they convert
findings.detail: The site has a form and live chat but no scheduling tool, so a visitor who is ready to commit must either call during business hours or wait for a callback after submitting the form. Flooring is a considered purchase, and research shows that home services leads who cannot self-schedule drop off at a significantly higher rate than those who can pick a time instantly. Every evening or weekend visitor, which is when homeowners typically browse, is a lead that FFC is asking to defer the decision until business hours when they may have forgotten or called a competitor.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know FFC Fast Flooring exists
findings.detail: A direct probe of AI model knowledge returned an explicit result: the model has no training data confirming FFC Fast Flooring exists in Acworth, GA, and would not recommend it to someone asking for a flooring contractor in the area. This is not a future concern: consumers are actively using ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews to get contractor recommendations today, and a business that AI cannot find or verify is simply not in the conversation. The fixes that close this gap, primarily structured data and entity strengthening, are within reach, and acting now is easier than catching up after competitors have established that presence.

findings.title: No retargeting capability means FFC pays for visitors it cannot follow up with
findings.detail: With no Meta pixel and no Google Ads conversion tag in place, FFC has no way to re-engage the visitors who browse the gallery or services page and leave without contacting them. In flooring, where a homeowner may visit three to five contractor sites before deciding, retargeting ads that bring FFC back in front of a recent visitor at the moment they are comparing options can be the deciding factor. Without the pixel installed, that audience is invisible and un-addressable, and any future ad spend starts from zero rather than from a warm pool of people who already showed interest.

findings.title: Duplicate H1 and missing local schema dilute Google's confidence in the page
findings.detail: Two H1 tags on the same page split the topical authority signal that Google uses to determine what a page is primarily about, which can suppress rankings for the core service keywords FFC needs most. Layered on top of that, the complete absence of local business schema means Google is inferring business type, location, and services from unstructured text rather than reading clean, machine-readable data: that is a meaningful confidence gap when Google is deciding which contractors to show in local results for Acworth flooring searches.

findings.title: LCP of 3.3 seconds is above Google's 'good' threshold and costs rankings
findings.detail: Google's Core Web Vitals use 2.5 seconds as the ceiling for a 'good' Largest Contentful Paint score; FFC's 3.3-second mobile LCP falls into the 'needs improvement' band. Page experience is a confirmed ranking factor, and on mobile, where the majority of local service searches happen, a slower load time also directly increases bounce rate before the visitor has even seen the content or the phone number.

findings.title: Eight images missing alt text create both an SEO and an accessibility gap
findings.detail: Of the 27 images on the site, 8 have no alt text at all. For a flooring contractor, gallery images of completed installs are among the highest-value SEO assets on the site because they can rank in Google Image Search for terms like 'hardwood floor installation Acworth' and drive direct clicks from buyers in the research phase. Every untagged image is an indexing opportunity forfeited, and the accessibility score of 85 confirms this is already measurably affecting usability for visitors using assistive technology.

quickWins: Update the Google Business Profile primary category from 'general contractor' to 'flooring contractor' or the most specific flooring-related category available in Google's taxonomy
Remove the duplicate H1 tag so each page carries exactly one clear, keyword-relevant headline
Install the Meta pixel and Google Ads conversion tag so visitor data begins accumulating immediately for future retargeting campaigns
Add descriptive alt text to the 8 images currently missing it, prioritizing gallery photos of completed flooring projects
audit_report.summary: FFC Fast Flooring has the reputation, the review count, and the site infrastructure that most local competitors would envy, but a set of specific, compounding gaps in schema, tracking, AI visibility, and conversion flow is quietly redirecting customers to whoever shows up more completely. The path to more booked jobs runs directly through these gaps, and OHM has mapped exactly where the work needs to happen. A 30-minute discovery call is the right next step to translate this audit into a prioritized plan.

categories.name: Website & Speed

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: Across all four pages scanned, there is no click-to-call phone number, no contact form, no booking option, no call to action, no live chat, and no email capture, meaning a visitor who wants to start a project has no direct path to do so from the site. The only trust signal present is a listed address, which makes this less a business website and more a digital placeholder that actively sends warm prospects elsewhere.

The most recent review was left 492 days ago, over 16 months, which signals to both Google's algorithm and to prospective clients that the business is either inactive or unresponsive. There are zero photos on the profile, which is one of the highest-impact free tools Google offers for flooring businesses where visual proof of work directly drives inquiries.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: There is no analytics platform, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads conversion tag installed anywhere on the site, meaning there is currently no data on how many people visit, where they come from, which pages they leave from, or whether any traffic source is producing leads. categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: No social profiles of any kind are linked from the site, and the scan detected no presence on Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, or TikTok, which is a significant missed opportunity for a flooring business where before-and-after project photos and short walkthrough videos consistently drive both referral traffic and direct inquiries. The site also has no video content whatsoever, despite video being one of the highest-performing formats for building trust in the commercial flooring category. Profile optimization, a consistent handle across platforms, a clear link in bio, and even a modest cadence of project posts would all be starting from zero.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers are allowed access to the site, which is the one positive signal here, but there is no structured data, no entity links connecting the business across the web, no FAQ content for AI to quote, and the site's 388 words of content are not sufficient depth for an AI model to build a meaningful understanding of what the business does or who it serves. When AI models are asked about commercial flooring options in the Atlanta or Acworth area, they have no basis to surface or recommend Atlanta Commercial Flooring, a gap that will compound as more buyers start their vendor search by asking an AI assistant rather than typing a query into Google. findings.title: Zero conversion paths mean paying traffic produces zero leads

Every visitor the site receives today is effectively wasted.

findings.title: 3 reviews at 3.7 stars is disqualifying for commercial contracts
findings.detail: Commercial clients, property managers, and general contractors routinely check Google reviews before shortlisting flooring vendors, and a profile with 3 reviews and a sub-4.0 rating is frequently filtered out before a first conversation happens. Competitors in the Acworth and broader Atlanta metro area with 40 to 100-plus reviews at 4.5 stars are capturing those inbound requests by default. The last review being 492 days old compounds this by suggesting to prospective clients that the business is dormant.

findings.title: No HTTPS means browsers warn visitors the site is not secure
findings.detail: Chrome, Safari, and Firefox all display a 'Not Secure' warning on sites without HTTPS, and for a business selling commercial flooring services where clients are evaluating professionalism and trust, that warning functions as a credibility killer before a visitor reads a line of copy. Google also uses HTTPS as a direct ranking factor, so the missing certificate is simultaneously hurting trust and search position.

findings.title: AI assistants do not recognize the business, making it invisible in the fastest-growing search channel
findings.detail: A live probe of what AI models know returned no training data or recognition of Atlanta Commercial Flooring in Acworth, and the absence of structured data, entity links, and sufficient content depth means there is no mechanism for that to change without deliberate action. As more procurement contacts and property managers begin sourcing vendors through AI-assisted searches, the businesses that AI can confidently describe and recommend will capture that traffic while unrecognized businesses are omitted entirely.

findings.title: No photos on the Google Business Profile removes the primary visual trust signal buyers use
findings.detail: Google Business Profile data consistently shows that profiles with photos receive significantly more direction requests and website clicks than those without, and for a flooring company, project photography is the single most persuasive element a prospective client evaluates. The current profile has zero photos, meaning the business looks either brand-new or abandoned next to any competitor who has uploaded even a modest portfolio.

findings.title: No tracking means there is no way to know what is working or where leads are being lost

findings.title: Mobile viewport misconfiguration undermines both user experience and Google ranking
findings.detail: The mobile viewport meta tag is absent, which means smartphones likely render the site as a scaled-down desktop version with tiny text and unresponsive elements, this directly increases bounce rates among the majority of local searchers who are on mobile. Google's mobile-first indexing means the mobile experience is the version Google primarily uses to determine rankings, so this single missing tag is actively suppressing the site's position in local search results.

Add the mobile viewport meta tag to the site's HTML head so the site renders correctly on smartphones and stops being penalized under Google's mobile-first index.
audit_report.summary: Atlanta Commercial Flooring has real assets, a functioning business, an active Google profile, and a site that loads reasonably fast, but the conversion infrastructure, local trust signals, and discoverability layer are not built out, which means the business is almost certainly generating far fewer inbound leads than the market would support. categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: The site is secure (HTTPS), mobile-responsive, and layout-stable (CLS of 0), which are genuine positives, but the mobile PageSpeed score of 68/100 and a Largest Contentful Paint of 7.7 seconds are well outside Google's 2.5-second threshold for a good user experience. On mobile, where the majority of local flooring searches happen, a 7.7-second load before the main content appears means a meaningful share of visitors leave before they ever see a product or a phone number, and a mixed-content flag adds a security warning risk that further erodes trust.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The site has local business schema, a canonical tag, and a page title, but it is missing a meta description entirely and has zero H1 headings anywhere across the scanned pages, which are two of the most basic on-page signals Google uses to understand and rank a page. With only 477 words of content across the site, there is virtually no topical depth for Google to surface ARZ Floors for the category and service queries that drive floor-shopping decisions, such as hardwood installation in Woodstock or LVP flooring near me.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: The site earns credit for having a click-to-call phone number, a lead form, an online booking option, and a clear CTA, which is a stronger conversion setup than most local flooring competitors. The gaps are the absence of live chat, which studies consistently show captures buyers who will not fill out a form or call during business hours, and no email or newsletter capture, meaning there is no way to stay in front of visitors who are still in the research phase of a flooring project.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: The Google Business Profile is a genuine asset: a 5.0 rating across 86 reviews is exceptional for a flooring store in a competitive suburban market like Woodstock, the most recent review is only 25 days old showing active reputation momentum, and hours, website, and phone are all properly listed. The photo count of 10 is functional but on the low end for a visual category where buyers rely heavily on seeing finished work before making contact, and whether the business description is filled in could not be confirmed in this scan and should be verified directly in the profile dashboard, as a missing description is a common and easily fixed gap.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: Google Analytics 4 is installed, which means there is baseline traffic visibility, but both the Facebook/Meta Pixel and the Google Ads conversion tag are absent, making it impossible to run retargeting campaigns or measure which ad spend is actually producing quote requests or bookings. Without conversion tracking, any future paid campaign is flying blind: money spent on Google or Meta ads cannot be optimized against the actions that matter, and buyers who visited the site but did not convert cannot be brought back with targeted ads.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: ARZ Floors maintains Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn profiles, and the site includes video, which is the right instinct for a visually driven category like flooring. However, there is no YouTube channel and no TikTok presence, and for a business where before-and-after transformations are the primary purchase trigger, those are the two platforms where flooring content consistently drives the highest organic reach and purchase intent right now. The opportunity is specific: consistent short-form video of installs, material comparisons, and project reveals, paired with complete and consistent profile bios and a single clear link destination, could generate a meaningful and free lead stream that does not currently exist.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers are allowed and structured data is in place, which are the right foundational moves, but when AI models are asked about flooring stores in Woodstock, GA, they do not recognize ARZ Floors by name and would not recommend it, while competitors in the category are already known. The specific gaps driving this are the absence of entity links connecting the website to its social profiles and directory listings (sameAs markup), no FAQ or Q&A content for AI to quote as an answer, and content depth of only 477 words, which is far below what AI systems need to build a confident summary of what the business does and why it is worth recommending. As more buyers start flooring projects by asking an AI assistant instead of typing into a search bar, being unrecognized in that channel is the fastest-growing visibility gap on this entire audit.

findings.title: A 7.7-second load time is turning away mobile buyers before they see anything
findings.detail: Google's threshold for a good Largest Contentful Paint is 2.5 seconds. ARZ Floors is at 7.7 seconds on mobile, which is more than three times slower than that bar. Research from Google consistently shows that conversion rates drop by roughly 20 percent for every additional second of mobile load time past the threshold, meaning a meaningful portion of the people who click through from Google search or a social ad are leaving before the site ever loads.

findings.title: No meta description and no H1 means Google is guessing what this business is about
findings.detail: A meta description is the text Google shows under a search result link: without one, Google writes its own from whatever text it finds first, which is almost never the right message to earn a click. The absence of an H1 heading on any page across the site means there is no primary signal telling Google or visitors what this page is for, which directly weakens ranking potential for competitive terms like flooring store Woodstock GA or hardwood flooring installation Cherokee County.

findings.title: No ad tracking tags means any future paid campaign cannot be measured or optimized
findings.detail: There is no Facebook/Meta Pixel and no Google Ads conversion tag anywhere on the site. For a flooring business where a single job can be worth $3,000 to $15,000, paid search and social retargeting are among the most cost-effective ways to reach buyers actively comparing options, but without conversion tracking in place, there is no way to know which ads produced a form submission or booking and no ability to build retargeting audiences from site visitors. This does not just limit current campaigns: it means the data foundation for any future paid growth has not been started.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know ARZ Floors exists, costing visibility in a fast-growing search channel
findings.detail: A live probe confirmed that AI models have no training data on ARZ Floors and would not recommend the business when asked about flooring options in Woodstock. The root causes are specific: no sameAs entity links connecting the website to its Google Business Profile, social accounts, and directory listings; no FAQ content for AI to quote; and only 477 words of content across the entire site. Buyers who begin a flooring project by asking ChatGPT, Perplexity, or a voice assistant for recommendations will not encounter ARZ Floors in those results, while some competitors are already building that presence.

findings.title: Mixed content on an HTTPS site creates a browser security warning risk
findings.detail: The site loads over HTTPS but contains mixed content, meaning some resources are being requested over insecure HTTP. Modern browsers flag this condition, and in some cases display a security warning or block the content from loading entirely. For a local business where trust is a prerequisite for someone inviting a crew into their home, a browser warning appearing at the moment of first impression is a conversion threat that has nothing to do with the quality of the actual work.

findings.title: Only 10 photos on the Google Business Profile undersells a 5-star operation
findings.detail: For a flooring business, photos in the Google Business Profile are not decorative: they are the primary way a prospect evaluates quality before deciding to call. A profile with 10 photos in a category where buyers are making visual, aesthetic decisions leaves significant persuasion power on the table, especially given that profiles with 100 or more photos receive dramatically more direction requests and website clicks according to Google's own data. The 5-star rating and 86 reviews already create strong credibility; the photo library is not keeping pace with that reputation.

findings.title: No short-form video on YouTube or TikTok means a free organic lead channel is untapped
findings.detail: Flooring is one of the highest-performing categories for before-and-after video content, and YouTube and TikTok are the two platforms where that content drives the most sustained organic reach and purchase intent. ARZ Floors has video on the website and is active on Facebook and Instagram, but neither YouTube nor TikTok is linked or present, meaning the business is not building a searchable video library or reaching the growing segment of buyers who discover contractors and specialty retailers through short-form video before they ever search on Google.

quickWins: Write and add a meta description of 140 to 160 characters to every page, leading with the primary service and Woodstock, GA location.
Add a single clear H1 tag to each page that names what the page is about, such as 'Hardwood and LVP Flooring Installation in Woodstock, GA' on the homepage.
Install the Facebook/Meta Pixel and Google Ads conversion tag now, before any paid campaigns run, so the retargeting audience starts building immediately.
Add sameAs markup to the homepage schema linking to the Google Business Profile, Facebook, Instagram, and any directory listings so AI models and search engines can connect the entity across the web.
audit_report.summary: ARZ Floors is genuinely strong where it is hardest to build: a 5-star reputation, active reviews, and real conversion infrastructure on the site. What is quietly costing this business new customers is a set of technical and visibility gaps, a slow mobile load, missing SEO basics, no ad tracking, and complete absence from AI search, that are fixable with the right prioritized plan. Open Heart Media built this audit before any conversation because the gaps were clear enough to be worth showing, and the revenue upside of closing them is significant enough that the specifics of how are worth a direct conversation.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the speed, SEO, tracking, and AI visibility gaps identified here could realistically recover 20 to 35 additional qualified leads per month based on current traffic patterns, translating to $60,000 to $150,000 or more in annual revenue depending on average job value and close rate.

audit_report.headline: Where Advanced Flooring Solutions is quietly losing customers before they ever make contact
audit_report.overallVerdict: Advanced Flooring Solutions has a functional website and a perfect star rating, but a 13.4-second mobile load time, only 5 Google reviews with the last one almost two years ago, zero tracking infrastructure, and no recognition from AI assistants combine to create a presence that is losing warm, local buyers to competitors every week.

categories.name: Website & Speed
categories.why: Google PageSpeed scores the mobile site at 47/100, with a Largest Contentful Paint of 13.4 seconds and a Cumulative Layout Shift of 0.305, both of which fail Google's Core Web Vitals thresholds by a wide margin. The site does pass on HTTPS, mobile viewport, and mixed-content checks, but those baseline passes cannot compensate for a load experience that causes the majority of mobile visitors to abandon the page before it finishes rendering.

categories.name: Getting Found (SEO)
categories.why: The page title, meta description, single H1, canonical tag, and a solid 2,633-word content count all pass, giving the site a competent on-page foundation. The critical missing piece is local business schema markup, which means Google and other search engines cannot machine-read the business name, address, service area, or category with confidence, reducing eligibility for rich results and the local pack.

categories.name: Converting Visitors
categories.why: A lead capture form, an online booking option, and a clear call to action are present across the site, which is a real asset. However, there is no click-to-call phone number anywhere on the site, no live chat, and no email or newsletter capture, meaning mobile visitors who want to call instantly hit a dead end, and the business collects no ongoing contact list from the traffic it does receive.

categories.name: Local Visibility
categories.why: The Google Business Profile exists, is linked to the website, and carries a perfect 5-star rating, but it has only 5 reviews total and the most recent one was posted 715 days ago, nearly two years back, which is a serious trust signal problem for any buyer comparing local flooring contractors. Business hours are not listed on the profile at all, which Google treats as incomplete and which pushes the listing down in local pack rankings. The profile has only 8 photos and whether the description field is filled in could not be verified on this run, but the combination of a stale, thin profile in a competitive home-improvement category means the business is almost certainly being ranked below local competitors who maintain their profiles actively.

categories.name: Tracking & Data
categories.why: No website analytics platform, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads conversion tag are installed anywhere on the site, meaning the business has no data on how many people visit, where they come from, which pages they leave from, or whether any form submission leads to a real job. Without this infrastructure, any future ad spend would be blind money, and there is currently no way to know how many warm leads the site is already losing.

categories.name: Social & Content
categories.why: Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube are all linked from the site, which shows awareness of the right platforms for a visual, project-based business like flooring. There is no video anywhere on the website itself, and TikTok, now a primary discovery channel for home improvement content, is absent entirely. The opportunity here is significant: a flooring business with real project photography has natural material for before-and-after content, and without optimized profile bios, consistent branding, active posting, and short-form video, those three linked profiles are likely underperforming and driving little referral traffic back to the site.

categories.name: AI Search Presence (AIO)
categories.why: AI crawlers including GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot are allowed to access the site, which is the right starting position, but there is no structured data, no FAQ schema, no entity links connecting the website to the business's social profiles or Google listing, and no llms.txt guidance file to help AI models understand what the business does and where it operates. When AI models were tested for knowledge of Advanced Flooring Solutions in Woodstock, GA, the result was no recognition whatsoever, meaning if a homeowner asks an AI assistant to recommend a flooring company in Woodstock, this business does not exist in that answer. As AI-assisted search becomes a primary discovery method for home services, being invisible to AI models is the single fastest-growing source of lost referrals, and closing this gap now is far easier than catching up once competitors have claimed the position.

findings.title: A 13.4-second mobile load time is turning away the majority of site visitors
findings.detail: Google's own research shows 53% of mobile users abandon a page that takes longer than 3 seconds to load. At 13.4 seconds for Largest Contentful Paint, Advanced Flooring Solutions is losing more than half of every mobile visitor before they ever see a service or a photo. In a category where customers are actively comparing 3 to 5 local businesses, a slow site is not an inconvenience, it is a direct transfer of customers to faster competitors.

findings.title: 5 reviews and a 715-day gap is costing the business Google ranking and buyer trust
findings.detail: A typical well-maintained flooring business in a suburban Atlanta market like Woodstock will have 40 to 100-plus Google reviews with activity in the last 30 to 60 days. Advanced Flooring Solutions has 5 reviews, the most recent of which is almost two years old, a signal Google's local algorithm reads as a dormant or low-volume business. Buyers reading the profile see the same thing, and in a high-consideration purchase like flooring where trust is everything, a nearly empty, stale review profile will consistently lose the comparison to competitors who show recent social proof.

findings.title: No analytics means the business is flying blind on traffic and leads
findings.detail: With no Google Analytics, no Meta pixel, and no Google Ads tag installed, there is no record of how many people visit the site each month, what they search for before arriving, which pages cause them to leave, or whether form submissions are converting into booked jobs. This makes it impossible to measure what is working, impossible to run effective paid ads, and impossible to build retargeting audiences from site visitors who did not convert. Every dollar spent on any future marketing is untracked until this is resolved.

findings.title: AI assistants do not know this business exists, and that gap is growing
findings.detail: A live test of AI model knowledge returned zero recognition of Advanced Flooring Solutions in Woodstock, GA. With no structured data, no FAQ content for AI to quote, and no entity links connecting the website to its social and Google profiles, the business has no footprint in the data layer that AI assistants draw from when answering buyer questions. As ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews handle more home-services queries, being absent from those answers means a growing portion of the market never sees this business at all.

findings.title: Business hours missing from Google Business Profile reduces ranking and drives away ready buyers
findings.detail: Google explicitly marks profiles without hours as incomplete, and incomplete profiles rank lower in the local pack. Beyond ranking, a buyer who is ready to call or visit and cannot confirm the business is open will often move to the next result rather than guess. In a category driven by in-store consultations and showroom visits, missing hours is a direct friction point between a motivated buyer and a first appointment.

findings.title: No click-to-call phone number on the website breaks the most common mobile conversion path
findings.detail: Mobile users searching for flooring services frequently want to call directly from the search result or the website, especially when they are in a comparison or decision moment. The scan confirmed no click-to-call number is present anywhere on the site across all pages reviewed. A customer who cannot tap to call in one touch will often abandon to a competitor who makes that action immediate.

findings.title: 22 of 30 images have no alt text, compounding both SEO and accessibility problems
findings.detail: For a flooring business, project photography is one of the primary trust and decision drivers, yet 73% of the site's images are invisible to search engine crawlers because they carry no descriptive alt text. This means Google Image Search, which drives meaningful referral traffic for visual home-improvement categories, is not indexing the portfolio content. It also creates accessibility failures that affect visitors using screen readers.

quickWins: Add business hours to the Google Business Profile today, this is a single field that affects local ranking immediately.
Add a click-to-call phone number to the site header and footer so mobile visitors can reach the business in one tap.
Install Google Analytics 4 on the site so that traffic, behavior, and form submissions begin generating real data from this point forward.
Request reviews from the last 12 to 24 months of satisfied customers using a direct Google review link, even 10 fresh reviews would move the profile out of dormant status.
audit_report.summary: Advanced Flooring Solutions has a real business with a perfect rating and genuine project work to show, but the combination of a slow website, a dormant Google profile, no tracking, and zero AI visibility means a significant number of local buyers who are actively looking for flooring help are not finding or choosing this business. Open Heart Media has already identified the specific gaps and knows the sequence in which closing them produces the fastest increase in customer inquiries. A 30-minute conversation is enough to map out what a realistic first 90 days looks like.
audit_report.estimate: Closing the highest-impact gaps identified here, specifically mobile speed, Google review recency, business hours, click-to-call, and analytics, could realistically move this business from near-invisible in local search to a top-3 local pack position in Woodstock, which for a flooring business averaging several thousand dollars per job typically represents 10 to 20 additional qualified leads per month.
